title: ASCII terminal output on Windows
text:
# ASCII terminal output on Windows

Lifecycle status: accepted

On Windows PowerShell and cmd.exe, CodeGraph terminal output should default to plain ASCII glyphs to avoid garbled characters, with environment variables to opt into Unicode or force ASCII. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.10 says CodeGraph uses ASCII by default on Windows, `CODEGRAPH_UNICODE=1` opts into Unicode, and `CODEGRAPH_ASCII=1` forces ASCII anywhere.

title: ASP.NET feature-folder routes
text:
# ASP.NET feature-folder routes

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph detects ASP.NET Core feature-folder controllers and resolves bare `[HttpGet]` actions with class `[Route]` prefixes. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks C# ASP.NET Core done, with realworld route detection moving 0->19 and eShopOnWeb 9->33.

title: ASP.NET markup coverage ceiling
text:
# ASP.NET markup coverage ceiling

Lifecycle status: accepted

Razor/Blazor markup parsing raises the honest ASP.NET eShopOnWeb FAIR coverage target from about 77% to about 90%, while the final gap remains reflection/proxy registration and static value reads. Evidence: docs/design/template-markup-parser.md#0 Quantified target and Non-goals sections state ASP.NET ~77% -> ~90%, not 95%, with reflection/proxy and C# static-const reads still separate work.

title: Actual dependent test reporting
text:
# Actual dependent test reporting

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph affected` must report tests and files that actually depend on changed code, not only files with import statements. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 `codegraph affected` real cross-file usage graph bullet.

title: Adaptive explore escape hatch
text:
# Adaptive explore escape hatch

Lifecycle status: accepted

Adaptive explore must remain disableable with `CODEGRAPH_ADAPTIVE_EXPLORE=0`. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 Status lists the escape hatch and the refined gate applies only when `CODEGRAPH_ADAPTIVE_EXPLORE != 0`.

title: Adaptive sibling skeletonization
text:
# Adaptive sibling skeletonization

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_explore` ships default-on adaptive sizing that skeletonizes files only when they are off-spine polymorphic siblings, rendering signatures instead of full bodies. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 Status says implemented, validated, default-on; the gate requires a spine, off-spine file, ≥3-implementer sibling, and not-spared status.

title: Additive function-ref references
text:
# Additive function-ref references

Lifecycle status: accepted

The shipped function-ref capture adds registration-site `references` edges while leaving nodes and `calls` edges unchanged across the validation corpus. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Validation reports all 17 repos had identical nodes and 0/0 calls deltas, with strictly additive refs such as redis +1918, Pascal +577, Swift +116, and TS/React +121.

title: Additive synthesized edges
text:
# Additive synthesized edges

Lifecycle status: accepted

Synthesized callback edges must be additive and never replace static edges; downstream tooling can filter them by `provenance='heuristic'` and `metadata.synthesizedBy`. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Edge cases/model states synthesized edges are additive and filterable.

title: Additive value-ref emission
text:
# Additive value-ref emission

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-reference emission must add `references` edges only and never create graph nodes. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#0 Edge semantics says value-reference edges are deduped per reader-target pair and additive, adding edges and never nodes.

title: Adoption metrics over token cost
text:
# Adoption metrics over token cost

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph adoption work must optimize wall-clock time, tool-call count, and Read=0 rather than treating token cost as the primary target. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 states this doctrine constraint explicitly and notes token cost is lower as a side effect.

title: Affected path normalization
text:
# Affected path normalization

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph affected` normalizes `./`-prefixed and absolute file paths as valid project file inputs instead of requiring bare project-relative paths. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says paths from other tools no longer silently match nothing and report no affected tests.

title: Affected traces usage graph
text:
# Affected traces usage graph

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph affected` follows real cross-file usage edges such as calls, references, instantiations, and class inheritance instead of following import statements. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 affected command no-tests bug bullet.

title: Agent A/B needs repo fit
text:
# Agent A/B needs repo fit

Lifecycle status: accepted

Agent A/B results must be interpreted against repository size and architecture, because a deterministic graph win can be obscured when the repo is too small or the target architecture makes both arms thrash. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 says Express inline-handler edges were deterministic wins, but realworld was below the size where CodeGraph beats reading and Ghost's custom API layering muddied both arms.

title: Agent identity telemetry
text:
# Agent identity telemetry

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph telemetry now includes which agents connect, making MCP client identity part of the shipped anonymous usage rollup rather than proposed plumbing. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 telemetry bullet says usage statistics include which agents connect.

title: Agent process cleanup
text:
# Agent process cleanup

Lifecycle status: accepted

A CodeGraph MCP server should stop and release watches, file descriptors, and SQLite WAL resources when its parent agent process dies. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 says `codegraph serve --mcp` shuts down as soon as its parent process changes on Linux after OOM, `kill -9`, or container teardown.

title: Agent usage attribution
text:
# Agent usage attribution

Lifecycle status: proposed

Telemetry should attribute MCP usage to the driving agent by recording MCP `clientInfo` client name and version in rollups. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Goals and Events sections name Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, opencode, and `client_name`/`client_version` from the MCP initialize handshake, with plumbing still to add.

title: Agent-agnostic trust instructions
text:
# Agent-agnostic trust instructions

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph agent instructions are agent-agnostic and explicitly steer agents to trust CodeGraph results instead of re-verifying with native search. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.7 says the new instructions tell each agent to trust CodeGraph results instead of re-verifying with grep, fixing Cursor and Codex fallback.

title: Alamofire closure-flow coverage
text:
# Alamofire closure-flow coverage

Lifecycle status: accepted

Closure-collection synthesis made Alamofire's validate flow reachable and precise, yielding 9 edges on Alamofire and 0 on non-Swift controls, with forced CodeGraph-only runs answering correctly. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 3c reports `trace(didCompleteTask, validate)` connects through the closure-collection hop, 9 precise Alamofire edges, 0 non-Swift control edges, and 3/3 forced CodeGraph-only correct answers.

title: Alamofire trace flounder collapse
text:
# Alamofire trace flounder collapse

Lifecycle status: accepted

Adding node relevance to endpoint scoring reduced Alamofire WITH-arm tool-call median from 12 to 8 and collapsed read variance from 0-12 to 1-4 by eliminating trace-collision floundering. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 3d reports the n=8 validation result after penalizing empty stubs and test-file symbols.

title: All-language callback registrations
text:
# All-language callback registrations

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph now records reference edges when functions are registered as callbacks across all supported languages, including function arguments, function-pointer or field assignment, handler tables, selectors, method references, and event wiring; ambiguous names produce no edge. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 callback-registration bullet.

title: All-language cross-file impact
text:
# All-language cross-file impact

Lifecycle status: accepted

Cross-file impact and blast-radius coverage spans all 22 supported languages and 14 web frameworks, with real-world repo validation and documented residual static-analysis frontiers. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 cross-file impact coverage bullet.

title: All-language doc marker cleanup
text:
# All-language doc marker cleanup

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph normalizes stored documentation text by stripping doc/comment markers across every supported language, including Rust/Swift/Kotlin `///` and `//!`, Python/Ruby/shell `#`, Lua/Luau `--` and block comments, and Pascal brace/star comments. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 doc-comment cleanup bullet says this was validated across all 19 code languages plus Svelte/Vue `<script>` blocks.

title: All-tier test-file exclusion
text:
# All-tier test-file exclusion

Lifecycle status: accepted

Adaptive explore excludes test files from all sizing tiers because tests rarely answer architecture questions and can consume scarce explore budget. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 Further refinement item 3 says `custom_lookups/tests.py` was eating 2.3 KB of Django's 28 KB budget and test-file exclusion was extended to all tiers.

title: Ambiguous mapper collisions drop
text:
# Ambiguous mapper collisions drop

Lifecycle status: accepted

Java-to-XML mapper synthesis must drop ambiguous simple-name collisions rather than guess, preserving precision over recall. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 says `mybatisJavaXmlEdges` joins Java methods to XML qualified names by suffix-match and drops ambiguous simple-name collisions, explicitly labeled precision over recall.

title: Ambiguous node returns all definitions
text:
# Ambiguous node returns all definitions

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_node` returns every definition for ambiguous symbol names, including overloaded methods and same-name methods on different types, with exact `file` or `line` filters available for large overload sets. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.9 Fixes.

title: Anonymous PostHog event mode
text:
# Anonymous PostHog event mode

Lifecycle status: accepted

Telemetry batches are sent to PostHog as anonymous events with `$process_person_profile: false` and `distinct_id` equal to the random `machine_id`, avoiding person profiles while preserving unique-machine counts. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Events section.

title: Anonymous aggregate usage answers
text:
# Anonymous aggregate usage answers

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph telemetry exists to answer aggregate anonymous usage questions: active machines, agent clients, install targets, tool and CLI usage/errors, indexed languages, version adoption, platform mix, and SQLite backend share. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Goals section.

title: Anonymous arrows remain uncovered
text:
# Anonymous arrows remain uncovered

Lifecycle status: accepted

Anonymous-arrow EventEmitter handlers remain uncovered because Phase 3 intentionally does not extract them as nodes. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work says `on('e', () => foo())` still produces no edge and is the highest remaining recall win.

title: Anonymous class node indexing
text:
# Anonymous class node indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Java and C# anonymous classes and their overridden methods are indexed as real class nodes so hidden overrides appear in graph trails without requiring a file read. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.7 New Features.

title: Anonymous handler link-through-body
text:
# Anonymous handler link-through-body

Lifecycle status: deprecated

Anonymous inline handlers still need a synthesizer link-through-body mechanism because named inline handlers are already extracted generically but anonymous handler linking is not built yet. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 Step 3 says named inline handlers are handled by generic extraction, while anonymous handlers need synthesizer link-through-body and are not yet built.

title: Anonymous route handler backlog
text:
# Anonymous route handler backlog

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph should add body-level flow recovery for framework route handlers expressed as anonymous functions or lambdas instead of named functions. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 leaves Go inline `func(c){}` handlers, Rust anonymous `.to` closures, Vapor route closures, and Kotlin Ktor route lambdas as frontiers because the anonymous handler body is lost or unnamed.

title: Anonymous route handler bodies
text:
# Anonymous route handler bodies

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph should recover flow from anonymous route handlers or lambdas when a framework route declaration has no named handler target. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 lists anonymous or closure route handlers as frontiers for Go inline `func(c){}` handlers, Rust anonymous `.to` closure handlers, Vapor closure handlers `app.get("x"){ }`, and Kotlin Ktor `routing { get("/x"){...} }` lambda handlers.

title: Anonymous usage telemetry
text:
# Anonymous usage telemetry

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph now ships anonymous usage telemetry for commands, MCP tools, indexed languages, and connected agents, with field-by-field documentation, local daily aggregation, public auditable ingest code, and multiple hard opt-outs. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 bullet 'Anonymous usage telemetry, documented field-by-field and easy to turn off.'

title: Anonymous wrapper traversal
text:
# Anonymous wrapper traversal

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph descends into anonymous function wrappers in JavaScript modules so wrapped inner functions and calls are indexed. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 cites AMD/RequireJS, NetSuite SuiteScript, and IIFE bundles that previously came up nearly empty.

title: Answer-sized explore output
text:
# Answer-sized explore output

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_explore` should size its output to the answer instead of always filling the budget cap. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 Motivation says the goal is to stop sibling-heavy flows from costing more than plain grep/read while still fitting the answer.

title: Apply MCP runtime memory flag
text:
# Apply MCP runtime memory flag

Lifecycle status: accepted

The MCP serve path needs to apply a Node/V8 runtime memory flag before serving. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says `serve --mcp` does a `--liftoff-only` re-exec for a Node memory flag and points to `src/extraction/wasm-runtime-flags.ts`.

title: Arrow body link-through synthesis
text:
# Arrow body link-through synthesis

Lifecycle status: proposed

Callback synthesis should add a link-through-body strategy for anonymous arrow handlers, linking dispatchers to calls inside the arrow body instead of requiring the arrow to be a node. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work item 1 names this fix explicitly.

title: Arrow callback link-through
text:
# Arrow callback link-through

Lifecycle status: proposed

Callback synthesis should handle anonymous-arrow handlers by parsing the arrow body and linking the dispatcher to calls inside the arrow. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work item 1 marks this as the highest remaining recall win for `on('e', () => foo())`.

title: Astro extractor
text:
# Astro extractor

Lifecycle status: accepted

The Astro extractor is the CodeGraph indexing surface for `.astro` frontmatter, client scripts, component usages, and file-based routes. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 Astro bullet.

title: Astro indexing
text:
# Astro indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph indexes `.astro` projects by extracting TypeScript frontmatter, client script blocks, component usages, Astro framework globals/imports, and `src/pages` routes including dynamic segments. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 Astro bullet.

title: Auto-sync trust failure mode
text:
# Auto-sync trust failure mode

Lifecycle status: accepted

The file watcher disables auto-sync once and reports that state when live watching can no longer be trusted. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says resource exhaustion or long-held write locks now produce one clear message, `codegraph status` and tool responses expose disabled auto-sync, and agents know to read files directly.

title: Auto-sync trust signaling
text:
# Auto-sync trust signaling

Lifecycle status: accepted

Agents and users must be told plainly when live auto-sync can no longer be trusted. CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says CodeGraph disables auto-sync with one clear message and tool/status responses say so, so agents read files directly instead of trusting a frozen index.

title: Avoid avoidable tool round-trips
text:
# Avoid avoidable tool round-trips

Lifecycle status: accepted

Tool guidance should steer agents to the intended first call so they do not spend an extra round trip on a prerequisite that is not actually required. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 says `codegraph_explore` guidance no longer suggests running `codegraph_search` first because that contradicted explore's call-it-first design and cost agents an extra round-trip.

title: Avoid explore read-backs
text:
# Avoid explore read-backs

Lifecycle status: accepted

Adaptive explore should avoid making agents Read back files that were collapsed by the explore output. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 Refinement says the first cut skeletonized files the agent then Read back, defeating the point, and later refinements target median 0 reads.

title: Background file watcher
text:
# Background file watcher

Lifecycle status: accepted

The background file watcher is the CodeGraph server component that observes project files and triggers index updates while the MCP server runs. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 describes the watcher exhausting file descriptors on macOS and its new recursive/bounded watch strategy.

title: Bare-name chained method matching
text:
# Bare-name chained method matching

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dropping the receiver from chained factory calls and name-matching only the bare method is an anti-pattern because it silently attaches calls to same-named methods on unrelated types. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 Motivation says this happened in 7 of 9 statically typed languages before the work and was a correctness bug.

title: Batched first-sync writes
text:
# Batched first-sync writes

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph batches large first-sync writes so repository indexing does not exceed SQLite's SQL variable limit. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says indexing a very large repository no longer aborts during first sync with a 'too many SQL variables' error.

title: Big non-sibling file clustering
text:
# Big non-sibling file clustering

Lifecycle status: proposed

Adaptive explore needs a future strategy for big non-sibling files whose clustered view is insufficient under the 28 KB explore budget. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Frontier says Django `query.py` and `sql/query.py` are not polymorphic families, so skeletonization cannot touch them and residual Reads belong to the explore-budget / big-file-clustering frontier.

title: Big value-ref sweeps need cleanup
text:
# Big value-ref sweeps need cleanup

Lifecycle status: accepted

Large value-ref validation sweeps can consume minutes and gigabytes per on/off arm, so validation runs must plan disk cleanup after `/tmp` repo/database pairs. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#3 §7 says indexing vscode took about 2 minutes and about a 1GB DB per arm, with each on/off pair hundreds of MB to over 2GB.

title: Blanket Read-deny routing
text:
# Blanket Read-deny routing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Blanket denial of `Read` to force CodeGraph use is an anti-pattern because agents fight the denial and route around it. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says the hook A/B made the agent use ToolSearch, retry denied Read, then use `Bash python3` to read the file.

title: Boundary promotion path
text:
# Boundary promotion path

Lifecycle status: accepted

Boundary notes are a temporary floor: when a boundary form later proves precision-gateable on real repositories, it can be promoted to a synthesizer channel and the boundary note disappears because the flow connects. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 Step 3 says precision-gateable boundary forms are promoted to synthesizer channels and the note disappears on its own.

title: Boundary reporting is observational
text:
# Boundary reporting is observational

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dynamic dispatch boundary reporting must be deterministic, run only when a flow fails to connect, leave fully connected flows unchanged, and avoid changing indexing or the graph itself. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features `codegraph_explore` dynamic dispatch boundary bullet.

title: Bounded background process lifetime
text:
# Bounded background process lifetime

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph helper, stdio MCP, and shared background server processes must wind down promptly when their launching editor/agent or client connection is gone. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 Windows helper, abrupt socket failure, and shared background server safeguard bullets.

title: Bounded stale startup window
text:
# Bounded stale startup window

Lifecycle status: accepted

The first tool call may answer before a huge repository reconcile fully finishes, bounded by `CODEGRAPH_CATCHUP_GATE_TIMEOUT_MS`. CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says the default gate is 3000ms, `=0` waits for the full reconcile, and the rest finishes in the background.

title: Bounded telemetry volume
text:
# Bounded telemetry volume

Lifecycle status: accepted

Daily rollups keep monthly telemetry volume roughly active machines times active days times distinct tools used, so the PostHog free tier covers tens of thousands of monthly active users. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Volume math paragraph.

title: Bridge built-in blocklists
text:
# Bridge built-in blocklists

Lifecycle status: accepted

Native bridge resolvers must block platform-wide built-in or lifecycle names when bridge matching would otherwise over-link generic selectors or methods. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#2 §8d lists Swift-ObjC blocked names such as `init`, `description`, `hash`, `count`, `add`, `remove`, `load`, and `save` because every NSObject subclass implements them, and React Native blocked names such as `addListener`, `removeListeners`, and `startObserving` because every `RCTEventEmitter` declares them.

title: Bridge built-ins are not bridge targets
text:
# Bridge built-ins are not bridge targets

Lifecycle status: accepted

Bridge resolvers should let ordinary name matching handle generic built-in names and should not synthesize bridge edges for them. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#2 §8d says the Swift-ObjC regular name matcher handles NSObject-wide names on its own, while React Native `.addListener(...)` and `.remove(...)` calls go through `NativeEventEmitter`, not the native bridge directly.

title: Bridge heuristic references
text:
# Bridge heuristic references

Lifecycle status: proposed

Cross-language bridge resolvers should emit ordinary `references` edges with `provenance:'heuristic'` and channel-specific `metadata.synthesizedBy`, reusing the existing MCP read-tool synthesized-edge surfacing path instead of adding graph plumbing. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#0 §1 says the fix emits `references` edges with heuristic provenance and `metadata.synthesizedBy:'<channel>'`; §4 says these new edges ride the existing metadata.synthesizedBy plumbing from #312/#403 with no additional plumbing.

title: Bridged dynamic hops in trace tools
text:
# Bridged dynamic hops in trace tools

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_trace`, `codegraph_callees`, and `codegraph_explore` follow flows with no static call edge by bridging callbacks, observer registrations, EventEmitter flows, React re-renders and JSX children, Flutter `setState` to `build`, C++ virtual overrides, and Java/Kotlin interface dispatch, labeling each bridged hop inline. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 New Features.

title: Bridging headers stay ordinary
text:
# Bridging headers stay ordinary

Lifecycle status: proposed

Swift bridging headers should be indexed as Objective-C headers but their `#import` lists should not be parsed as a special manifest of what is visible to Swift. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §7 says `.h` files are indexed through #165 content sniffing, while bridging-header file content parsing is an anti-goal and the header should be treated as a normal ObjC header.

title: Build output exclusion
text:
# Build output exclusion

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph should avoid indexing committed build output directories as source coverage evidence when those directories are generated artifacts. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 notes that NestJS realworld committed `dist/` build output gets indexed and marks it as a general build-dir-ignore follow-up.

title: Build output exclusion backlog
text:
# Build output exclusion backlog

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph should add a general build-directory ignore rule so committed generated output such as NestJS `dist/` does not pollute indexed framework coverage. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 marks committed `dist/` build output being indexed in NestJS realworld as a general build-dir-ignore follow-up.

title: Bundled CodeGraph runtime
text:
# Bundled CodeGraph runtime

Lifecycle status: accepted

The bundled CodeGraph runtime is the self-contained distribution/runtime layer used by standalone installers and npm packages to run without relying on the user's Node/native build environment. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 releases 0.9.0 through 0.9.2 describe the self-contained runtime, bundled real SQLite, standalone installers, and Windows launcher invoking the bundled runtime directly.

title: Bundled SQLite WAL backend
text:
# Bundled SQLite WAL backend

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph uses real SQLite with WAL and FTS5 built into the bundled runtime to fix concurrent-read lock errors at the root and improve performance for users previously on the WASM fallback. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.0 New Features says this explicitly.

title: C assignment callback uniqueness gate
text:
# C assignment callback uniqueness gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

C extern callbacks registered by assignment across files may resolve only when the callback name is repo-unique; initializer tables are exempt because they are ungated at file scope. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits documents the cross-file assignment limit and the initializer-table exception.

title: C callback struct deferral
text:
# C callback struct deferral

Lifecycle status: deprecated

CodeGraph deliberately does not synthesize C callback-struct dispatch where `s->fn()` would fan out to hundreds of targets, and pure-virtual C++ base declarations remain unbridged because declarations are not extracted as nodes. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks C callback structs as a 422-way fan-out too noisy to synthesize and notes pure-virtual base methods are not extracted as nodes.

title: C fn-pointer deferred forms
text:
# C fn-pointer deferred forms

Lifecycle status: accepted

The shipped C fn-pointer synthesizer intentionally leaves direct function-pointer variables, array-of-function-pointers without a struct, C++ class function-pointer fields, and macro-built tables for later work. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#2 Deferred list names fp=f; fp(), array-of-fn-pointers, C++ class fn-pointer fields, and redis MAKE_CMD macro tables as out of scope.

title: C fn-pointer dispatch synthesizer
text:
# C fn-pointer dispatch synthesizer

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph shipped synthesizedBy:'fn-pointer-dispatch' for C/systems-language member-function-pointer dispatch keyed by (struct type, function-pointer field), linking field registrations to indirect recv->field(...) calls without minting new nodes. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#2 C/C++ fn-pointer dispatch row marks it shipped on 2026-06-22, names c-fnptr-synthesizer.ts, and reports validation on git, redis, curl, and lua control.

title: C fn-pointer double-hop assignment
text:
# C fn-pointer double-hop assignment

Lifecycle status: accepted

Real C fn-pointer dispatch needs field-to-field assignment handling because registrations can copy an already-registered field into another struct field before the indirect call. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#2 says the shipped source-read synth handles h->func = found->fn, the issue's hook_demo.c shape.

title: C fn-pointer struct-field key
text:
# C fn-pointer struct-field key

Lifecycle status: accepted

C fn-pointer dispatch synthesis must key registrations and indirect calls by the pair (struct type, function-pointer field) and only bridge when the receiver resolves to that struct type. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#2 says the shipped fn-pointer dispatch is keyed by (struct type, fn-pointer field), with receiver resolution from parameter/local type or unique-field fallback.

title: C macro prototype misparse
text:
# C macro prototype misparse

Lifecycle status: accepted

C macro-prefixed prototypes can be parsed as bare-identifier declarations named after the return type, creating spurious type-named globals that every function of that type may reference. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#3 §7 says `CURL_EXTERN` and `XXH_PUBLIC_API` prototypes misparse this way and the durable fix is to skip bare-identifier declarators in the C branch.

title: C value-ref extraction guards
text:
# C value-ref extraction guards

Lifecycle status: accepted

C value-reference support required emitting file-scope const/var nodes and skipping bare-identifier declarators that tree-sitter misparses from macro-prefixed prototypes. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says C required the Ruby treatment because extractor nodes were missing plus a C-specific guard for bare-identifier declarators named after return types.

title: C# handler type from base list
text:
# C# handler type from base list

Lifecycle status: accepted

C# method nodes have no `signature`, so MediatR handler request types must be recovered from the handler class base-list source such as `IRequestHandler<X,...>`. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 MediatR row says `csharp.ts` defines no `getSignature` and Pass 1 reads the first generic argument from the class base list.

title: C++ address-of-only registration
text:
# C++ address-of-only registration

Lifecycle status: accepted

C++ callback registration capture keeps `&my_cb` and file-scope tables but drops bare-name registrations because generic-name collisions made bare identifiers net-negative on real C++ repos. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits cites fmt collision behavior and says C++ bare-name registration is dropped by `addressOfOnly`, while C files keep bare args.

title: C++ bare-name callback matching
text:
# C++ bare-name callback matching

Lifecycle status: accepted

Matching C++ bare identifiers as callback registrations is an anti-pattern because generic-name collisions made it net-negative on real C++ code. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits says `register_handler(my_cb)` without `&` is dropped by `addressOfOnly` after fmt showed the collision rate made bare ids net-negative.

title: C++ export-macro misparse suppression
text:
# C++ export-macro misparse suppression

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph detects and drops bogus function nodes produced when C++ export or visibility macros make class or struct declarations parse like functions. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says `class MYLIB_EXPORT Foo : public Bar { ... }` no longer appears as a phantom function spanning the class body.

title: C++ extractor
text:
# C++ extractor

Lifecycle status: accepted

The C++ extractor is the CodeGraph indexing surface for C++ declarations and references, including class/struct parsing affected by export or visibility macros. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes describes the C++ export-macro class/struct mis-indexing fix.

title: C++ free function real names
text:
# C++ free function real names

Lifecycle status: accepted

C++ free functions with qualified-type parameters or trailing return types are now indexed under their actual function names. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says such functions were mistakenly named after a type like `string`, so calls never resolved and the defining file looked unused; now cross-file calls, callers, and blast radius work.

title: C++ override synthesis
text:
# C++ override synthesis

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph combines C++ inheritance extraction for `base_class_clause` with a capped C++-only override synthesizer from base virtual methods to subclass overrides. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks C/C++ done, reporting leveldb extends edges 219->298 and 12 precise `cpp-override` edges such as `Iterator::Next` to `MergingIterator`.

title: C++ return-typed chained receiver resolution
text:
# C++ return-typed chained receiver resolution

Lifecycle status: accepted

C++ chained receiver calls infer the receiver class from the inner call's return type and create the edge only when that class actually has the called method. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 C++ singleton/factory/chained getter bullet.

title: C++ value-ref support
text:
# C++ value-ref support

Lifecycle status: deprecated

C++ value-reference support was attempted and reverted because tree-sitter-cpp and `.h` routing produced persistent bogus file-scope constants/variables in real template- and macro-heavy code. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says C++ was attempted and reverted, two guards removed about 83% of gross leaks, but residual leaks remained pervasive and did not meet the precision bar.

title: CI telemetry retained
text:
# CI telemetry retained

Lifecycle status: accepted

CI telemetry events are kept and tagged with `ci: true` because engine-in-CI is a real usage mode, with volume to be revisited if CI dominates. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Open questions.

title: CLI graph access surface
text:
# CLI graph access surface

Lifecycle status: accepted

The CLI graph access surface is the `codegraph explore` and `codegraph node` command pair that exposes MCP-equivalent graph reads to shell-only agents. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 subagents bullet.

title: CLI mirrors MCP graph tools
text:
# CLI mirrors MCP graph tools

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph explore` and `codegraph node` print exactly what the matching MCP tools return so non-MCP and delegated shell-only agents can use the graph. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 subagents bullet.

title: CSharp namespace-qualified types
text:
# CSharp namespace-qualified types

Lifecycle status: accepted

C# types are tracked by namespace-qualified name so same-named types in different namespaces resolve separately and impact does not collapse them into one arbitrary match. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 C# namespace-qualified type bullet.

title: CSharp primary constructor parsing
text:
# CSharp primary constructor parsing

Lifecycle status: accepted

C# parsing now uses an up-to-date grammar that understands C# 12 primary constructors and records their parameters as dependencies. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says attributed primary-constructor parameters previously confused the parser enough to drop classes and methods, and now service dependencies from constructor parameters show up in blast radius and contract-dependent answers.

title: CSharp record struct indexing
text:
# CSharp record struct indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

C# `record struct`, `readonly record struct`, and positional one-line record structs now index with `struct` kind and no longer halt extraction of later declarations. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 C# record struct bullet.

title: CSharp record type indexing
text:
# CSharp record type indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

C# `record`, `record class`, and `record struct` declarations are now indexed as types. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says records were previously skipped entirely, so references, generic arguments, construction sites, and the record-defining file had no callers or dependents.

title: CSharp static value reads
text:
# CSharp static value reads

Lifecycle status: proposed

Convention-heavy apps need C# static-const/static-member value-read coverage as a separate pass from template markup parsing. Evidence: docs/design/template-markup-parser.md#0 Quantified target and Non-goals say C# static-const reads remain outside markup parsing and require extending the static-member pass to C#/TS.

title: Callable flow path unchanged
text:
# Callable flow path unchanged

Lifecycle status: accepted

The non-callable synth-hop surfacing fix leaves normal callable flow behavior unchanged because dynNamed stays empty for callable-only flows. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#2 redux-thunk follow-up 2 says the fix is a no-op for callable flows and trezor was unchanged.

title: Callable string position gate
text:
# Callable string position gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

PHP strings and Ruby symbols are treated as callable references only in known callable positions or hook DSLs; arbitrary PHP strings and framework registries are deliberately uncaptured until a framework-specific resolver exists. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits says PHP strings outside known-HOF positions and Ruby symbols outside hook DSLs are not trustworthy as callables, and WordPress-style registries belong in a `frameworks/` resolver if added.

title: Callback edge synthesizer
text:
# Callback edge synthesizer

Lifecycle status: accepted

`src/resolution/callback-synthesizer.ts` is the CodeGraph component that runs whole-graph callback and EventEmitter edge synthesis. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Status and Files touched name the merged synthesizer and describe it as the whole-graph synthesis pass.

title: Callback flow reachability
text:
# Callback flow reachability

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph needs dispatcher-to-callback flow edges for observer, event-emitter, and signal patterns so questions like how an update reaches the screen have graph paths. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Motivation says the goal is to close the dynamic-dispatch hole static extraction leaves for callbacks registered elsewhere through a shared store.

title: Callback registration visibility
text:
# Callback registration visibility

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph must surface where function-valued callbacks are registered so agents can answer where a callback is wired up instead of treating it as dead code. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Problem says function values passed as arguments, assigned, or placed in handler tables produced no edge in 19/19 tree-sitter languages, making registered callbacks look dead and hiding registration sites.

title: Callback synthesis corpus audit
text:
# Callback synthesis corpus audit

Lifecycle status: proposed

Callback synthesis needs a broad precision and recall audit across the full corpus, tallying synthesized edges per repo and spot-checking for EventEmitter-heavy explosions. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work item 6 calls for this audit.

title: Callback synthesis corpus audit
text:
# Callback synthesis corpus audit

Lifecycle status: proposed

Run a broad corpus audit that tallies synthesized edges per repo, spot-checks precision and recall, and confirms no explosion on EventEmitter-heavy repos. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work item 6 calls for this audit.

title: Callback synthesis test coverage
text:
# Callback synthesis test coverage

Lifecycle status: proposed

Add tests for callback synthesis: a vitest fixture for EventEmitter, extractor tests for named nested function extraction, and resolver tests for the Django side. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work item 7 names these tests and CHANGELOG work.

title: Callback synthesis tests
text:
# Callback synthesis tests

Lifecycle status: proposed

Callback synthesis should have vitest coverage for the EventEmitter fixture plus extractor tests for named nested functions and resolver tests for the Django side. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work item 7 says to add synthesizer, extractor, and resolver tests plus CHANGELOG coverage.

title: Canonical flow corpus case
text:
# Canonical flow corpus case

Lifecycle status: accepted

Each framework coverage pass should start with the framework's canonical "how does X reach/become Y" flow question and a real repository added to the agent-eval corpus. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 Step 1 says to pick the framework's signature data/control flow and a real repo, adding it to `.claude/skills/agent-eval/corpus.json`.

title: Celery decorator gate
text:
# Celery decorator gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

Celery dispatch precision depends on reading task decorators from source lines above the function definition because the function node start line excludes the decorator and no `decorates` edge exists. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Celery row says `@shared_task` is an unresolved external import and the decorator must be read from lines above `def`.

title: Celery deferred forms
text:
# Celery deferred forms

Lifecycle status: accepted

Celery synthesis v1 intentionally leaves canvas dispatch, class-based `Task` subclasses, `app.send_task('dotted.name')` string dispatch, and aliased imports for later work. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Celery row lists those forms under Deferred.

title: Celery dispatch synthesizer
text:
# Celery dispatch synthesizer

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph shipped `celeryDispatchEdges` for Celery by linking `.delay()` and `.apply_async()` call sites to Python task functions gated by task decorators. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Celery row marks it shipped on 2026-06-20 with 100% precision on paperless-ngx and pretix plus zero edges on httpie.

title: Celery task-decorator gate
text:
# Celery task-decorator gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

Celery dispatch synthesis must only link a `.delay()` or `.apply_async()` call when the dispatched name resolves to a Python function carrying a task decorator. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Celery row says precision rests on the decorator gate and the `kind==='function'` filter drops same-named test-method collisions.

title: Chained call resolver
text:
# Chained call resolver

Lifecycle status: accepted

The chained call resolver is the CodeGraph resolution/extraction surface for factory and fluent calls whose receiver is itself a call. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 names `src/resolution/name-matcher.ts`, `resolution/index.ts`, `tree-sitter.ts`, bespoke extractors, and `languages/*.ts` as the components for chained static-factory and fluent call resolution.

title: Chained method call resolution
text:
# Chained method call resolution

Lifecycle status: accepted

Chained method calls now resolve to their definitions instead of requiring a single-segment receiver. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says `builder.Services.AddCoreServices(...)` and similar C# extension methods or guard clauses previously found no definition, and the fix applies to C# and any language with chained calls.

title: Chained receiver marker encoding
text:
# Chained receiver marker encoding

Lifecycle status: accepted

Extraction encodes eligible chained receivers as marker strings such as `Foo.getInstance().bar`, using the `().` marker to preserve that the receiver is itself a call while remaining distinguishable from ordinary refs. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 The 3-part mechanism says `tree-sitter.ts` or bespoke extractors use this marker and language gates only re-encode factory chains.

title: Chained-call precision wins
text:
# Chained-call precision wins

Lifecycle status: accepted

The shipped mechanism often retargeted or removed wrong edges rather than merely adding missing edges, producing precision wins in Kotlin, Rust, Scala, Dart, Objective-C, and Pascal. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 Coverage reports real-repo A/B removed wrong-edge matches such as Kotlin -438, Rust -775, Scala -59, Objective-C -75, and Pascal -18.

title: Checksum-verified release bundles
text:
# Checksum-verified release bundles

Lifecycle status: accepted

Release archives ship `SHA256SUMS`, and the npm launcher verifies downloaded bundles against it, aborting on mismatch while skipping verification for older releases without checksums. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 New Features.

title: Class instantiations are callers
text:
# Class instantiations are callers

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_callers` and the callers command list class construction sites as calls to the class constructor, and callees/trace cross instantiations the same way. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 class instantiation callers bullet.

title: Class node member outlines
text:
# Class node member outlines

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_node` returns compact member outlines for class, interface, struct, and enum nodes while keeping full source for functions and methods. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.8.0 New Features says this replaces returning the entire class body for those type nodes.

title: Claude Code front-load hook
text:
# Claude Code front-load hook

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph ships an optional Claude Code prompt hook that detects structural questions and injects relevant source plus call paths into the prompt up front. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#9 Claude Code bullet says `codegraph install` asks to enable it by default, `codegraph uninstall` removes it, and `codegraph upgrade` turns it on for existing Claude setups.

title: Claude Code prompt hook
text:
# Claude Code prompt hook

Lifecycle status: accepted

The Claude Code prompt hook is the agent-specific hook surface that can front-load CodeGraph context for structural prompts. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#9 says the feature is Claude Code only because Claude Code is the agent with prompt hooks.

title: Clean reversible agent setup
text:
# Clean reversible agent setup

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph users need one command that can reverse CodeGraph agent setup across supported clients while preserving project indexes and user-owned configuration. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.3 says `codegraph uninstall` removes CodeGraph from every configured agent, removes only what `codegraph install` wrote, and leaves `.codegraph/` alone.

title: Closure collection element-invoke gate
text:
# Closure collection element-invoke gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

Closure-collection synthesis must require the dispatcher loop to invoke each collection element, because that proves the collection holds closures and prevents append-only collections from producing edges. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 3c calls `$0(`/`it(` the precision gate and says repos with no closure-collection dispatch yield 0 edges regardless of append sites.

title: Closure collection synthesis
text:
# Closure collection synthesis

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph uses `closureCollectionEdges` to link collection-draining dispatchers to closure-append registrars for Swift-style closure collections across files and classes. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 3c says Alamofire validation required callback-synthesizer `closureCollectionEdges`, pairing element-invoking collection iteration with same-field closure append sites globally by field name.

title: CodeGraph installer
text:
# CodeGraph installer

Lifecycle status: accepted

The CodeGraph installer is the CLI surface that writes agent MCP configuration, PATH installation state, and project/global setup for supported agents. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 releases 0.7.7, 0.7.9, 0.8.0, and 0.9.2 describe `codegraph install`, standalone installers, target flags, agent configs, and installer-specific fixes.

title: CodeGraph library API
text:
# CodeGraph library API

Lifecycle status: accepted

The CodeGraph library API is the embedded programmatic surface exposing index and graph checks without shelling out, including `CodeGraph.getLastIndexedAt()`. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features `codegraph status --json` bullet.

title: Cold daemon exceeds startup window
text:
# Cold daemon exceeds startup window

Lifecycle status: accepted

Under load, the current `serve --mcp` cold path can exceed the host MCP startup window because it re-execs for a Node memory flag and spawns or binds a detached daemon before tools are usable. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 gives this as the P2 root cause and notes `CODEGRAPH_WASM_RELAUNCHED=1` plus daemon prewarming remove those latencies in evals.

title: Committed ignored-default directories indexed
text:
# Committed ignored-default directories indexed

Lifecycle status: accepted

After `.gitignore` became the source of truth, committed files under directories like `vendor/`, `Pods/`, or `dist/` are indexed unless excluded through `.gitignore` rules. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.2 notes this behavior change and says to add a `.gitignore` negation to exclude them.

title: CommonJS bindings are value refs
text:
# CommonJS bindings are value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

CommonJS `var x = require(...)` bindings and module-level mutable state should not be treated as value-ref false positives when same-file readers actually depend on them. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §3 says these are correct same-file reads, changing the binding affects readers, impact deduplicates against `calls` edges, and higher JS edge share is fine if precision holds.

title: Completeness before cost drops
text:
# Completeness before cost drops

Lifecycle status: accepted

Coverage makes complete graph answers and Read-0 runs possible, but it does not guarantee lower cost because agents may still read to confirm source and codegraph calls can trade for reads. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 says coverage enables rather than forces the no-read path and the reliable win is completeness plus making Read-0 possible.

title: Component barrel re-export resolution
text:
# Component barrel re-export resolution

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph follows Svelte and Vue default component re-exports through barrel files and resolves imports used by `.svelte` and `.vue` files. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says components imported via `index.ts`, workspace packages like `@scope/ui/widgets`, and bare directory imports no longer falsely report 0 callers.

title: Concurrent reads without lock failures
text:
# Concurrent reads without lock failures

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph storage must support concurrent reads without intermittent `database is locked` failures. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.0 says the old intermittent `database is locked` errors are gone for good and real SQLite with WAL fixes concurrent-read lock errors at the root.

title: Config key-only indexing
text:
# Config key-only indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph indexes Spring configuration files by key only and omits their values from `codegraph_explore` and `codegraph_node` output; Shopify Liquid schema blocks are likewise indexed by name only. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 1.0.0 Security.

title: Configurable index directory
text:
# Configurable index directory

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph supports `CODEGRAPH_DIR` to set the per-project index directory name, defaulting to `.codegraph`, so one working tree can hold independent indexes such as `.codegraph-win` and `.codegraph`. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features `CODEGRAPH_DIR` bullet.

title: Confirm value-ref nodes exist
text:
# Confirm value-ref nodes exist

Lifecycle status: accepted

The value-reference coverage table's easy-path guess can be wrong, so a language extension must confirm that file-scope const/var nodes are actually emitted before trusting the apparent grammar path. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says C was the worked example where the extractor did not emit C file-scope const/var nodes at all and therefore §5 step C is mandatory.

title: Conformance chained-call pass
text:
# Conformance chained-call pass

Lifecycle status: accepted

Failed chained-call refs in `CHAIN_LANGUAGES` are deferred and re-resolved after inheritance and conformance edges exist, walking supertypes for inherited, default-interface, trait, mixin, and embedded methods. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 Conformance pass (#754) describes `resolveChainedCallsViaConformance()` after edges exist.

title: Constant read node check
text:
# Constant read node check

Lifecycle status: accepted

A new value-reference language must confirm the grammar node type used for constant reads before sweeping, because a reader-scan mismatch produces zero edges even when targets register correctly. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A names this as the PHP lesson: PHP constant references are `name` nodes, not `identifier` or `constant`, so edges did not form until `name` was added to `flushValueRefs`.

title: Convention app residual frontier
text:
# Convention app residual frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph should treat reflection/proxy registration and static-member value reads as a separate frontier from template markup parsing for convention-heavy apps aiming beyond the ASP.NET ~90% ceiling. Evidence: docs/design/template-markup-parser.md#0 Non-goals says reaching literal 95% additionally needs reflection/DI-registration modeling and extending the static-member pass to C#/TS, tracked separately.

title: Core indexer
text:
# Core indexer

Lifecycle status: accepted

The core indexer is the CodeGraph indexing pipeline that walks project files, extracts symbols and relationships, and persists the index database. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 indexing fixes cover dynamic call relationship linking, first-sync SQL batching, non-ASCII directory traversal, worktree exclusion, and broad-root refusal.

title: Core-floor skeletonization gate
text:
# Core-floor skeletonization gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

Keeping only the first N files full and skeletonizing the rest is unsafe because it can collapse distinct non-sibling flow steps. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Dead ends item 4 says a plain core-floor gate skeletonized Excalidraw's distinct steps and caused a 17% cost regression; the sibling condition is what makes skeletonization safe.

title: Cost outliers flipped cheaper
text:
# Cost outliers flipped cheaper

Lifecycle status: accepted

The refined adaptive explore design flipped OkHttp and Django from cost outliers into cheaper WITH-CodeGraph runs. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 Validation reports OkHttp `$0.45 → $0.50` and Django `$0.56 → $0.63`, about 10% cheaper, with read-back fixes.

title: Coverage drives CodeGraph sufficiency
text:
# Coverage drives CodeGraph sufficiency

Lifecycle status: accepted

The lever for agents using CodeGraph instead of Read is graph coverage, not prompting, hooks, or new tools; missing flows make agents reconstruct them from files, while present flows let agents answer without reading. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 1 says empirical memory proved coverage is the lever for sufficiency and gives the Excalidraw Read 0 result after closing the update-flow hole.

title: Cross-OS index sharing is unsafe
text:
# Cross-OS index sharing is unsafe

Lifecycle status: accepted

A CodeGraph index directory must not be shared between Windows and WSL because the background-server lock and SQLite database are tied to the writing OS, and SQLite locking across the WSL2/Windows filesystem boundary is unreliable. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features `CODEGRAPH_DIR` bullet.

title: Cross-language bridge flow reachability
text:
# Cross-language bridge flow reachability

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph trace, callers, callees, impact, and flow-context calls should connect end-to-end across Swift-Objective-C and JavaScript-native runtime dispatch boundaries instead of stopping at language-isolated indexes. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#0 Mission and §1 say post-#165 Swift, Objective-C, and JavaScript/TypeScript index correctly in isolation but mixed iOS, React Native, and Expo cross-language flows silently break and force agents to reconstruct bridges by reading files.

title: Current-code query results
text:
# Current-code query results

Lifecycle status: accepted

The first CodeGraph query in a session should reflect the current workspace, including edits made while the server was down or outside the editor. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 says the MCP server catches up on connect, filesystem change detection picks up git pulls, branch switches, and outside-editor edits, and the first query reflects current code.

title: Cursor explicit project path
text:
# Cursor explicit project path

Lifecycle status: accepted

The installer passes the correct project path into Cursor's MCP config so globally installed CodeGraph resolves the workspace even when Cursor launches MCP servers with the wrong working directory. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.7 Fixes says this works around Cursor launching MCP servers with the wrong working directory and fixes global installs reporting `not initialized` in every workspace.

title: Cursor orphan rule cleanup
text:
# Cursor orphan rule cleanup

Lifecycle status: accepted

Cursor uninstall now deletes the leftover `.cursor/rules/codegraph.mdc` file outright instead of leaving an orphaned empty rule, while preserving content outside CodeGraph markers. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.3 Fixes.

title: DRF inherited action frontier
text:
# DRF inherited action frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph still needs DRF ViewSet CRUD action coverage inherited from framework base classes rather than declared in the user's ViewSet. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 lists inherited DRF viewset CRUD actions as a Django/DRF residual after `router.register` extraction was fixed.

title: Daemon opt-out and version pinning
text:
# Daemon opt-out and version pinning

Lifecycle status: accepted

`CODEGRAPH_NO_DAEMON=1` opts out to one independent server per client, and daemon connections are version-pinned so upgrades never mix CodeGraph versions over the connection. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 New Features.

title: Daemon restart session continuity
text:
# Daemon restart session continuity

Lifecycle status: accepted

A session should keep CodeGraph tools available when the shared background server is restarted underneath it, without requiring the session to restart. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 daemon restart fallback bullet.

title: Daemon-gated tool exposure
text:
# Daemon-gated tool exposure

Lifecycle status: accepted

The shipped `serve --mcp` cold path makes tools usable only after a liftoff re-exec and detached daemon spawn or bind. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 gives this as the P2 root cause: `serve --mcp` does `--liftoff-only` re-exec and spawns/binds a detached daemon before tools are usable.

title: Daemon-independent tool discovery
text:
# Daemon-independent tool discovery

Lifecycle status: proposed

MCP tool discovery should not require the detached daemon to finish connecting. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 recommends exposing the static tool list instantly and decoupling `tools/list` from daemon readiness.

title: Daily local usage rollups
text:
# Daily local usage rollups

Lifecycle status: accepted

Usage events are aggregated locally into one `usage_rollup` event per `(day, kind, name)` per machine instead of emitting a per-call event stream. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Non-goals and Events sections.

title: Dart full method extraction
text:
# Dart full method extraction

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dart methods are extracted with full method bodies rather than signature-only extraction, so flow and callers/callees can see their implementation calls. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 Fixes says Dart methods that were extracted signature-only were fixed.

title: Dart generated binding noise
text:
# Dart generated binding noise

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dart generated FFI/JNI binding files can inflate sibling-class ambiguity when header-only generators are not filtered, even though common generated suffixes are already excluded. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says generated Dart JNIGEN `_bindings.dart` files with many `static final _class` targets are noisy, while `.g.dart`, `.freezed.dart`, and `.pb.dart` are filtered.

title: Dart mixin and type edges
text:
# Dart mixin and type edges

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dart `with` mixins and method parameter or return type annotations now record dependencies. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says the whole `with` clause used to be dropped, classes declared only with a mixin could lose their superclass link, and types referenced only as types had no dependents.

title: Dart static-final value refs
text:
# Dart static-final value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dart value-reference support extracts `static_final_declaration` as constants, relies on grammar separation to avoid instance/local leaks, and extends reader scanning to include the next-sibling `function_body` attached outside the stored signature node. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says `static_final_declaration` exactly captures top-level/static const/final, locals and instance fields use other grammar nodes, and the sibling body scan was required to find reads.

title: Dead resolver hook
text:
# Dead resolver hook

Lifecycle status: accepted

A framework resolver hook declared only in the interface and never invoked is an anti-pattern because shipped framework extractors silently contribute no route nodes or route-handler edges. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#0 Background says all framework resolvers had `extractNodes?`, none were called, and the graph had zero practical `route` kind nodes as a result.

title: Declarator grammar verification
text:
# Declarator grammar verification

Lifecycle status: accepted

Every new value-reference language must add its actual grammar declarator node types and bound-name extraction to the `flushValueRefs` shadow-prune switch, after verifying them by parsing a sample. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5B says this step is load-bearing, the table must not be trusted without parsing, and skipping it makes the prune silently do nothing so intra-file shadowing creates false positives.

title: Declared return type requirement
text:
# Declared return type requirement

Lifecycle status: accepted

The chained-call mechanism requires reliably declared factory return types to recover the receiver type. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 Full README classification says the real requirement is a declared return type, not merely being statically typed, and that gradually typed or dynamic languages omit them too often.

title: Declared return types define chain fit
text:
# Declared return types define chain fit

Lifecycle status: accepted

The lesson from #750 is that chained-call support fits languages with reliably declared return types, not the broader or narrower label of statically typed languages. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 says the original statically-typed README enumeration was incomplete and the through-line is reliable declared return types.

title: Declared-return chained-call mechanism
text:
# Declared-return chained-call mechanism

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph shipped a three-part mechanism for chained static-factory and fluent call resolution across 13 languages: capture declared return types, preserve chained receivers at extraction, then resolve and validate the outer method on the returned type. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 Status and The 3-part mechanism describe the shipped design for C++, C, PHP, Java, Kotlin, C#, Swift, Rust, Go, Scala, Dart, Objective-C, and Pascal/Delphi.

title: Default dependency directory excludes
text:
# Default dependency directory excludes

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph excludes dependency, build, and cache directories such as `node_modules`, `vendor`, `dist`, `build`, `target`, `.venv`, `__pycache__`, `Pods`, and `.next` by default, while allowing `.gitignore` negation to opt paths back in. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 Fixes.

title: Default import module dependencies
text:
# Default import module dependencies

Lifecycle status: accepted

TypeScript and JavaScript renamed default imports now record dependencies on their imported modules while external packages still create no edge. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says default-imported Express/NestJS route-controller modules previously looked unused because only named imports linked.

title: Default init indexing
text:
# Default init indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph init` builds the initial index by default while still accepting `-i`/`--index` so existing commands and scripts continue to work. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.8 New Features.

title: Default-on value refs
text:
# Default-on value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-reference edges are enabled by default for TS/JS/TSX, Go, Python, Rust, Ruby, C, Java, C#, PHP, Scala, Kotlin, Swift, Dart, and Pascal, and can be disabled with `CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS=0`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#0 Status says the feature is shipped and default-on for that complete language set, with `CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS=0` as the opt-out.

title: Default-on value refs
text:
# Default-on value refs

Lifecycle status: superseded

Value-reference edges are enabled by default for the validated language set and can be disabled with `CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS=0`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §1 names `valueRefsEnabled` as default ON with env opt-out, and §2 says default ON shipped for TS/JS/tsx, Go, Python, Rust, Ruby, C, Java, and C# in PR #895 and later language PRs.

title: Definition-level monorepo precision
text:
# Definition-level monorepo precision

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph must distinguish same-named symbols and types across monorepo apps, packages, files, and namespaces so callers and impact do not conflate unrelated definitions. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 same-named symbols and C# namespace-qualified type bullets.

title: Delphi form resource ownership
text:
# Delphi form resource ownership

Lifecycle status: accepted

Delphi `.dfm` and `.fmx` form definitions now link to their same-named `.pas` code-behind units through the `{$R *.dfm}` ownership directive. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says forms used only as definitions previously had no dependents, and editing a form now surfaces its owning unit.

title: Dependency-free telemetry client
text:
# Dependency-free telemetry client

Lifecycle status: accepted

The telemetry client is a small dependency-free module using in-memory counters, a bounded JSONL queue, synchronous exit append for deltas, opportunistic capped flushes, atomic queue claims, and silent fire-and-forget failure handling. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Client architecture section.

title: Detached lingering daemon
text:
# Detached lingering daemon

Lifecycle status: accepted

The daemon runs detached, outlives any single editor or terminal session, lingers briefly after the last client disconnects, then exits and cleans up; `CODEGRAPH_DAEMON_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` tunes the idle wait. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 New Features.

title: Deterministic hole localization
text:
# Deterministic hole localization

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dynamic-dispatch holes are located without an agent by reindexing the repo, running `probe-trace` between source and target symbols, using `probe-node` at the break symbol, and confirming the break is dynamic by reading the break symbol body. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 Step 2 says this exact process located `_iterable_class` and `triggerUpdate`.

title: Disabled telemetry opens no socket
text:
# Disabled telemetry opens no socket

Lifecycle status: accepted

When telemetry is disabled, no CodeGraph process may open a socket to the telemetry endpoint, including any opted-out ping. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Principles item 3.

title: Dispatch difficulty gradient
text:
# Dispatch difficulty gradient

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dynamic-dispatch work follows a real difficulty gradient: named-reference dispatch is cheap resolver work, anonymous callback dispatch is medium synthesizer work, and anonymous-arrow handlers are the hard remaining gap because they have no identity and require link-through-body synthesis. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#6 states this gradient directly under Known limits and gotchas.

title: Dispatch indirection reachability
text:
# Dispatch indirection reachability

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph needs synthesized edges across dispatch-through-indirection patterns so agent exploration can traverse real flows hidden behind registries, generated hooks, store dispatches, and action/effect mechanisms. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 says redux-thunk was the first shipped member and this backlog queues the remaining dispatch shapes behind it.

title: Dispatch mission done checklist
text:
# Dispatch mission done checklist

Lifecycle status: accepted

The dynamic-dispatch coverage mission is done only when every language-framework row has an end-to-end canonical trace, some Read-0 agent runs with the glue present, no node explosion, no regression, matrix evidence with validating repo and numbers, and ship-prep work covering mechanism tests, CHANGELOG, incremental wiring, and commit. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#6 Definition of done states these criteria for the whole mission.

title: Dispatch resolution deferral
text:
# Dispatch resolution deferral

Lifecycle status: deprecated

Function-as-value dispatch resolution remains deliberately uncovered while only the deterministic registration side ships. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Non-goal says resolving `o->cb(x)` needs data-flow through struct fields, partial coverage is worse than none, wrong edges are worse than silence, and dispatch resolution stays uncovered.

title: Dispatch synthesizer family
text:
# Dispatch synthesizer family

Lifecycle status: accepted

The dispatch synthesizer family is the CodeGraph resolution surface for dispatch-through-indirection shapes such as redux-thunk, RTK Query, object registries, Vuex, Pinia, and NgRx effects. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 defines the backlog as the dispatch-through-indirection family and lists shape-specific synthesizers and edge functions.

title: Distinctive value-ref target gate
text:
# Distinctive value-ref target gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-reference targets must be constants or variables with names at least three characters long, containing uppercase or underscore characters, and owned by file/class/module-like scope so common lowercase locals and single-letter names do not create noisy edges. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §1 lists the target gate and says the distinctive-name rule dodges single-letter and all-lowercase shadowing.

title: Django AST extraction deferred
text:
# Django AST extraction deferred

Lifecycle status: accepted

This framework-resolver wiring plan leaves Django route extraction regex-based for the targeted `path`, `url`, `re_path`, `include`, DRF router, CBV `.as_view()`, and dotted-path shapes; a tree-sitter AST rewrite is a larger follow-up and does not block the hook wiring. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#0 Scope Note explicitly says the plan does not move Django extraction from regex to AST and that the regex approach is fine for the PR's target shapes.

title: Django DRF route extraction
text:
# Django DRF route extraction

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph resolves Django and DRF URL declarations to views and ViewSets, including DRF router registrations, while retaining prior ORM QuerySet→SQL coverage. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 marks url→view via `path`/`url`/`as_view`, DRF `router.register`→ViewSet, and ORM QuerySet→SQL done on realworld, wagtail, and saleor.

title: Django URL handler shape coverage
text:
# Django URL handler shape coverage

Lifecycle status: proposed

`djangoResolver.extract` should cover the Django URL declaration shapes named in the task tests: `path()` with CBV `.as_view()`, dotted module class `.as_view()`, bare function views, `include()`, and legacy `re_path`/`url`. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#1 Step 1 lists failing tests for each shape and asserts the expected route nodes and unresolved references.

title: Django include URL dependencies
text:
# Django include URL dependencies

Lifecycle status: accepted

Django `include('app.urls')` now records a dependency from the project URLconf to the included app `urls.py`. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says app route modules mounted only through `include` no longer report no dependents and editing them surfaces the project that mounts them.

title: Django resolver extract port
text:
# Django resolver extract port

Lifecycle status: superseded

Port the Django framework resolver to the new `extract(filePath, content): { nodes, references }` contract so URL declarations emit `route` nodes and route-to-view or route-to-include unresolved references. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#1 Task 3 and Step 3 replace `djangoResolver` with an `extract()` implementation that creates `Node` route records plus `UnresolvedRef` entries for handlers resolved by `resolveHandlerName()`.

title: Django resolver extract shipped
text:
# Django resolver extract shipped

Lifecycle status: accepted

The Django resolver emits route nodes and handler references under the new `extract(filePath, content): { nodes, references }` contract, and its end-to-end path proves a real `urls.py -> views.py` edge. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#4 Fix says existing resolvers now emit both nodes and references; Tests says the Django integration test verifies a real `urls.py -> views.py` edge.

title: Do not depend on host pending retry
text:
# Do not depend on host pending retry

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph should file the host-side wait/retry request but not depend on MCP-client pending retry as the P2 fix. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says wait/retry is Claude Code client behavior, not CodeGraph's to fix, and recommends leaning on CodeGraph-side fixes instead.

title: Doc cleanup validation breadth
text:
# Doc cleanup validation breadth

Lifecycle status: accepted

The doc-comment cleanup was validated end-to-end across all 19 code languages plus Svelte and Vue `<script>` blocks, making documentation text cleanliness a cross-language behavior rather than a narrow parser fix. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 doc-comment cleanup bullet.

title: Downloaded bundles verify integrity
text:
# Downloaded bundles verify integrity

Lifecycle status: accepted

Downloaded CodeGraph release bundles must be checked against release-published checksums before execution or use. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 says release archives ship `SHA256SUMS` and the npm launcher verifies downloaded bundles, aborting on mismatch.

title: Drupal entity handler frontier
text:
# Drupal entity handler frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph still needs Drupal entity-annotation and attribute-hook handling because `_entity_form: type.op` resolves through PHP `#[ContentEntityType]` handlers and Drupal 11 moved procedural hooks to `#[Hook]` attributes. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 names the entity-annotation handler frontier and says core has 418 `#[Hook]` files versus 3 procedural hooks, leaving the current hook detection obsolete.

title: Drupal routing handler resolver
text:
# Drupal routing handler resolver

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph resolves Drupal routing YAML `_controller` and `_form` handlers through FQCN claimsReference, single-colon controller-service matching, and Drupal project detection from composer metadata plus `*.info.yml` fallback. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks PHP Drupal done, citing admin_toolbar 0->14, webform, and core 536->731 route resolution gains.

title: Dual extraction path coverage
text:
# Dual extraction path coverage

Lifecycle status: accepted

Framework extraction wiring must cover both the main-thread `extractFromSource` path and the worker-thread parse path, otherwise route extraction remains incomplete depending on how parsing is executed. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#0 File Structure says `src/extraction/index.ts` plugs framework extraction into `ExtractionOrchestrator.indexAll` and `src/extraction/parse-worker.ts` passes detected framework names into the worker because both paths have to cover this.

title: Dynamic boundary detector
text:
# Dynamic boundary detector

Lifecycle status: accepted

`src/mcp/dynamic-boundaries.ts` is the CodeGraph component that surfaces dynamic dispatch boundaries when a static trace cannot safely synthesize an edge. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 Step 3 names `src/mcp/dynamic-boundaries.ts` and #687 as the boundary-surfacing mechanism.

title: Dynamic flow boundary reporting
text:
# Dynamic flow boundary reporting

Lifecycle status: accepted
