`codegraph_explore` now announces the exact dispatch site where a static path stops and shortlists likely runtime targets when the dispatch key is visible in source. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features `codegraph_explore` dynamic dispatch boundary bullet.

title: Embeddable graph API
text:
# Embeddable graph API

Lifecycle status: accepted

Applications should be able to drive CodeGraph programmatically as a library instead of only through the CLI or MCP server. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.8 says `require("@colbymchenry/codegraph")` and `import` expose the programmatic API for embedding, such as from an Electron process.

title: Embedded API Node floor
text:
# Embedded API Node floor

Lifecycle status: accepted

Embedded CodeGraph runs on the host application's runtime and therefore requires Node 22.5+ for built-in SQLite. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.8 New Features.

title: Empty optional MCP lists
text:
# Empty optional MCP lists

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph's MCP server answers `resources/list` and `prompts/list` probes with empty lists instead of errors. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says this clears `-32601` messages that opencode and Codex logged on connect.

title: End-to-end dispatch flow closure
text:
# End-to-end dispatch flow closure

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dispatch synthesizers must close flows end-to-end before shipping because partial coverage is worse than none. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Discipline item 5 cites playbook section 7 and says to close each flow end-to-end and re-measure, never ship a half-bridged flow.

title: End-to-end flow answers
text:
# End-to-end flow answers

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph tools should answer how execution flows from an entry point to downstream handlers or callees without requiring follow-up file reads or tool hops. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 says request-to-handler flows trace end-to-end, `codegraph_trace` returns a self-contained flow dossier, and `codegraph_explore` leads with execution flow when the query names flow symbols.

title: Endpoint before telemetry release
text:
# Endpoint before telemetry release

Lifecycle status: proposed

Worker deploy and DNS must go live before releasing the first telemetry-enabled client so the first shipping client never POSTs to a missing endpoint. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Rollout step 2.

title: Enterprise Java config reachability
text:
# Enterprise Java config reachability

Lifecycle status: accepted

Enterprise Java traces should connect mapper and configuration references to the implementation or config keys they use, including common Spring and MyBatis indirection. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 says MyBatis XML mappers link to Java mapper interfaces, Spring config references resolve to application config keys, and field-injected beans resolve to concrete implementations.

title: Enterprise Spring MyBatis flow tracing
text:
# Enterprise Spring MyBatis flow tracing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph traces enterprise Spring and MyBatis flows by indexing MyBatis XML mappers, linking them to Java mapper interfaces, resolving Spring `@Value` and `@ConfigurationProperties` keys with relaxed binding, and resolving field-injected concrete beans. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 New Features.

title: Entry-node skeletonization gate
text:
# Entry-node skeletonization gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

Using entry-node membership as the skeletonization gate fails for precise symbol-bag explore queries because every chain participant is named and therefore treated as an entry node. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Dead ends item 2 says this leaves no separation and nothing skeletonizes.

title: Event fan-out cap
text:
# Event fan-out cap

Lifecycle status: accepted

EventEmitter synthesis must skip event literals with more than six handlers or dispatchers until receiver-type matching exists, to avoid over-linking generic events like `error` or `change`. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Phase 2 says the build uses `EVENT_FANOUT_CAP = 6` as the precision guard instead of receiver-type matching.

title: EventEmitter channel synthesis
text:
# EventEmitter channel synthesis

Lifecycle status: accepted

EventEmitter synthesis scans files for literal `on`/`once`/`addListener` registrations and `emit`/`fire`/`dispatchEvent` dispatches, correlates by event-name literal, and links the enclosing dispatcher function to named handlers. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Phase 2 describes the file-oriented scan and event-name correlation.

title: EventEmitter receiver matching
text:
# EventEmitter receiver matching

Lifecycle status: proposed

EventEmitter synthesis should use receiver-type matching so `x.emit('change')` links only to handlers registered on the same receiver type, allowing the fan-out cap to relax. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work item 3 proposes replacing or augmenting the fan-out cap with `type_of`-based receiver-type matching.

title: Exact function-ref resolution
text:
# Exact function-ref resolution

Lifecycle status: accepted

Function-ref resolution must match only function or method targets in the same language family, prefer same-file exact matches, allow cross-file matches only when unique, avoid self-loops, and never use fuzzy fallback. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Mechanism and Precision rule 9 state `resolveViaImport` then `matchFunctionRef`, exact names only, same-file first, unique cross-file only, ambiguity yields no edge, and `matchReference` short-circuits `function_ref` refs to avoid fuzzy fallback.

title: Exact symbol source locations
text:
# Exact symbol source locations

Lifecycle status: accepted

Indexed symbol locations must match the file's actual line numbers so search, node, and explore output can point to the exact source line. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 says Svelte and Vue `<script>` symbols were reported one line below their actual location and now match the file exactly.

title: Exact valueRef edge filter
text:
# Exact valueRef edge filter

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-ref validation queries must filter exact value-reference edges with `kind='references'` and metadata containing `"valueRef":true`, not broad `LIKE '%valueRef%'` matching. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §4.1 says the precise filter is required because broad LIKE matches filenames such as `textModelValueReference.ts`.

title: Excalidraw no-read update answers
text:
# Excalidraw no-read update answers

Lifecycle status: accepted

Closing the Excalidraw update-flow hole enabled 2 of 3 headless agent runs to answer how an update reaches the screen with Read 0 and a complete answer, while not forcing agents that choose to confirm by reading. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 1 reports this result and caveats that coverage enables but does not force the no-read path.

title: Explain static flow dead ends
text:
# Explain static flow dead ends

Lifecycle status: accepted

When CodeGraph cannot connect requested symbols statically because execution dispatches through runtime mechanisms, the explore surface should explain where the static path stops instead of going silent. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features `codegraph_explore` dynamic dispatch boundary bullet.

title: Explicit indexing control
text:
# Explicit indexing control

Lifecycle status: accepted

Installing CodeGraph must not implicitly decide what project gets indexed. CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says `codegraph install` now wires agents and stops, while graph construction is explicitly `codegraph init` or `codegraph index` so users decide what gets indexed and when.

title: Explicit telemetry schema growth
text:
# Explicit telemetry schema growth

Lifecycle status: accepted

Adding any telemetry field requires a PR that edits docs/design/telemetry.md, repo-root TELEMETRY.md, and the Worker allowlist together. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Principles item 1.

title: Explore blast radius footer
text:
# Explore blast radius footer

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_explore` includes a compact blast-radius section listing who depends on inspected symbols by location and which test files cover them, skipping symbols with no dependents to keep output short. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.9 New Features.

title: Explore call-it-first guidance
text:
# Explore call-it-first guidance

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_explore` parameter guidance no longer tells agents to run `codegraph_search` first, preserving explore's intended call-it-first workflow. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 `codegraph_explore` guidance bullet.

title: Explore complete source units
text:
# Explore complete source units

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_explore` must not return truncated method bodies; when it reaches its size budget, it should omit whole methods or whole files and list what was dropped. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.9 Fixes says explore never returns half a method anymore.

title: Explore flow-first answers
text:
# Explore flow-first answers

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_explore` leads with execution flow when a query names symbols in a flow, finding call paths among those symbols including dynamic-dispatch hops. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 New Features.

title: Explore output hard cap
text:
# Explore output hard cap

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_explore` output must be hard-capped to its size budget so oversized responses do not overrun the cap and stay in the agent context across turns. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.8.0 Fixes states explore output is now hard-capped to its size budget.

title: Explore primary MCP surface
text:
# Explore primary MCP surface

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_explore` became the primary MCP tool: it accepts plain questions, returns Read-equivalent source grouped by file, includes flow information, and replaces the narrower `codegraph_context` and `codegraph_trace` tools. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.9 New Features.

title: Explore ranking compatibility escape hatch
text:
# Explore ranking compatibility escape hatch

Lifecycle status: accepted

Multi-term ranking must leave single-layer projects unaffected and provide an environment-variable rollback to the previous ranking. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#10 says single-layer projects are unaffected and `CODEGRAPH_RANK_NO_MULTITERM=1` reverts to the previous ranking.

title: Explore source line numbers
text:
# Explore source line numbers

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_explore` includes line numbers in source output so agents can cite `file:line` directly from explore results without reopening files. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.8.0 New Features says source now includes line numbers and `CODEGRAPH_EXPLORE_LINENUMS=0` disables it.

title: Explore-only flow surfacing
text:
# Explore-only flow surfacing

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_explore` is now the single surfacing tool for synthesized callback flows; removed `codegraph_trace` and `codegraph_context` are replaced by explore Flow output and the `codegraph_node` trail. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Update 2026-06-01 says those MCP tools were removed and `codegraph_explore` is the single surfacing tool now.

title: Expo generic method bridge indexing
text:
# Expo generic method bridge indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Expo Module methods declared with generic type syntax such as `AsyncFunction<Float>("getBatteryLevelAsync")` are indexed instead of being dropped. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 React Native / Expo generic Android method bullet.

title: Expo modules extractor
text:
# Expo modules extractor

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph extracts Expo Modules Swift/Kotlin `Module { Name; Function; AsyncFunction; Property }` declarations into synthetic method nodes so JS `requireNativeModule('X').fn(...)` calls resolve through existing name matching. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks Expo Modules done, with expo-haptics 6 nodes, expo-camera 41, and an Expo SDK sweep of 134 method nodes.

title: Express custom router frontier
text:
# Express custom router frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph still needs coverage for custom router abstractions that do not use Express-style `app.get` or `router.post` route shapes. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 says payload's 6.4k-file codebase had 0 routes because its router abstraction is not `app.get`-style, leaving custom routers as the Express residual.

title: Express final handler rule
text:
# Express final handler rule

Lifecycle status: proposed

Express route extraction must treat the final comma-separated handler argument as the route handler reference because intermediate arguments conventionally represent middleware. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#2 Task 5 Step 1 comments that multiple handlers should prefer the last one, and Step 3 implements `handlerParts[handlerParts.length - 1]`.

title: Express handler shape coverage
text:
# Express handler shape coverage

Lifecycle status: proposed

Express resolver extraction should emit route nodes and route-to-handler references for `app` and `router` method calls, including inline handler identifiers, middleware chains, and controller method references. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#2 Task 5 Step 1 lists failing tests for `app.get('/users', listUsers)`, `router.post('/items', auth, createItem)`, and `app.get('/x', userController.list)`.

title: Express inline handler resolution
text:
# Express inline handler resolution

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph resolves Express/Koa named handlers, middleware/controller/service flows, and inline arrow handlers to service body calls. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 marks request→route→handler→service done, including named handlers, middleware, controller/service resolver, and inline arrow handlers→service body calls validated on realworld, parse, and ghost with 65 ghost edges.

title: Express resolver extract port
text:
# Express resolver extract port

Lifecycle status: superseded

Replace the Express resolver's old `extractNodes` path with `extract(filePath, content): { nodes, references }` so Express-style route calls create route nodes and unresolved handler references. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#2 Task 5 Step 3 instructs replacing `extractNodes` with `extract`, matching `(app|router).METHOD('/path', handler-expr)`, emitting `Node` route objects, and using `extractTailIdent` for handler references.

title: Express resolver extract shipped
text:
# Express resolver extract shipped

Lifecycle status: accepted

The Express resolver emits route nodes and handler references under the new `extract(filePath, content): { nodes, references }` contract. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#4 Fix says Express was among the existing framework resolvers updated to emit both route nodes and handler references.

title: Extend tools before adding tools
text:
# Extend tools before adding tools

Lifecycle status: accepted

Extending an existing CodeGraph tool is more likely to be adopted by agents than adding a new tool. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says new tools fare worse than extending an existing one, citing under-pick of `trace` and removal of `codegraph_context`.

title: Extension config fail-soft
text:
# Extension config fail-soft

Lifecycle status: accepted

Custom extension mapping must not break indexing: malformed config or typoed language names are warned about and skipped, and projects without `codegraph.json` behave as before. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#10 says malformed configs and typoed languages are skipped with warnings rather than breaking indexing, and absent config preserves previous behavior.

title: Extension mappings override built-ins
text:
# Extension mappings override built-ins

Lifecycle status: accepted

Repo-local extension mappings layer on top of built-in language extensions and win on conflict, allowing projects to repoint even a built-in extension such as `.h` to C++. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#10 says mappings layer on top of built-ins, win on conflict, and can re-point `.h` to `cpp`.

title: Extraction blast-radius validation
text:
# Extraction blast-radius validation

Lifecycle status: accepted

Changes in the shared tree-sitter extraction walker must re-check node counts across several languages because a callback extraction tweak can affect broad node emission. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#6 says extraction changes are high blast radius, the Phase-3 named-inline-callback extraction is in the shared `tree-sitter.ts` walker, and node counts across several languages must be re-checked after any extraction change.

title: Fabric view extractor
text:
# Fabric view extractor

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph extracts React Native Fabric and legacy Paper view components from Codegen TS specs, `RCT_EXPORT_VIEW_PROPERTY`, and `@ReactProp`, then synthesizes component-to-native implementation links by RN naming conventions. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks Fabric/Paper views done and validates RNSegmentedControl, RNScreens, and RNSkia, including monorepo package detection for RNSkia.

title: Fail-soft gitignore parsing
text:
# Fail-soft gitignore parsing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph skips a `.gitignore` that is not valid UTF-8 and drops only individual unparseable patterns from text ignore files, logging a warning naming the file while indexing continues. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 `.gitignore` invalid UTF-8 and unparseable pattern bullet.

title: Fail-soft ignore parsing
text:
# Fail-soft ignore parsing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Indexing must continue when an ignore file contains invalid UTF-8 or a pattern the matcher cannot compile, while naming the offending file in a warning. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 `.gitignore` invalid UTF-8 and unparseable pattern bullet.

title: Family base methods read back
text:
# Family base methods read back

Lifecycle status: accepted

Whole-file family skeletonization can elide the base method that actually answers the question, causing the agent to Read it back. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Frontier says `compiler.py` is skeletonized whole, so `SQLCompiler.execute_sql` becomes a signature and is Read back in about half the Django runs.

title: Far endpoints must be queryable
text:
# Far endpoints must be queryable

Lifecycle status: accepted

A synthesizer whose far endpoint no normal query would name has little value even if it adds an edge. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Discipline item 4 cites the trezor eleven-explores tail and says to prefer shapes whose endpoints are names agents type.

title: Field-observer channel synthesis
text:
# Field-observer channel synthesis

Lifecycle status: accepted

Field-observer synthesis pairs registrar and dispatcher candidates by same file plus same callback-store field, recovers named registration arguments, and synthesizes dispatcher-to-callback edges capped at 40 callbacks per channel. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Phase 1 describes the shipped algorithm and its divergence from class-based pairing and tree-sitter argument recovery.

title: Fifteen-language value-ref validation
text:
# Fifteen-language value-ref validation

Lifecycle status: accepted

The shipped value-reference feature passed the documented validation matrix across all fifteen supported languages: TS/JS, Go, Python, Rust, Ruby, C, Java, C#, PHP, Scala, Kotlin, Swift, Dart, and Pascal kept node counts identical on/off, held precision guards, and showed that disabling value refs makes impact analysis under-report constants read by many symbols. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#1 Validation matrix states node count never moved across S/M/L repos in all fifteen languages, precision guards held, and the `impact` OFF column is the bug.

title: File-wide class-scope targets
text:
# File-wide class-scope targets

Lifecycle status: accepted

Class-scope value-reference matching uses a file-wide target map with one target per name per file rather than strict same-class matching. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A says class-scope precision intentionally uses a file-wide target map because lexical-scope languages such as Ruby allow a nested class to read an enclosing class constant, and strict same-class matching would drop those valid reads.

title: Filesystem-based change detection
text:
# Filesystem-based change detection

Lifecycle status: accepted

Index freshness is driven by filesystem change detection instead of `git status`, so `git pull`, branch switches, and outside-editor edits are picked up without a full re-index. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 Fixes.

title: First-party telemetry endpoint
text:
# First-party telemetry endpoint

Lifecycle status: accepted

Published clients may only talk to `telemetry.getcodegraph.com`; the domain must be first-party because the URL baked into an npm release POSTs there forever. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Principles item 4.

title: First-turn CodeGraph availability
text:
# First-turn CodeGraph availability

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph tools should be available before the agent's first turn so the session does not start with `Read`/`grep` as the only path. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 frames P2 as `serve --mcp` being pending when the first turn fires, causing agents to start without CodeGraph.

title: Flag A/B preserves indexes
text:
# Flag A/B preserves indexes

Lifecycle status: accepted

A value-ref flag A/B must use fresh on/off indexes and must not reuse the agent-eval template as-is when it switches builds and re-indexes without preserving the flag-specific index. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §4.3 says to pre-warm separate on/off daemons and warns that `scripts/agent-eval/ab-new-vs-baseline.sh` switches builds and re-indexes with no flag, wiping a flag-specific index.

title: Flask FastAPI decorator coverage
text:
# Flask FastAPI decorator coverage

Lifecycle status: proposed

Flask and FastAPI resolver extraction should emit route nodes and route-to-handler references for the decorator shapes named in the tests: Flask `@app.route`, Flask blueprint `@users_bp.route(..., methods=['POST'])`, FastAPI `@app.get`, and FastAPI `@router.post`. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#2 Task 4 Step 1 lists failing tests asserting route names such as `GET /users` and `POST /<id>` plus handler reference names.

title: Flask FastAPI resolver extract port
text:
# Flask FastAPI resolver extract port

Lifecycle status: superseded

Port the Flask and FastAPI resolvers to the `extract(filePath, content): { nodes, references }` contract so Python decorator routes create `route` nodes and route-to-handler unresolved references. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#2 Task 4 Step 3 replaces `flaskResolver` and `fastapiResolver` with `extract()` implementations that guard on `.py`, call `extractDecoratorRoutes`, and keep resolver-specific detection and `resolve()` behavior.

title: Flask FastAPI resolver extract shipped
text:
# Flask FastAPI resolver extract shipped

Lifecycle status: accepted

The Flask and FastAPI resolvers emit route nodes and handler references under the new `extract(filePath, content): { nodes, references }` contract. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#4 Fix says all existing framework resolvers, including Flask and FastAPI, were updated to emit both route nodes and handler references.

title: Flask FastAPI route expansion
text:
# Flask FastAPI route expansion

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph resolves Flask and FastAPI route decorators across intervening decorators, stacked routes, router-root empty paths, built-in-like handler names, Flask-RESTful resources, tuple methods, and app-factory/subdirectory detection. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 marks Flask handler resolution across `@login_required`, stacked `@x.route`, FastAPI `@router.get("")` including multiline, a bare-name builtin guard, Flask-RESTful `add_resource`, tuple `methods=('GET',)`, and broadened detection as done with microblog, redash, realworld, Netflix dispatch, and flask-realworld metrics.

title: Flat-cost recursive watcher
text:
# Flat-cost recursive watcher

Lifecycle status: accepted

The background watcher now uses a single recursive watch on macOS and Windows and bounded per-directory watches on Linux. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says this replaced one open file handle per watched file, keeping watcher cost flat no matter how large the project is.

title: Flexible affected path inputs
text:
# Flexible affected path inputs

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph affected` should accept the path forms other tools commonly emit, including `./`-prefixed and absolute paths, instead of silently treating them as no match. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says passing `./src/x.ts` or an absolute path used to report no affected tests and now works.

title: Flow spine stays full
text:
# Flow spine stays full

Lifecycle status: accepted

Symbols on the traced flow spine must be kept as full source because they are the mechanism the agent is walking. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 The refined gate requires files to be off the flow spine before skeletonization, and says the chain is always kept full.

title: Flutter app-dispatch frontier
text:
# Flutter app-dispatch frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph still lacks Flutter MVVM Command/ChangeNotifier dispatch and `Navigator.push(MaterialPageRoute(builder:))` navigation route bridging. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks those as hole-identified Flutter frontiers after setState/build support.

title: Flutter setState build synthesis
text:
# Flutter setState build synthesis

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph synthesizes Dart `setState` callers to `build` and fixes Dart method ranges so method bodies span sibling body nodes rather than signature-only lines. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks Flutter done, says the range fix is required for body analysis, and validates counter, books, and compass_app widget flows without control regressions.

title: Focused default MCP tools
text:
# Focused default MCP tools

Lifecycle status: accepted

The default MCP tool list is four tools: `codegraph_explore`, `codegraph_node`, `codegraph_search`, and `codegraph_callers`; `CODEGRAPH_MCP_TOOLS` can still re-enable the other functional tools. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 bullet 'The MCP tool list is now a focused default of four.'

title: Forced CodeGraph-only isolates sufficiency
text:
# Forced CodeGraph-only isolates sufficiency

Lifecycle status: accepted

Blocking Read, Grep, Glob, and Bash search is the variance-free way to test whether CodeGraph output is sufficient separately from whether agents adopt it voluntarily. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 3d says the forced CodeGraph-only hook confirms sufficiency separately from adoption, and Section 3c reports 3/3 forced CodeGraph-only Alamofire answers were correct.

title: Forks are not independent validation
text:
# Forks are not independent validation

Lifecycle status: accepted

A forked repository does not satisfy the independent-repository validation bar for a dispatch shape because it can share the same design lineage and skeleton. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#2 says trezor-suite and OneKey hardware-js-sdk are two indexable repos but one design lineage because OneKey is a @trezor/connect fork with the same findMethod/MethodConstructor/ApiMethods skeleton.

title: Framework extract hook
text:
# Framework extract hook

Lifecycle status: superseded

CodeGraph should replace the unused `FrameworkResolver.extractNodes?(filePath, content): Node[]` hook with `extract?(filePath, content): { nodes, references }` so each framework resolver can contribute both route nodes and route-to-handler unresolved references. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#0 Architecture and Task 1 specify replacing `extractNodes?` with `extract?` returning `FrameworkExtractionResult`.

title: Framework extract hook shipped
text:
# Framework extract hook shipped

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph replaced the dead `extractNodes?(filePath, content): Node[]` hook with `extract?(filePath, content): { nodes, references }` so framework resolvers can emit both route nodes and handler references. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#4 Fix says the dead hook was replaced with `extract?(filePath, content): { nodes, references }`.

title: Framework extraction dispatch
text:
# Framework extraction dispatch

Lifecycle status: superseded

CodeGraph should call framework `extract()` once per parsed file during extraction for detected frameworks whose `languages` include that file's language, using a new `getApplicableFrameworks(language)` helper while preserving project-level `detectFrameworks`. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#0 Architecture says extraction runs after tree-sitter parses a file for any framework whose language matches; Task 2 adds `getApplicableFrameworks` to filter detected frameworks by `languages` with universal fallback.

title: Framework extraction test coverage shipped
text:
# Framework extraction test coverage shipped

Lifecycle status: accepted

Framework extraction is covered by per-framework unit tests in `__tests__/frameworks.test.ts` and an end-to-end Django integration test in `__tests__/frameworks-integration.test.ts` that verifies a real `urls.py -> views.py` edge. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#4 Tests lists those unit and integration test files and the real Django edge assertion.

title: Framework extraction test split
text:
# Framework extraction test split

Lifecycle status: superseded

Framework extraction tests should be split into fast string-in/string-out framework unit tests and a slower CodeGraph DB integration test that proves a route-to-class `references` edge exists end to end. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#0 File Structure adds `__tests__/frameworks.test.ts` and `__tests__/frameworks-integration.test.ts`; the rationale says unit tests are deterministic and millisecond-fast while the DB integration test gives the strongest behavioral guarantee.

title: Framework extractor warning isolation
text:
# Framework extractor warning isolation

Lifecycle status: proposed

Framework extractor failures should be isolated per extractor and reported as warning errors instead of aborting file extraction. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#3 Task 7 Step 3 wraps each `fw.extract(filePath, content)` in `try/catch` and pushes a warning with `Framework extractor '<name>' failed` into `result.errors`.

title: Framework hooks need call sites
text:
# Framework hooks need call sites

Lifecycle status: accepted

Framework extension hooks must have an exercised extraction call site and tests proving the hook is invoked, otherwise resolver methods can exist only on the interface while contributing no graph data. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#0 Background says grep found exactly one `extractNodes` reference, the interface definition, so none of the shipped resolver hooks were ever called.

title: Framework resolver layer
text:
# Framework resolver layer

Lifecycle status: accepted

The framework resolver layer is CodeGraph's resolution surface for framework-specific named-reference resolution such as Django ORM descriptor calls. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 3a lists `src/resolution/types.ts`, `src/resolution/index.ts`, and `src/resolution/frameworks/python.ts` as the resolver files for the Django descriptor pattern.

title: Framework route README coverage
text:
# Framework route README coverage

Lifecycle status: proposed

The README should document framework-aware route extraction, the supported framework families, and that `codegraph_callers(YourView)` can surface route patterns as incoming edges. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#3 Task 8 Step 3 provides the README section and caller-query behavior to add.

title: Framework route extractors
text:
# Framework route extractors

Lifecycle status: accepted

Framework route extractors are the CodeGraph extraction and synthesis surface for turning web-framework route declarations into route nodes and route-to-handler edges. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 is organized around canonical web framework request/route flows and lists route extraction or synthesis mechanisms for React Router, Express/Koa, Django/DRF, Flask/FastAPI, Go routers, GoFrame, Rust web frameworks, Spring, Kotlin Spring, and Vapor.

title: Framework-aware route docs
text:
# Framework-aware route docs

Lifecycle status: proposed

Document framework-aware route extraction in the README, including the supported routing families and the `codegraph_callers(YourView)` route-pattern behavior. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#3 Task 8 Step 3 appends a `Framework-aware Routes` README section listing supported frameworks and the caller-query behavior.

title: Framework-level dispatch completion
text:
# Framework-level dispatch completion

Lifecycle status: accepted

Claiming a framework is covered after one dispatch shape is an anti-pattern because it hides other shapes in the same framework. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Discipline item 2 says do not let 'we did Redux' hide redux-thunk, RTK Query, and slice-dispatch as separate shapes.

title: Frameworks excluded from value refs
text:
# Frameworks excluded from value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

Frameworks are not a separate value-reference coverage axis; value refs are framework-agnostic and framework behavior belongs to route-node extraction. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §2b says the README framework list is a separate route-node extraction feature, value-refs cover constants through underlying language support, and no separate framework matrix is needed.

title: Frontend crowd-out avoided
text:
# Frontend crowd-out avoided

Lifecycle status: accepted

Backend-flow questions in multi-layer API-plus-frontend repositories now return the server-side service or handler instead of a wall of frontend views. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#10 says files corroborated by two or more distinct query terms are kept even when a denser unrelated layer would otherwise crowd them out.

title: Frontier dispatch surfacing
text:
# Frontier dispatch surfacing

Lifecycle status: accepted

When a dynamic dispatch form cannot be precision-gated into a static edge, CodeGraph should still show where the flow continues and likely candidate targets so readers do not have to reconstruct the flow from files. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 Step 3 says boundary surfacing announces the dispatch site, file:line, form, and candidate targets, saving the read-reconstruction spiral.

title: Frontier triage pass
text:
# Frontier triage pass

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph swept the documented dynamic-dispatch frontiers, closed tractable high-value partials, and deliberately left noisy or hard forms unbuilt. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#6 Frontier pass says React Router object data-router, Next.js route false-positive fixes, Flask-RESTful, Flask tuple methods, Flask app-factory detection, and gorilla/mux confirmation were done, while C callback structs, metaprogramming finders, reactive runtimes, Akka actor dispatch, anonymous inline closures, React lazy data-router, and C++ pure-virtual base methods were left because forcing them would add noise and violate partial-coverage discipline.

title: Full Read parity for file view
text:
# Full Read parity for file view

Lifecycle status: accepted

`handleFileView` makes `codegraph_node` read an indexed source file exactly like the `Read` tool, but faster, while adding only a one-line blast-radius header. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 marks P1 resolved on 2026-06-08 via Read parity and lists the shipped `handleFileView` behavior, tests, and full-suite validation.

title: Full index rebuild command
text:
# Full index rebuild command

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph index` rebuilds the full graph from scratch. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says rerunning `index` on an unchanged project now clears and re-indexes for the same result as fresh `init`, while `codegraph sync` remains the fast incremental path.

title: Function reference capture pipeline
text:
# Function reference capture pipeline

Lifecycle status: accepted

The function reference capture pipeline is the CodeGraph extraction and resolution path for function-as-value registration sites. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Mechanism names `src/extraction/function-ref.ts`, `flushFnRefCandidates`, internal `referenceKind: 'function_ref'`, `resolveOne`, `resolveViaImport`, `matchFunctionRef`, and `src/resolution/index.ts`.

title: Function-ref extraction gate
text:
# Function-ref extraction gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

Function-ref candidates survive extraction only when the name matches a same-file function or method or an imported binding, with C-family file-scope initializer positions as the specific ungated exception. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Precision rules 1 and 2 describe the gate, the imported-binding-only condition, the C file-scope constant-expression exception, and the false positives caused when local RHS/varinit positions were ungated.

title: Function-ref false positives are language-specific
text:
# Function-ref false positives are language-specific

Lifecycle status: accepted

Function-reference precision depends on language-specific value-position rules because each broadening rule in the design was bought by real-repo false positives. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Precision rules cite failures in excalidraw, redis/jemalloc, fmt, Alamofire, docopt.py, and generated jquery, leading to imported-binding gates, C++ address-of-only matching, Swift overload refusal, param-forward skips, destructuring skips, and generated/minified skips.

title: Function-ref registration capture
text:
# Function-ref registration capture

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph ships function-as-value registration capture by extracting deterministic value-position candidates, gating them, resolving them as internal `function_ref` references, and emitting ordinary `references` edges with function-ref metadata. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Mechanism describes the capture → gate → unresolved `function_ref` → exact resolution → `references` edge pipeline and says callers/callees/impact radius already traverse `references`, so no graph-layer changes were needed.

title: Function-ref shadowing residual
text:
# Function-ref shadowing residual

Lifecycle status: accepted

Function-ref capture accepts a residual ambiguity where local variables or parameters shadow imported or same-file functions, because resolving it would require local-scope tracking beyond the deliberately uncovered data-flow frontier. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits reports roughly 1-2 such cases per 20 sampled edges on callback-heavy repos while the file-level dependency was real in every observed case.

title: Function-ref validation invariants
text:
# Function-ref validation invariants

Lifecycle status: accepted

Function-ref capture must prove node counts identical, `calls` edges unchanged, `references` strictly additive, sampled `fnRef` edges precise, and unresolved ref batches drained. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Validation says the 2026-06-11 A/B used fresh public OSS clones, identical nodes, untouched calls, additive references, source-line spot checks, and fully drained `unresolved_refs`.

title: Gate needs separable candidates
text:
# Gate needs separable candidates

Lifecycle status: accepted

A skeletonization gate must distinguish named flow participants from collapsible candidates; entry-node membership is not separable for precise symbol-bag queries because those queries name every chain participant. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Dead ends item 2 says gating on entry-node membership leaves no separation and nothing skeletonizes.

title: Gemini Antigravity installer targets
text:
# Gemini Antigravity installer targets

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph install` supports Gemini CLI, the rebranded Antigravity CLI, and the Antigravity IDE, preserving sibling settings and MCP servers across reinstalls. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 New Features.

title: Generated artifact rank demotion
text:
# Generated artifact rank demotion

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph ranks generated artifacts such as protobuf, gRPC stubs, mocks, and build output last in search, trace, and explore so results land on real implementation source instead of auto-generated placeholders. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.7 New Features.

title: Generated-file guard is path-only
text:
# Generated-file guard is path-only

Lifecycle status: accepted

The value-ref generated-file guard only skips suffix-recognized generated paths and cannot catch content-minified bundles. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §3 says `isGeneratedFile(path)` runs first in `flushValueRefs`, skips suffix-recognized generated files like `.pb.ts` and `.min.js`, and is path-only so content-minified bundles are outside the guard.

title: Generic bridge built-in matching
text:
# Generic bridge built-in matching

Lifecycle status: accepted

Matching generic built-in bridge names as framework bridge targets is an anti-pattern because it turns ubiquitous platform methods into false cross-language edges. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#2 §8d says NSObject-wide names would bridge to arbitrary project-local ObjC methods as noise, and RNFirebase initially had 78 edges including 60 false positives to `addListener:` / `remove:` before the RCTEventEmitter blocklist cut it to 18 precise edges.

title: Gin agent rabbit-hole collapse
text:
# Gin agent rabbit-hole collapse

Lifecycle status: accepted

Gin middleware-chain synthesis turned prior agent rabbit-holing on `Context.Next` into clean CodeGraph runs, with no Read/Grep/Bash or Workflow calls in the WITH arm. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 reports Gin `callees(Next)` now surfaces Logger, Recovery, ErrorLogger, and handlers with stable node count, and Agent A/B flipped from a codegraph-negative rabbit-hole to clean runs with 38% fewer tool calls.

title: Gin middleware chain tracing
text:
# Gin middleware chain tracing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph connects Go Gin middleware chains end-to-end in trace and explore so following a request reaches middleware and route handlers registered through `.Use()` and `.GET()` rather than dead-ending at framework dispatch. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.8 New Features.

title: Gin middleware-chain synthesis
text:
# Gin middleware-chain synthesis

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph adds `ginMiddlewareChainEdges` to connect Gin's slice-index middleware dispatcher to every named HandlerFunc registered through `.Use`, `.GET`, and related route registration APIs. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 says Gin's `(*Context).Next` dispatches through `c.handlers[c.index](c)`, tree-sitter cannot resolve that slice-index call, and the synthesizer finds the dispatcher and links it to registered named handlers, gated on the dispatcher existing, closures skipped, and capped.

title: GitHub release bundle fallback
text:
# GitHub release bundle fallback

Lifecycle status: accepted

The npm launcher falls back to downloading and caching the platform bundle from GitHub Releases when a registry mirror lacks the matching per-platform package, with `CODEGRAPH_NO_DOWNLOAD=1` and `CODEGRAPH_DOWNLOAD_BASE` controls. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 Fixes.

title: Gitignore-backed indexing
text:
# Gitignore-backed indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph indexes with zero config by honoring `.gitignore` in git repositories via git and in non-git projects by reading `.gitignore` files directly. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.2 New Features says indexing honors `.gitignore` everywhere and `.gitignore` is the way to keep paths out of the graph.

title: Global CLI binary executable bit
text:
# Global CLI binary executable bit

Lifecycle status: accepted

The packaged global `codegraph` CLI binary must ship executable so fresh global installs can run from the shell without manual chmod. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.6 says 0.7.5 shipped the CLI without its executable bit, causing `permission denied`, and 0.7.6 fixed fresh installs.

title: Go cross-file receiver binding
text:
# Go cross-file receiver binding

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph attaches Go methods to their receiver type even when the type and method are declared in different files. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says cross-file methods are no longer orphaned from their struct, and structs with interface-satisfying methods spread across files now link to implemented interfaces.

title: Go cross-package struct creation
text:
# Go cross-package struct creation

Lifecycle status: accepted

Go composite literals and type conversions now link to the package or type being constructed or converted to. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says `render.XML{...}`, `pkga.Widget{...}`, registry literals, and conversions like `(*Wrapped)(x)` now create dependencies, closing the gap for types only constructed elsewhere.

title: Go enclosing declaration caller attribution
text:
# Go enclosing declaration caller attribution

Lifecycle status: accepted

Go calls made inside inline functions, struct method literals, or package-level callback closures are attributed to the enclosing declaration instead of leaking to the file node. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 Go caller attribution bullet says `codegraph_callers` and `codegraph_impact` now surface closures that use the edited function.

title: Go extractor
text:
# Go extractor

Lifecycle status: accepted

The Go extractor is the CodeGraph indexing surface for Go declarations, closure call sites, and caller attribution. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 Go caller attribution bullet.

title: Go gRPC implementation bridging
text:
# Go gRPC implementation bridging

Lifecycle status: accepted

Go gRPC interface stubs connect to their hand-written implementations so callers, callees, impact, and trace land on the real method rather than the empty generated stub. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.7 New Features.

title: Go generic receiver binding
text:
# Go generic receiver binding

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph attaches Go methods declared on generic receiver types to their receiver type. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says methods like `func (s *Stack[T]) Push(...)` now correctly affect callers, callees, and impact.

title: Go group route extraction
text:
# Go group route extraction

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph resolves Go web routes on any route group receiver rather than only `r` or `router`, and gorilla/mux remains covered by any-receiver `HandleFunc`/`Handle` handling. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 marks routes on any group variable such as `v1.GET` and `PublicGroup.GET` done, says this fixed group-routed apps on gin-vue-admin, realworld, and gitness, and confirms gorilla/mux subrouter-var handling while ignoring `.Methods()` chains.

title: Go structural interface implementations
text:
# Go structural interface implementations

Lifecycle status: accepted

Go interfaces now connect to concrete implementations inferred from matching method sets, and calls through an interface reach every implementation. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says Go has no `implements` keyword, so CodeGraph now infers the link and impact flows from interface methods to concrete implementations behind plugin or strategy patterns.

title: GoFrame g.Meta route synthesis
text:
# GoFrame g.Meta route synthesis

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph extracts GoFrame request-type `g.Meta` route tags into route nodes and synthesizes route→controller-method edges by matching the controller method signature's package-qualified request type rather than by method name. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 marks GoFrame `g.Meta` route coverage done via `frameworks/goframe.ts`, requires `path:`, encodes package-qualified request types, joins by method signature, separates identical bare names by `pkg.Type`, and uses an addon-root tiebreak to avoid core/addon cross-links.

title: GoFrame literal-path hunting eliminated
text:
# GoFrame literal-path hunting eliminated

Lifecycle status: accepted

GoFrame route synthesis eliminated agent file-reading and grep-hunting for non-existent literal routes while preserving the same correct call path. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 reports gfast Agent A/B WITH used one `codegraph_explore`, zero Read/Grep, about 20s, and correct, while WITHOUT averaged 7.5 Reads, hunted for non-existent `/dept/add`, reread `sys_dept.go` up to 12 times, and took about 42s.

title: GoFrame request-type signature key
text:
# GoFrame request-type signature key

Lifecycle status: accepted

GoFrame route synthesis must key routes by package-qualified request type and controller method signatures, not by bare request type or method name. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 says `DeptSearchReq` is served by `List`, `GetDictReq` by `GetDictData`, and `pkg.Type` is required to separate many identical bare request names such as `cash.ListReq` and `order.ListReq`.

title: Grammar compilation V8 flag
text:
# Grammar compilation V8 flag

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph launches with a V8 flag that keeps grammar compilation off the optimizing tier, and launch paths that miss the flag re-exec once with it automatically. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.3 Fixes says this prevents Node.js 22/24 `Fatal process out of memory: Zone` crashes on large multi-language projects.

title: Graph fixes still need trace adoption
text:
# Graph fixes still need trace adoption

Lifecycle status: accepted

A correct graph connectivity fix may not reduce agent reads if the agent does not invoke the graph operation that exercises the new edges. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 says the Spring interface/bean/config fixes are correct, but the agent A/B was null because runs went context→explore→Read and never invoked `trace`, so agent-visible read reduction remains adoption-gated.

title: Half-bridged dispatch flow
text:
# Half-bridged dispatch flow

Lifecycle status: accepted

Shipping a dispatch synthesizer that bridges only part of a flow is an anti-pattern because partial coverage is worse than none. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Discipline item 5 says to close each flow end-to-end and never ship a half-bridged flow.

title: Handler-array closure tracing
text:
# Handler-array closure tracing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph traces closure arrays and similar handler-list patterns by connecting closures appended to a collection with the later loop that invokes them, covering Swift deferred validation flows. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.8 New Features.

title: Hermes Agent installer target
text:
# Hermes Agent installer target

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph install` supports Hermes Agent by wiring the CodeGraph MCP server for Hermes like the other supported agents. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.2 New Features says `codegraph install` now supports Hermes Agent (Nous Research).

title: Hermes YAML config preservation
text:
# Hermes YAML config preservation

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph install --target hermes` handles PyYAML block-style lists and reinstalls cleanly even on an already-corrupted `~/.hermes/config.yaml`, instead of corrupting the file. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 Fixes.

title: Heuristic synthesized-edge provenance
text:
# Heuristic synthesized-edge provenance

Lifecycle status: accepted

Synthesized callback edges use `provenance: 'heuristic'` plus metadata such as `synthesizedBy`, `via`, `event`, or `field`, rather than a new provenance enum or confidence tiers. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Provenance notes `Edge.provenance` is a fixed enum and says the designed `callback-synthesis` provenance and confidence tiers were not implemented.

title: High-precision callback synthesis
text:
# High-precision callback synthesis

Lifecycle status: accepted

The shipped synthesis had high precision in validation, adding one correct Excalidraw edge out of 27,214 and only three nodes after named nested extraction. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 TL;DR and Validation report `triggerUpdate -> triggerRender`, `use -> onmount`, one synthesized Excalidraw edge, and nodes 9,286 to 9,289.

title: Home root indexing refusal
text:
# Home root indexing refusal

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph refuses to initialize or index from a home directory or filesystem root unless the user passes `--force`. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says this prevents accidental multi-gigabyte indexes and watcher churn over caches, `Library`, and every other project under the root.

title: Honest full index rebuilds
text:
# Honest full index rebuilds

Lifecycle status: accepted

A full index command must report and produce a complete graph rebuild rather than an empty-looking skipped summary. CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says rerunning `codegraph index` on unchanged projects previously reported `0 nodes, 0 edges` and now clears and re-indexes every time.

title: Human CLI affordances
text:
# Human CLI affordances

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph CLI behavior should match how people guess commands and avoid presenting agent-only internals as commands humans need to run directly. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says `codegraph daemon` provides an interactive daemon manager, `version` aliases all print the installed version, and manual `codegraph serve --mcp` now explains what to run instead and is removed from the command listing.

title: Human-run MCP guidance
text:
# Human-run MCP guidance

Lifecycle status: accepted

When a person runs `codegraph serve --mcp` by hand, CodeGraph explains that agents start it and points to `codegraph status` and `codegraph daemon`; the command is also dropped from the command listing. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says the old behavior hung silently waiting for input and looked broken.

title: Ignore-file parser
text:
# Ignore-file parser

Lifecycle status: accepted

The ignore-file parser is the CodeGraph indexing surface that reads `.gitignore` text and turns patterns into matcher rules during sync/index. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 `.gitignore` invalid UTF-8 and unparseable pattern bullet.

title: Ignored-parent project opening
text:
# Ignored-parent project opening

Lifecycle status: accepted

The shared MCP daemon opens and auto-syncs an indexed project even when an enclosing git repository ignores that project directory. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says the daemon no longer fails with a `path.relative()` error and starts watching as expected, especially visible with Codex on Windows.

title: Impact follows real dependencies
text:
# Impact follows real dependencies

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph impact excludes unrelated sibling methods connected only by the structural `contains` relationship and follows real dependency edges instead. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says asking what a symbol impacts no longer drags in every unrelated sibling method of its class.

title: Implicit framework wiring reachability
text:
# Implicit framework wiring reachability

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph must model framework relationships that are wired by convention or runtime macros rather than explicit imports, so impact and trace reach the real dependent files. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 Rocket routes, SvelteKit load/actions, Nuxt auto-imported components, and React Native event wrapper bullets.

title: In-place upgrade command
text:
# In-place upgrade command

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph upgrade` updates CodeGraph to latest or a specified version in place, detecting standalone, npm, or npx install mode across macOS, Linux, and Windows. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 upgrade bullet.

title: Inactive CodeGraph preserves trust
text:
# Inactive CodeGraph preserves trust

Lifecycle status: accepted

When a workspace lacks a CodeGraph index, agents should see a quiet inactive state and guidance rather than a full toolset that fails on every call. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 quiet-in-unindexed-projects bullet says the old failure mode taught agents to distrust CodeGraph.

title: Inactive no-index MCP mode
text:
# Inactive no-index MCP mode

Lifecycle status: accepted

In workspaces without a CodeGraph index, the MCP server announces itself as inactive, lists no tools, and returns guidance for unindexed target projects instead of tool errors. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 quiet-in-unindexed-projects bullet.

title: Incoming edge preservation on sync
text:
# Incoming edge preservation on sync

Lifecycle status: accepted

Incremental sync preserves incoming cross-file caller and reference edges when re-indexing an edited file. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says edits, including docstring-only edits, no longer make callers disappear until a full re-index; incoming edges are re-matched even when line numbers shift.

title: Incremental callback synthesis
text:
# Incremental callback synthesis

Lifecycle status: proposed

Callback synthesis should run during incremental `resolveAndPersist`, not only full-index `resolveAndPersistBatched`. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work item 2 says incremental re-index will not refresh synthesized edges until this is wired in.

title: Incremental synthesis refresh
text:
# Incremental synthesis refresh

Lifecycle status: proposed

Incremental re-index must refresh synthesized callback edges, not only full-index batched resolution. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work item 2 says synthesis currently runs only in `resolveAndPersistBatched` and should be wired into `resolveAndPersist`.

title: Independent framework resolver commits
text:
# Independent framework resolver commits

Lifecycle status: accepted

Each framework resolver port should be committed independently so any one framework's route extraction can be reverted without rolling back the others. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#3 Task 6 says each framework gets its own commit and marks independent commits as important so regressions can be reverted framework-by-framework.

title: Index artifacts stay out of VCS status
text:
# Index artifacts stay out of VCS status

Lifecycle status: accepted

Generated CodeGraph index artifacts must not appear as untracked or committed project files. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says `.codegraph/` no longer clutters `git status`, and legacy `.codegraph/.gitignore` files are upgraded to stop `daemon.pid` from being committed while customized ignores are left untouched.

title: Index directory resolver
text:
# Index directory resolver

Lifecycle status: accepted

The index directory resolver is the CodeGraph configuration surface that chooses the per-project index directory name, defaulting to `.codegraph` and allowing `CODEGRAPH_DIR` overrides. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features `CODEGRAPH_DIR` bullet.

title: Index-dependent detectors need populated indexes
text:
# Index-dependent detectors need populated indexes

Lifecycle status: accepted

Framework detectors that depend on indexed files must be initialized after extraction, not during CodeGraph construction, or they fail silently across unrelated frameworks. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#2 §8c says the bug affected every framework resolver that read `context.getAllFiles()` / `context.readFile()`, including UIKit, SwiftUI, swift-objc-bridge, and react-native-bridge, and was a pre-existing latent bug rather than bridge-specific.

title: Indexed resolver detection
text:
# Indexed resolver detection

Lifecycle status: accepted

Framework resolver detection must run against the populated CodeGraph index when `detect()` consults `context.getAllFiles()` or `context.readFile()`. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#2 §8c says UIKit, SwiftUI, swift-objc-bridge, and react-native-bridge all returned false during construction-time initialization because no files had been indexed yet.

title: Indexer symlink read allowance
text:
# Indexer symlink read allowance

Lifecycle status: accepted

The indexer's own read path follows in-repo symlinked directories that point outside the project, while file-serving root confinement remains unchanged. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says symlink-discovered files no longer hit `Path traversal blocked in batch reader`, but `../` escape guards and agent file-content protections remain unchanged.

title: Inert repos remain unchanged
text:
# Inert repos remain unchanged

Lifecycle status: accepted

Repos without off-spine ≥3-implementer sibling groups remain at zero skeletons under the refined gate. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 says Excalidraw, Tokio, VS Code, and Gin have byte-identical explore output or 0 skeletons verified by probe.

title: Inherited callback references
text:
# Inherited callback references

Lifecycle status: accepted

Callback registrations now resolve inherited `this.<member>` methods in TS/JS, Java/Kotlin class method references, and Swift bare callback names scoped to the enclosing type. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 callback-registration coverage deepened bullet.

title: Inherited template value refs
text:
# Inherited template value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

Svelte, Vue, and Astro value-reference coverage is inherited through their existing script/frontmatter reparse path rather than implemented as separate language work. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §2b says their extractors re-parse `<script>` or frontmatter as TypeScript/JavaScript in `VALUE_REF_LANGS`, verified that `.svelte` consts edge readers, and no separate matrix row is needed.

title: Inherited this-member resolution
text:
# Inherited this-member resolution

Lifecycle status: accepted

`this.X` inherited members resolve through the supertype pass using a depth-capped BFS over implements/extends after edges persist, sharing the lifecycle of the #750 conformance pass. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits names `resolveDeferredThisMemberRefs` and says getter reads such as `const s = this.snapshot` still produce true dependency references with an imperfect registration flavor.

title: Init leaves project ready
text:
# Init leaves project ready

Lifecycle status: accepted

After `codegraph init`, a project should already have an initial index without requiring users to remember an extra indexing flag. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.8 says `codegraph init` now builds the initial index by default and `-i` remains accepted for compatibility.

title: InitSync options are ignored
text:
# InitSync options are ignored

Lifecycle status: accepted

Do not rely on `CodeGraph.initSync(dir, opts)` include options during value-ref validation: `initSync` takes only the path and default config indexes `.ts`, `.tsx`, and `.js`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#3 §7 lists this as a trap already hit.

title: Initializer call extraction
text:
# Initializer call extraction

Lifecycle status: accepted

TypeScript/JavaScript calls inside top-level variable initializers and inline object-literal methods are extracted so callers includes those call sites, including in Vue single-file components. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 Fixes.

title: Inline named handlers need nodes
text:
# Inline named handlers need nodes

Lifecycle status: accepted

EventEmitter synthesis on real repos needs inline named handlers to be extracted as nodes before they can be linked. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Phase 3 identifies inline `function onmount(){}` handlers not being nodes as the real blocker and says extraction of named nested functions fixed it.

title: Inotify limit partial watch
text:
# Inotify limit partial watch

Lifecycle status: accepted

On Linux inotify exhaustion, CodeGraph reports the exact watch-limit setting and keeps watching the directories it could register. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says it names `fs.inotify.max_user_watches`, gives an example sysctl command, and relies on sync/git hooks for the rest.

title: Install config-only behavior
text:
# Install config-only behavior

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph install` wires agent configuration but does not index the current directory. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says building a project's graph is always explicit via `codegraph init` or `codegraph index`, eliminating divergence between project-local and global install behavior.

title: Install freshness management
text:
# Install freshness management

Lifecycle status: accepted

Users need first-party commands and status signals that keep the CodeGraph binary and project indexes aligned with engine improvements. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 upgrade and status bullets.

title: Install without local Node
text:
# Install without local Node

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph should install and run even on machines with no local Node.js installation. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.0 says CodeGraph ships its own self-contained runtime and installs on any Node version or none; release 0.9.1 fixes standalone installers on machines with no Node installed.

title: Installer marker block cleanup
text:
# Installer marker block cleanup

Lifecycle status: superseded

`codegraph install` and `codegraph uninstall` strip duplicate CodeGraph instruction blocks from agent instruction files and remove the entire `CODEGRAPH_START`/`CODEGRAPH_END` marked block left by older versions. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.7 New Features.

title: Instance-chain preservation
text:
# Instance-chain preservation

Lifecycle status: accepted

Per-language extraction gates must keep instance chains bare so existing resolution is not regressed; only capitalized-receiver or factory chains should be re-encoded. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 says a per-language gate keeps `list.map().filter()` bare and Edge cases says the gate keeps instance chains bare so existing resolution is never regressed.

title: Instant MCP handshake
text:
# Instant MCP handshake

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph answers the MCP opening handshake immediately instead of blocking while the index loads, so the first tool call in a new session reliably goes through CodeGraph rather than racing warmup and falling back to grep/read. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.8 Fixes.

title: Instant static tools list
text:
# Instant static tools list

Lifecycle status: superseded

CodeGraph should answer MCP `tools/list` locally and instantly from static tool definitions, mark tools exposed, and resolve the daemon in the background for real tool calls. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 ranks this as the biggest shippable P2 win and says to use `getStaticTools` locally rather than waiting on daemon connect if that is the current behavior.

title: Interactive daemon manager
text:
# Interactive daemon manager

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph ships `codegraph daemon` with alias `daemons` as an interactive manager for background daemons, showing the current project first and allowing stop-one or stop-all. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says this replaces hunting for a pid and killing it by hand.

title: JSX route file indexing
text:
# JSX route file indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

React Router and Next.js routes defined in `.tsx` and `.jsx` files are indexed. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says JSX route declarations, `createBrowserRouter`, and Next.js `app/` or `pages/` files now show in search/explore and connect to the component they render.

title: JSX-scoped component resolution
text:
# JSX-scoped component resolution

Lifecycle status: accepted

PascalCase component resolution now applies only from JSX-capable files, and Svelte/Vue component resolution uses same-directory or otherwise unambiguous candidates instead of arbitrary same-named files. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 TypeScript/React/Svelte/Vue bullet.

title: JVM and CSharp const-field kind switch
text:
# JVM and CSharp const-field kind switch

Lifecycle status: accepted

Java and C# value-reference support emits only shared const-like fields as `constant` while leaving instance `final` and `readonly` fields as `field`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says Java `static final` and C# `const`/`static readonly` use an `isConst` predicate plus `extractField` kind switch, while instance final/readonly fields stay `field`.

title: JVM qualified member ungated refs
text:
# JVM qualified member ungated refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

Qualified `Type::member` candidates in Java and Kotlin skip the name gate while staying scope-suffix-anchored and unique-or-drop, because same-package references and Kotlin companions often need no import and explicit reference syntax is self-selecting. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits says `Type::method` resolves cross-file, qualified candidates skip the name gate, decoys do not match unrelated refs, and companion members extract transparently.

title: JVM variable method-ref silence
text:
# JVM variable method-ref silence

Lifecycle status: accepted

Java and Kotlin method references through variables such as `subscriber::onNext` or `m::run0` deliberately emit no edge because the receiver type is statically unknown and prior bare capture produced wrong same-file matches. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits says the qualified rework drops variable receiver method refs after RxJava baseline bare capture misresolved them.

title: Java annotation dependency edges
text:
# Java annotation dependency edges

Lifecycle status: accepted

Java annotation definitions are indexed as types and annotation usages on classes, methods, and fields now depend on them. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says `@interface` types and `@Foo` modifiers were previously uncaptured, so Spring, JPA, and Gson annotation-driven code showed no users or dependency edges.

title: Java annotation range fact
text:
# Java annotation range fact

Lifecycle status: accepted

Java method node ranges include leading annotations, so Spring listener annotation gates must scan downward from the node start line across consecutive annotation lines rather than looking above the method declaration. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Spring events row calls this a key Java fact and says `startLine` is the first annotation line.

title: Kiro installer target
text:
# Kiro installer target

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph install` supports Kiro CLI and IDE on macOS, Linux, and Windows, with its own steering file so Kiro loads CodeGraph guidance naturally. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 New Features.

title: Kotlin Spring route support
text:
# Kotlin Spring route support

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph extends Spring route resolution to Kotlin files and Kotlin `fun name(` handler syntax while preserving Java Spring behavior. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 says the Spring resolver had been Java-only with a Java method regex, was extended to `.kt` plus Kotlin `fun name(` matching, validates petclinic-kotlin 0→18 and 18/18, resolves DI controller→repo, and leaves Java Spring unchanged at realworld 19/19.

title: Kotlin companion fixture trap
text:
# Kotlin companion fixture trap

Lifecycle status: accepted

Do not chase a single-line Kotlin `class X { companion object { ... } }` companion-method failure as a product bug, because it is an upstream tree-sitter-kotlin ERROR-node misparse seen only in the probe fixture. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits says real multi-line companion code extracts transparently and the single-line form only appeared in the probe fixture.

title: Kotlin expect actual links
text:
# Kotlin expect actual links

Lifecycle status: accepted

Kotlin Multiplatform `actual` declarations now link to the common `expect` declaration they fulfill, including `actual typealias` for an `expect class`. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says platform actuals previously looked dependency-free because common callers resolved only to `expect`, and changing an actual now surfaces the common API and its users.

title: Kotlin property-declaration value refs
text:
# Kotlin property-declaration value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

Kotlin value-reference support extracts `property_declaration` names, classifies top-level/object/companion properties as constant or variable and class properties as fields, scans `simple_identifier` reads, and prunes property shadowing. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says Kotlin combined the C nested-name fix, Scala enclosing-scope rule, PHP reader-scan move, and shadow-prune property declaration wiring.

title: Language dependency extractors
text:
# Language dependency extractors

Lifecycle status: accepted

The language dependency extractors are the CodeGraph indexing and resolution surfaces that emit dependency edges from language-specific constructs across Lua/Luau, Swift, Java, Kotlin, Scala, PHP, Objective-C, Dart, C++, Ruby, C#, Go, Python, and TypeScript/JavaScript. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 enumerates per-language impact and affected fixes for those constructs.

title: Language import resolver
text:
# Language import resolver

Lifecycle status: accepted

The language import resolver is the CodeGraph resolution surface that maps import/include/reference syntax to the correct file or symbol within language, platform, and source-set boundaries. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 TypeScript/native same-name, C/C++ quoted include, and Kotlin Multiplatform import bullets.

title: Language-gated framework extraction dispatch
text:
# Language-gated framework extraction dispatch

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph calls `extract()` inside the extraction pipeline for each framework whose declared `languages` include the current file's language. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#4 Fix says `extract()` is called inside the extraction pipeline for every framework whose `languages` include the file language.

title: Laravel controller route resolver
text:
# Laravel controller route resolver

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph resolves Laravel `Route::get([Ctrl::class,'m'])`, `'Ctrl@m'`, and `Route::resource` declarations to the precise controller method instead of matching bare method names to the wrong controller. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks PHP Laravel done and notes the previous bug where every `index` resolved to ArticleController.

title: Laravel dual registration sources
text:
# Laravel dual registration sources

Lifecycle status: accepted

Laravel event synthesis needs both typed `handle(EventType $e)` declarations and the EventServiceProvider `$listen` map because real repositories use both and untyped listener handles can only be linked through `$listen`. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Laravel events row says both mechanisms are real and needed, with koel's untyped `PruneLibrary` linked only via `$listen`.

title: Laravel event deferred forms
text:
# Laravel event deferred forms

Lifecycle status: accepted

Laravel event synthesis v1 intentionally leaves static-trait `XEvent::dispatch()`, `Event::listen(closure)`, framework-event string-literal `$listen` keys that are never `event(new)` dispatched, and event simple-name namespace collisions for later work. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Laravel events row lists those forms under Deferred.

title: Laravel event synthesizer
text:
# Laravel event synthesizer

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph shipped `laravelEventEdges` for Laravel events by combining typed listener `handle(EventType $e)` declarations with the EventServiceProvider `$listen` map, then linking `event(new XEvent(...))` call sites to matching listener handles. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Laravel events row marks it shipped on 2026-06-21 with 100% precision on koel and firefly-iii plus zero edges on guzzle.

title: Laravel event-call gate
text:
# Laravel event-call gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

Laravel event synthesis must match only `event(new XEvent(...))` call sites, which excludes queued job dispatch by construction and avoids job-vs-event ambiguity. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Laravel events row says job exclusion is free because jobs use `::dispatch()` or `dispatch()` and matching only `event(new X)` excludes them.

title: Laravel fluent handler frontier
text:
# Laravel fluent handler frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph still needs Laravel route handler parsing for fluent `->uses()` and `['uses'=>...]` forms. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 says firefly resolves only 3 of 568 Laravel routes because those handler formats are not parsed.

title: Large repo indexing completes
text:
# Large repo indexing completes

Lifecycle status: accepted

Indexing must complete on large multi-language projects under supported Node runtimes instead of aborting during grammar compilation. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.3 says large multi-language indexing no longer aborts with a V8 `Fatal process out of memory: Zone` crash on Node.js 22 and 24.

title: Layer-balanced explore retrieval
text:
# Layer-balanced explore retrieval

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_explore` should return the implementation file that genuinely matches a backend-flow question even when a larger, denser frontend layer uses the same domain words. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#10 says API-server files in admin-UI-over-API projects were previously pushed out by the more interconnected frontend layer, and backend-flow questions should return the service or handler that does the work.

title: Lean MCP context budget
text:
# Lean MCP context budget

Lifecycle status: accepted
