A four-tool default MCP surface saves context tokens every session and steers agents toward the right tool by presence alone. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 focused MCP default bullet.

title: Legacy index ignore migration
text:
# Legacy index ignore migration

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph upgrades old generated `.codegraph/.gitignore` files in place when any CodeGraph command runs, while leaving user-customized ignore files untouched. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says older ignores that listed only database, cache, and logs are upgraded to stop `daemon.pid` from being committed.

title: Line-numbered source surfaces
text:
# Line-numbered source surfaces

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_node` and `codegraph_trace` emit line-numbered source so agents can cite or edit exact lines without re-reading files to recover line numbers. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 New Features.

title: Literal native bridge keys
text:
# Literal native bridge keys

Lifecycle status: proposed

Native bridge resolution should only resolve literal bridge keys; dynamic or computed forms such as `NativeModules[someVar]` and `requireNativeModule(name)` where `name` is a parameter remain out of scope. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §7 lists dynamic/computed bridge keys as an anti-goal and says only literal-key access is resolved, matching the dynamic-dispatch Lua frontier.

title: Local fallback after daemon restart
text:
# Local fallback after daemon restart

Lifecycle status: accepted

When the shared background server restarts under an active session, CodeGraph keeps the session working by serving it locally instead of letting requests hang or the connection die silently. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 daemon restart fallback bullet.

title: Local-first privacy promise
text:
# Local-first privacy promise

Lifecycle status: accepted

Telemetry must preserve and make provable CodeGraph's local-first promise that user code never leaves the machine. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 says telemetry has to keep the pitch "your code never leaves your machine" true and provable.

title: Lombok explicit-source guard
text:
# Lombok explicit-source guard

Lifecycle status: accepted

Lombok-generated member indexing must not override methods explicitly written by the user, must not synthesize accessors for static fields, and must leave non-Lombok classes unaffected. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#9 Lombok bullet states those precision guards while saying generated members are marked as Lombok-generated rather than hand-written.

title: Lombok generated member indexing
text:
# Lombok generated member indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph indexes Java members generated by Lombok annotations as real generated symbols, including getters, setters, builder methods, equals/hashCode/toString, and the `@Slf4j` `log` field. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#9 Lombok bullet says these members now appear in `codegraph search`, `codegraph_explore`, and `codegraph_node`, and callers trace through them like hand-written methods while being marked Lombok-generated.

title: Lombok generated member reachability
text:
# Lombok generated member reachability

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph should make Lombok-generated Java members reachable in search and flow exploration even though those members do not appear in source. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#9 Lombok bullet says calls like `user.getName()`, `User.builder()`, and `log.info(...)` used to resolve to nothing and break call-chain analysis.

title: Low-value ranking for sizing
text:
# Low-value ranking for sizing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Demoting or ranking low-value files is an ineffective way to shrink adaptive explore output because the budget is refilled with other full bodies. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Dead ends item 1 says broadening `isLowValuePath` barely changed size, from 28,478 to 28,424, and concludes ranking is not shrinking.

title: Lua extractor
text:
# Lua extractor

Lifecycle status: accepted

The Lua/Luau extractor is the CodeGraph indexing surface for `require` calls and module-file resolution. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 Lua and Luau require bullet.

title: Lua language indexing
text:
# Lua language indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph indexes `.lua` projects, including functions, table methods, local variables, `require(...)` imports, and call edges. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.0 New Features says Lua indexing covers Neovim plugins, Kong, OpenResty, and game code with those extracted facts.

title: Lua module dispatch coverage
text:
# Lua module dispatch coverage

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph treats Lua/Luau dominant module dispatch as already covered by general import and name resolution after measurement, with no code change. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 says Neovim module-heavy `require('x')` plus `x.fn()` flows already work, telescope.nvim has 220 imports and 335 cross-file `mod.fn` calls, and Luau instance-path require is handled by the extractor.

title: Lua require module-file links
text:
# Lua require module-file links

Lifecycle status: accepted

Lua and Luau `require` calls link dotted module paths and Roblox instance-path requires to their module files. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 Lua and Luau require bullet.

title: Lua reverse require dependents
text:
# Lua reverse require dependents

Lifecycle status: accepted

Lua and Luau `require` edges now let an edited module surface every file that requires it. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says requires previously resolved to nothing, so a Lua/Luau module looked like it had no dependents, and now editing a module surfaces every requiring file.

title: Lua value-ref backlog
text:
# Lua value-ref backlog

Lifecycle status: deprecated

Lua and Luau value-reference support remains a proposed extension for file/chunk `local X =` and global assignments, but must be classified before implementation because distinctive uppercase-name gating catches fewer Lua constants. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §2b lists Lua/Luau under remaining likely easy path, with file/chunk locals and globals and a note that casing varies.

title: Lua value-ref backlog
text:
# Lua value-ref backlog

Lifecycle status: superseded

Lua and Luau value-reference support remains a proposed extension for file/chunk `local X =` and global assignments, but must be classified before implementation because distinctive uppercase-name gating catches fewer Lua constants. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §2b lists Lua/Luau under remaining likely easy path, with file/chunk locals and globals and a note that casing varies.

title: Lua/Luau value-ref backlog
text:
# Lua/Luau value-ref backlog

Lifecycle status: proposed

Lua and Luau value-reference support remains a proposed extension for file/chunk `local X =` and global assignments, but must be classified before implementation because distinctive uppercase-name gating catches fewer Lua constants. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §2b lists Lua/Luau under remaining likely easy path, with file/chunk locals and globals and a note that casing varies.

title: Luau language indexing
text:
# Luau language indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph indexes `.luau` projects with Luau-specific typed features: type aliases, `export type` aliases, typed function signatures, generics, and Roblox instance-path requires, on top of Lua extraction. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.0 New Features describes this Luau support.

title: MCP bold label rendering
text:
# MCP bold label rendering

Lifecycle status: accepted

MCP tool results use bold labels instead of Markdown headings for internal section structure. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says status summaries, search hits, and exploration file sections no longer render as oversized headings in Markdown clients, while terminal/CLI output is unchanged.

title: MCP clientInfo telemetry plumbing
text:
# MCP clientInfo telemetry plumbing

Lifecycle status: superseded

Usage rollups should include MCP `client_name` and `client_version` from the initialize handshake, but the plumbing to read `src/mcp/session.ts` `case 'initialize'` is still to add. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Events `usage_rollup` description.

title: MCP connect catch-up
text:
# MCP connect catch-up

Lifecycle status: accepted

The MCP server reconciles changes that happened while it was not running before serving the first query. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 Fixes says the first query now reflects current code instead of a stale snapshot.

title: MCP fatal-error exit
text:
# MCP fatal-error exit

Lifecycle status: accepted

The CodeGraph MCP server logs unexpected internal errors and exits cleanly instead of remaining in a broken 100% CPU state. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says a fresh server starts on the next request after such an error.

title: MCP guidance single source
text:
# MCP guidance single source

Lifecycle status: superseded

CodeGraph guidance for agents should come from the MCP server rather than duplicated installer-written instruction blocks in each agent's local instruction file. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.7 says the MCP server is now the single source of truth and duplicate `## CodeGraph` instruction blocks are stripped on install/uninstall.

title: MCP input failure triggers shutdown
text:
# MCP input failure triggers shutdown

Lifecycle status: accepted

The stdio MCP server treats any input stream failure as a disconnect and tears the stream down so an orphaned server exits promptly. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 abrupt editor/agent connection drop bullet.

title: MCP process self-recovery
text:
# MCP process self-recovery

Lifecycle status: accepted

The CodeGraph MCP server must recover from lockups and unexpected internal errors without leaving users to kill a wedged process by hand. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says a watchdog stops the server when the main thread stops responding, and internal errors now log and exit cleanly so a fresh server starts on the next request.

title: MCP startup path
text:
# MCP startup path

Lifecycle status: accepted

The `serve --mcp` startup path spans the proxy, detached daemon, and runtime flag relaunch modules that determine when CodeGraph tools become visible to the host. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 lists `src/mcp/proxy.ts`, `src/mcp/index.ts`, `src/mcp/daemon.ts`, and `src/extraction/wasm-runtime-flags.ts` as startup, daemon, proxy, and runtime flag pointers.

title: MCP timeout is not exposure timing
text:
# MCP timeout is not exposure timing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Increasing `MCP_TIMEOUT` does not fix startup pending when the failure is delayed tool exposure rather than a connection timeout. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says `MCP_TIMEOUT` did not help because the problem is tool exposure timing, not a connection timeout.

title: MCP tool subset env var
text:
# MCP tool subset env var

Lifecycle status: superseded

`CODEGRAPH_MCP_TOOLS` lets users expose only a chosen subset of CodeGraph tools over MCP without editing client config; unset exposes all tools. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 New Features.

title: MCP tool-surface scoping
text:
# MCP tool-surface scoping

Lifecycle status: accepted

Users need to expose only a selected subset of CodeGraph MCP tools without editing each client's MCP configuration. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 introduces `CODEGRAPH_MCP_TOOLS` with examples such as `trace,search,node,context`.

title: MCP watchdog shutdown
text:
# MCP watchdog shutdown

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph's MCP server runs a lightweight watchdog that stops the process if the main thread locks up, with `CODEGRAPH_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_MS` to tune and `CODEGRAPH_NO_WATCHDOG=1` to disable. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says it can no longer sit pinned at 100% CPU with no way to recover.

title: Manual prewarm is not general
text:
# Manual prewarm is not general

Lifecycle status: accepted

Manual daemon prewarming cannot be the general solution for real users, even though it removes bind latency in evals. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says prewarming a daemon is proven in `ab-new-vs-baseline.sh`, but a real user cannot pre-warm.

title: Manual sync after watcher distrust
text:
# Manual sync after watcher distrust

Lifecycle status: accepted

When live watching cannot be trusted, users must rely on `codegraph sync` or git sync hooks until auto-sync is restored. CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says CodeGraph disables auto-sync once with a clear message instead of retrying forever or serving a stale index as healthy.

title: Markdown client transcript readability
text:
# Markdown client transcript readability

Lifecycle status: accepted

MCP tool results must render with normal-size structure in Markdown clients. CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says headings in tools like `codegraph_search` and `codegraph_explore` filled transcripts with large-font noise, so section headers are now bold labels while preserving structure.

title: Marker-fenced agent instructions
text:
# Marker-fenced agent instructions

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph install` writes a small marker-fenced CodeGraph section into CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and GEMINI.md that points agents at both CLI and MCP surfaces; it preserves user content, upgrades from the old long block, and uninstall removes it. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 subagents bullet.

title: Measure before assuming holes
text:
# Measure before assuming holes

Lifecycle status: accepted

Measure framework usage before assuming a dynamic-dispatch hole; Svelte's presumed event-handler gap was not the real gap because modern Svelte often uses form actions and callback props instead of `on:click={fn}`. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 explicitly states this lesson in the Svelte/SvelteKit row.

title: MediatR deferred forms
text:
# MediatR deferred forms

Lifecycle status: accepted

MediatR synthesis v1 intentionally leaves generic collection-domain-event publish, record-positional or factory-built arguments, and `ICommandHandler<T>` facade indirection for later work. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 MediatR / CQRS row lists those forms under Deferred.

title: MediatR dispatch synthesizer
text:
# MediatR dispatch synthesizer

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph shipped `mediatrDispatchEdges` for MediatR/CQRS by mapping `_mediator.Send` and `.Publish` calls to matching `IRequestHandler` or `INotificationHandler` `Handle` methods through type-keyed two-pass synthesis. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 MediatR / CQRS row marks it shipped on 2026-06-20 with 100% precision on CleanArchitecture and eShop plus zero edges on Newtonsoft.Json.

title: MediatR handler-map gate
text:
# MediatR handler-map gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

MediatR synthesis must only bridge calls whose receiver is mediator-like and whose resolved request type exists in the handler map. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 MediatR row lists these two precision gates and says they exclude MAUI `MessagingCenter.Send`, `HttpClient.Send`, and same-named DTO collisions without handlers.

title: MediatR variable-passed idiom
text:
# MediatR variable-passed idiom

Lifecycle status: accepted

The dominant .NET MediatR call shape is variable-passed rather than inline construction, so dispatch synthesis must resolve `mediator.Send(command)` through local construction and declared parameter/local types. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 says eShop had zero genuine inline `Send(new X)` calls and every send was `mediator.Send(command)`.

title: Member-name overlap ambiguity
text:
# Member-name overlap ambiguity

Lifecycle status: accepted

Same-file value-reference matching accepts a bounded residual ambiguity when a shared constant name overlaps with a method, class, or sibling companion/type name in Scala/Kotlin/Swift. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#2 says Scala's interchangeable `val`/`def` members and Kotlin's val/def-or-class name overlap cannot be distinguished by same-file name matching, and Swift shares the sibling-type name-overlap bound; investigated collisions were bounded and sampled reads were genuine.

title: Mirror-lag install resilience
text:
# Mirror-lag install resilience

Lifecycle status: accepted

Installing CodeGraph should succeed even when a registry mirror has not yet mirrored the matching per-platform package, with an explicit way to disable or redirect fallback downloads. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 says the launcher downloads missing bundles from GitHub Releases, caches them, supports `CODEGRAPH_NO_DOWNLOAD=1`, and allows `CODEGRAPH_DOWNLOAD_BASE`.

title: Mixed iOS bridge closure
text:
# Mixed iOS bridge closure

Lifecycle status: proposed

Mixed iOS bridge coverage must close both Swift-to-Objective-C and Objective-C-to-Swift directions, including methods, properties, initializers, and protocols, before measuring or shipping the flow. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#0 §1 says for mixed iOS both directions and all bridged kinds must close before measuring.

title: Mixed native bridge rollout shipped
text:
# Mixed native bridge rollout shipped

Lifecycle status: accepted

Mixed iOS, React Native, and Expo projects trace end-to-end across Swift-Objective-C auto-bridging, React Native legacy bridge and TurboModules, native-to-JS event channels, Expo Modules, and Fabric/Codegen view components. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 New Features says all of these bridges connect flows through gaps static parsing alone cannot follow.

title: Module-qualified symbol lookup
text:
# Module-qualified symbol lookup

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph tool lookups resolve module-qualified names such as `module::symbol`, `Module.symbol`, and `module/symbol`, including multi-level paths and Rust `crate`, `super`, and `self` prefixes. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.10 Fixes states these lookup forms now resolve in codegraph tools.

title: Multi-agent install prompt
text:
# Multi-agent install prompt

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph install` ships a multi-select agent picker that can configure Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, and opencode in one run, with detected agents pre-selected. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.7 New Features says the command sets up those agents from one multi-select prompt with detected agents pre-checked.

title: Multi-agent uninstall command
text:
# Multi-agent uninstall command

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph ships `codegraph uninstall` to remove CodeGraph setup from Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, opencode, and Hermes Agent in one step, with global/local config selection and scripted flags. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.3 New Features.

title: Multi-repository workspace coverage
text:
# Multi-repository workspace coverage

Lifecycle status: accepted

A workspace root containing several independent git repositories should index as one graph so explore, impact, callers, sync, and live watching cover every nested project. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features multi-repository workspace bullet.

title: Multi-repository workspace indexing
text:
# Multi-repository workspace indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Running `codegraph init` at a directory root containing several independent git repositories now indexes every nested project into one graph, and sync/live watching pick up child-repo changes. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features multi-repository workspace bullet.

title: Multi-term explore retention
text:
# Multi-term explore retention

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_explore` keeps a file in the answer when it is corroborated by two or more distinct query terms, preventing a larger unrelated layer from crowding it out. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#10 says backend-flow queries in repos with an API server and large frontend now preserve the server-side file that matches several query terms.

title: Multilanguage interface implementation links
text:
# Multilanguage interface implementation links

Lifecycle status: accepted

Interface-to-implementation linking works for C#, TypeScript, JavaScript, Swift, and Scala, extending the previously Java/Kotlin-only coverage so interface method investigation surfaces concrete implementations. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.7 New Features.

title: MyBatis XML mapper extraction
text:
# MyBatis XML mapper extraction

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph treats MyBatis XML mappers as a first-class extracted language and synthesizes Java DAO method edges to matching XML SQL statement nodes. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 marks XML mapper extraction done via `src/extraction/mybatis-extractor.ts`, emits method-shaped nodes for mapper statements, `<sql>` fragments and `<include>` references, uses `mybatisJavaXmlEdges` to join Java methods to XML qualified names by suffix-match, drops ambiguous simple-name collisions, and connects full controller→service→impl→mapper→XML traces.

title: MyBatis cross-module include frontier
text:
# MyBatis cross-module include frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph still needs fuller cross-module MyBatis XML include coverage when mapper fragments are referenced across files without the dotted namespace form. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 lists cross-module XML statement references as a coverage frontier and notes they work when the include uses the dotted namespace form.

title: Name-keyed supertype union
text:
# Name-keyed supertype union

Lifecycle status: accepted

Looking up supertypes by class name alone is an anti-pattern because common class names can union unrelated parents and create cross-class wrong edges. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits says name-keyed `getSupertypes('Engine')` unioned every Rails `Engine` parent and produced a wrong edge, while the node-anchored walk eliminated it.

title: Named descriptor resolver pattern
text:
# Named descriptor resolver pattern

Lifecycle status: accepted

Named attribute or descriptor dynamic calls should be handled by a framework resolver using `claimsReference` and `resolve()` when a named reference exists. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 2 says a named ref such as `_iterable_class` goes to a resolver, and section 3a says `djangoResolver` claims and resolves `_iterable_class` to `ModelIterable.__iter__`.

title: Named nested function extraction
text:
# Named nested function extraction

Lifecycle status: accepted

The extractor now creates nodes for named nested functions so inline named handlers can be linked by callback synthesis. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Phase 3 says `visitFunctionBody` previously walked through nested functions without extracting them, and the fix extracts nested functions when `extractName` returns a real name.

title: Named spare requires uniqueness
text:
# Named spare requires uniqueness

Lifecycle status: accepted

A named callable should spare a file only when the name is unique or near-unique, because common method names across many variants would otherwise keep too many files full. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 Further refinement item 1 says `as_sql` has 110 definitions and naming it must not keep every backend variant full, while unique `getResponseWithInterceptorChain` still spares RealCall.

title: Named-callable spare with family override
text:
# Named-callable spare with family override

Lifecycle status: accepted

The refined gate keeps files full when the agent named a callable in them unless the file itself defines a ≥3-implementation supertype, in which case it skeletonizes anyway. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 Refinement describes sparing RealCall but skeletonizing Django `compiler.py` because it defines `SQLCompiler`.

title: Named-cluster survival
text:
# Named-cluster survival

Lifecycle status: accepted

Non-sibling files inject agent-named method definitions into clusters, rank them at high importance, and cap cluster selection by per-file and remaining-total budget so named clusters survive trimming. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 Further refinement item 4 describes preserving Django `_fetch_all` rather than source-order trimming it.

title: Named-handler synthesis guard
text:
# Named-handler synthesis guard

Lifecycle status: accepted

Callback synthesis deliberately links named handlers and does not extract anonymous arrows as standalone nodes, using named-only handlers as a precision and node-count guard. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Provenance and Phase 3 say named-only handlers are part of the precision guards and anonymous arrows fall through to existing recursion.

title: Native bridge dynamic frontier
text:
# Native bridge dynamic frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph native-bridge coverage remains limited around nonliteral or generated bridge forms: Swift generics over ObjC protocols, Swift extensions on ObjC classes, React Native dynamic module keys, TurboModule native impl classes without legacy macros, Expo trailing-closure bodies, and Fabric event-handler props. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 lists these as hole-identified frontiers across Swift/ObjC, RN legacy, TurboModules, Expo Modules, and Fabric/Paper rows.

title: Native bridge phased rollout
text:
# Native bridge phased rollout

Lifecycle status: superseded

Native bridge implementation should proceed in a fixed sequence: Swift-Objective-C first, React Native legacy bridge second, native-to-JS events third, Expo Modules fourth, TurboModules fifth, and Fabric view components last. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §6 says the order is fixed by the difficulty gradient and by what closes a flow end-to-end on the smallest repo first.

title: Native bridge validation bar
text:
# Native bridge validation bar

Lifecycle status: proposed

Native bridge validation must combine pure-language regression probes, cross-language trace probes, real-agent A/B with at least two runs per arm, Read=0 within the explore-call budget, no pure-control regression, and no node-count explosion. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §5a-§5b define these bars for mixed iOS and React Native, including `select count(*) from nodes` before/after and pure-Swift, pure-ObjC, and pure-JS controls.

title: Native bridge validation corpus
text:
# Native bridge validation corpus

Lifecycle status: proposed

Native bridge work should be validated on real small, medium, and large mixed iOS and React Native repositories plus a narrower Expo corpus, each with canonical cross-bridge flows. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §5 lists candidate small/medium/large repos for mixed iOS and React Native, two Expo scopes, and says the implementation PR confirms choices after verifying each repo still builds an index cleanly.

title: Native build step removed
text:
# Native build step removed

Lifecycle status: accepted

The self-contained runtime removes the native build step entirely for normal installation. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.0 says real SQLite built into the bundled runtime removes the native build step entirely.

title: Native static reads stay in family
text:
# Native static reads stay in family

Lifecycle status: accepted

Native `Type.member` static reads no longer link to coincidentally same-named classes in another language family, while genuine cross-language bridges remain enabled. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 `BatteryManager.EXTRA_LEVEL` bullet.

title: Natural Read replacement
text:
# Natural Read replacement

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph file view must behave enough like `Read` that agents reach for it naturally instead of falling back to `Read`. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 states the fix was to make `codegraph_node` read a file exactly like the Read tool, only faster, so the agent reaches for it naturally.

title: Necessary-file explore exemption
text:
# Necessary-file explore exemption

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph exempts necessary named/spine files from the 90%-budget early break and total cap, then uses a 1.5x final ceiling so `codegraph_explore` renders the sequential flow it assembled instead of slicing required content. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 coverage matrix says NAMED token defs, symbol-defining files, named/spine exemptions, and a 1.5x ceiling let Alamofire render build+validators-exec+validate in one explore while Excalidraw stayed at 0 reads.

title: NestJS RouterModule prefix propagation
text:
# NestJS RouterModule prefix propagation

Lifecycle status: accepted

NestJS route prefixes from `RouterModule.register([...])`, including nested `children`, propagate to controller routes so route labels include full paths such as `GET /admin/users`. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 Fixes.

title: NestJS route extraction
text:
# NestJS route extraction

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph recognizes NestJS projects from `@nestjs/*` dependencies and surfaces the route binding for HTTP controllers, GraphQL resolvers, microservice handlers, and WebSocket gateways. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.8.0 New Features describes automatic NestJS detection and those handler families.

title: Nested repository ignore boundaries
text:
# Nested repository ignore boundaries

Lifecycle status: accepted

When CodeGraph indexes a multi-repository workspace, each child repository's own `.gitignore` must be respected even when the parent repo ignores child repos to keep `git status` quiet. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features multi-repository workspace bullet.

title: NgRx effects synthesizer backlog
text:
# NgRx effects synthesizer backlog

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph should add an NgRx effects synthesizer that bridges action class/type dispatches to createEffect handlers through ofType. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Tier A lists NgRx effects as not started, with createEffect, actions.pipe(ofType(LoginAction)), and Store.dispatch(new LoginAction()) as the static anchors.

title: No JVM extractor redesign
text:
# No JVM extractor redesign

Lifecycle status: proposed

React Native bridge work should use the Kotlin and Java extraction quality already available and only allow tiny refinements for missing `@ReactMethod` literal names, not a redesign of JVM extraction. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §7 marks Android Kotlin/Java extraction quality out of scope and narrows allowable work to tiny extractor refinement for annotation literal names.

title: No codegraph-pro telemetry
text:
# No codegraph-pro telemetry

Lifecycle status: accepted

The private codegraph-pro fork must keep telemetry default-off and not enableable by the installer; customer containers also set CODEGRAPH_TELEMETRY=0 and the rule must survive upstream merges. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 codegraph-pro rule.

title: No dependency route wiring
text:
# No dependency route wiring

Lifecycle status: accepted

Framework resolver extraction wiring must use the existing TypeScript, vitest, tree-sitter, and better-sqlite3 stack without adding new dependencies. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#0 Tech Stack states `No new dependencies`.

title: No explosion dispatch validation
text:
# No explosion dispatch validation

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dynamic-dispatch coverage changes must keep node count stable, avoid regressions on a control repo, and spot-check synthesized or resolved edges for precise targets before being considered successful. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 Step 5 and Success criteria require no node explosion, no control-repo regression, and precise spot-checked synthesized edges.

title: No identity-derived telemetry
text:
# No identity-derived telemetry

Lifecycle status: accepted

Telemetry must not store IP addresses or hardware fingerprints; the machine ID is a random UUID rather than a hardware-derived identifier. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Non-goals / never collected and Events sections.

title: No lingering extractNodes hooks
text:
# No lingering extractNodes hooks

Lifecycle status: accepted

After the framework extraction migration, `extractNodes` references must be eliminated from `src/` and tests so the old dead hook cannot remain as a parallel API. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#3 Task 8 Step 1 requires grepping `extractNodes` across `src/` and `__tests__/` and expects zero matches.

title: No phantom symbols in impact
text:
# No phantom symbols in impact

Lifecycle status: accepted

Impact and caller analysis must not include symbols created only by parser misclassification. CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says C++ export-macro class declarations were mis-indexed as phantom `function` nodes that became false callers and skewed symbol counts.

title: No project-content telemetry
text:
# No project-content telemetry

Lifecycle status: accepted

Telemetry must never collect source code, file paths, file names, repository names, symbol names, query strings, search terms, or anything derived from indexed project contents. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Non-goals / never collected.

title: No-read flow answers
text:
# No-read flow answers

Lifecycle status: accepted

A successful framework coverage pass should let an agent answer the canonical flow question with Read 0 in at least some runs and include the glue symbols that previously required reading. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 Success criteria require Read 0 to be achievable and the glue symbols to appear in the answer.

title: Node 25 remains blocked
text:
# Node 25 remains blocked

Lifecycle status: accepted

Node 25 must remain blocked for CodeGraph until its variant of the grammar compilation crash is fixed by a suitable mitigation. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.3 says Node 25 stays blocked because the V8 flag does not fix that variant of the bug.

title: Node-anchored supertype pass
text:
# Node-anchored supertype pass

Lifecycle status: accepted

The supertype pass walks from the concrete file-anchored class node through implements/extends targets to `contains`-anchored members instead of unioning parents by class name. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits says name-keyed `getSupertypes('Engine')` unioned every Rails `Engine` parent and produced a wrong cross-class edge, while the node walk reduced rails edges from +440 to +385 with all sampled edges genuine.

title: Non-call dependency reachability
text:
# Non-call dependency reachability

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph must record dependency edges for language constructs that are not ordinary calls or imports when those constructs determine who depends on a file or symbol. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 repeatedly says modules, templates, annotations, property wrappers, type signatures, mixins, form resources, enum/static values, and framework includes previously made edited files look like they had no dependents, and now surface their real blast radius.

title: Non-callable synth hop surfacing
text:
# Non-callable synth hop surfacing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Explore now feeds named CONSTANT, VARIABLE, and FIELD nodes that participate in heuristic edges into the Dynamic-dispatch links scan and renders a generic synth-edge note for synthesized hops. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#2 redux-thunk follow-up 2 says dynNamed fixes constant-to-constant redux-thunk surfacing tier-independently and generalizes to future constant/variable/field synths.

title: Non-fatal framework extractor failures
text:
# Non-fatal framework extractor failures

Lifecycle status: proposed

A failing framework-specific extractor should not abort the whole per-file extraction result; it should surface as a warning while the rest of extraction continues. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#3 Task 7 Step 3 wraps framework extraction in `try/catch` and appends a warning error instead of throwing.

title: Non-interface sibling detection
text:
# Non-interface sibling detection

Lifecycle status: proposed

Adaptive explore should eventually detect sibling families that are not represented by `implements` or `extends` edges. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Frontier says Go `HandlerFunc` slices and function-pointer registries are not caught, and Gin's middleware chain does not trip the gate because its handlers are funcs rather than interface implementations.

title: Non-unique callable whole-file spare
text:
# Non-unique callable whole-file spare

Lifecycle status: accepted

Treating every named callable as a whole-file spare floods the budget when the callable name is common across many variants. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 Further refinement item 1 says `as_sql` has 110 definitions and naming it must not keep every backend variant full.

title: Noninteractive installer flags
text:
# Noninteractive installer flags

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph install` supports noninteractive operation through target, location, confirmation, permission, and config-printing flags. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.7 New Features lists `--target`, `--location`, `--yes`, `--no-permissions`, and `--print-config` for scripting and CI.

title: Npm git dependencies stay excluded
text:
# Npm git dependencies stay excluded

Lifecycle status: accepted

Multi-repository workspace indexing must continue excluding git repositories inside `node_modules` because npm git dependencies are dependencies, not workspace projects. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features multi-repository workspace bullet.

title: Nuxt directory-prefixed component matching
text:
# Nuxt directory-prefixed component matching

Lifecycle status: accepted

Nuxt nested components are matched from PascalCase template tags using the Nuxt directory-prefixed auto-import name fallback. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 Nuxt nested components bullet.

title: ORM metaprogramming frontier
text:
# ORM metaprogramming frontier

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph has not yet resolved ORM metaprogramming dispatch for EF Core LINQ/DbSet, ActiveRecord dynamic finders, Eloquent dynamic finders and relationships, or Spring Data JPA derived queries. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 lists ActiveRecord dynamic finders, Eloquent dynamic finders, and Spring Data JPA derived queries as deferred metaprogramming frontiers, extending the earlier ORM frontier captured from #3.

title: ORM metaprogramming frontier
text:
# ORM metaprogramming frontier

Lifecycle status: superseded

CodeGraph has not yet resolved ORM metaprogramming dispatch for EF Core LINQ/DbSet, ActiveRecord dynamic finders, or Eloquent dynamic finders and relationships. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks these as hole-identified frontiers in the ASP.NET Core, Rails, and Laravel rows.

title: Object function symbol extraction
text:
# Object function symbol extraction

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph indexes functions defined inside stores and handler objects as real symbols, including Zustand actions and similar Redux, Pinia, MobX, exported handler, and route-map shapes. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.9 New Features.

title: Object registry synthesizer v1
text:
# Object registry synthesizer v1

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph shipped objectRegistryEdges for name-to-class registry and command-bus dispatch, linking dispatcher functions to registered callable handler entries from object-literal registries and computed-key dispatch. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Tier A marks Name-to-class registry / command bus as shipped v1 on 2026-06-20 with objectRegistryEdges and describes its handler-target behavior and validation.

title: Object registry v1 deferred forms
text:
# Object registry v1 deferred forms

Lifecycle status: accepted

Object registry synthesis v1 intentionally leaves assign-then-call, registry augmentation, method-shorthand recall, and cross-file barrel-namespace variants for later work. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Object registry row lists those deferred variants after the shipped v1 validation notes.

title: Objective-C message import completeness
text:
# Objective-C message import completeness

Lifecycle status: accepted

Objective-C impact and `codegraph affected` now resolve single-argument message selectors, class-message receivers, `#import` headers, and class-method calls through receiver types. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says these four fixes raised typical libraries from roughly a third-to-half of files with real dependents to about 90%.

title: Objective-C structural indexing
text:
# Objective-C structural indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Objective-C `.m`, `.mm`, and content-sniffed `.h` files parse with structural extraction for multi-part selectors, properties, imports, and superclass/protocol relationships. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 New Features.

title: Objective-C value-ref backlog
text:
# Objective-C value-ref backlog

Lifecycle status: proposed

Objective-C value-reference support remains proposed and needs the Ruby/class-scope treatment because constants include `static const`, `extern const`, and partially supported macros, and extractor kind emission must be confirmed before enabling. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §2b lists Objective-C under remaining needs-Ruby-treatment work and says class/type-heavy constants often extract as `field` or `property`, which the value-ref gate rejects unless re-kinded.

title: Offline telemetry stays silent
text:
# Offline telemetry stays silent

Lifecycle status: accepted

In offline or air-gapped environments, telemetry flushes fail silently, the buffer remains capped, and steady state is a bounded file with zero noise. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Client architecture Offline / air-gapped paragraph.

title: One framework hides many shapes
text:
# One framework hides many shapes

Lifecycle status: accepted

A framework label must not be treated as a single dispatch shape because Redux alone splits into thunk chains, RTK Query endpoints/hooks, and plain slice dispatch. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Discipline item 2 says the trezor-to-shapeshift split proves one framework is not one shape.

title: One install covers active agents
text:
# One install covers active agents

Lifecycle status: accepted

A single `codegraph install` should wire up every agent/editor a user actually uses, instead of requiring per-agent setup. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.7 says `codegraph install` sets up Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, and opencode from one multi-select prompt, with detected agents pre-checked, so a single install wires every editor.

title: One-line standalone installers
text:
# One-line standalone installers

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph ships one-line standalone installers for macOS/Linux (`install.sh`) and Windows (`install.ps1`) that fetch the self-contained bundle and put `codegraph` on PATH. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.0 New Features describes `install.sh` and `install.ps1` needing no Node.js.

title: Over-approximate instance reachability
text:
# Over-approximate instance reachability

Lifecycle status: accepted

Callback synthesized edges model reachability rather than instance precision; unregister/off behavior is ignored. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Edge cases/model says over-approximation across instances is accepted and unregister/off are ignored.

title: PHP callable registration edges
text:
# PHP callable registration edges

Lifecycle status: accepted

PHP string and array callables in trusted callable positions now link to functions and methods, including across files and through `$this` inheritance; arbitrary function string arguments are ignored. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 PHP callables bullet.

title: PHP constant name reader scan
text:
# PHP constant name reader scan

Lifecycle status: accepted

PHP value-reference support scans `name` nodes as constant references while avoiding extractor and shadow-prune changes because PHP constants already extract and `$var` locals cannot shadow bare constants. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says PHP was one reader-scan line for bare `X`, `self::X`, and `Foo::X`, with no extractor change and no prune wiring.

title: PHP namespaced dependency edges
text:
# PHP namespaced dependency edges

Lifecycle status: accepted

PHP impact and `codegraph affected` now track classes by fully namespaced name and record dependencies from `use` imports plus parameter, property, and return type hints. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says PHP previously ignored namespaces and linked only calls, `new`, and inheritance, collapsing same-named framework classes and missing imported DI contracts.

title: PHP static include dependencies
text:
# PHP static include dependencies

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph creates file-to-file dependency edges for PHP `include`, `require`, `include_once`, and `require_once` when the included path is static, while skipping dynamic includes. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says procedural/script-style PHP includes now affect `codegraph_callers` and `codegraph_impact`; dynamic forms like `include $var` are skipped.

title: Parameter shadowing residual
text:
# Parameter shadowing residual

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value refs intentionally leave parameter-only shadowing unguarded because adding parameter pruning would over-prune legitimate constants whose names coincide with parameters. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §3 lists parameter-only shadowing as a known intentional limitation and says the prune counts declarators, not params.

title: Parent-death MCP shutdown
text:
# Parent-death MCP shutdown

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph serve --mcp` shuts down on Linux when its parent process changes, releasing inotify watches, file descriptors, and SQLite WAL resources after OOM, `kill -9`, or container teardown; `CODEGRAPH_PPID_POLL_MS` tunes polling. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 Fixes.

title: Parent-kind sample check
text:
# Parent-kind sample check

Lifecycle status: accepted

Before enabling value references for the next class-scope language, inspect the parent kind of a sample constant and widen the target gate when that shared parent kind is missing. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A explicitly calls this the lesson for the next class-scope language and says missing `struct:`, `enum:`, or `interface:`-style parent kinds make the feature silently emit nothing despite nodes existing.

title: Parse fidelity before C++ value refs
text:
# Parse fidelity before C++ value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

Do not retry C++ value-reference edges until parse fidelity is solved, because partial guards against ERROR ancestors and compound-statement declarations still leave class-member, parameter, template, macro, and header misparse leaks. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says DON'T retry C++ without solving parse fidelity first and lists the residual leak classes.

title: Partial Linux live watch
text:
# Partial Linux live watch

Lifecycle status: accepted

On Linux inotify exhaustion, CodeGraph continues live-watching only the directories it could register while sync or git hooks cover the rest. CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says CodeGraph names `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` and keeps partial watching instead of silently leaving half the tree unwatched.

title: Pascal case-sensitive misses
text:
# Pascal case-sensitive misses

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value-reference scanning may miss references that differ only by case because Pascal is case-insensitive while the reader scan matches exact text; this is a false negative, not a false positive. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says differently-cased Pascal references are missed and not worth normalizing.

title: Pascal const value refs
text:
# Pascal const value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value-reference support adds Pascal to the enabled language set, uses existing unit/class `const` extraction, adds `declConst`/`declVar` shadow pruning, and extends reader scanning to the sibling `block` body of procedure headers. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says Pascal was add-to-`VALUE_REF_LANGS` plus shadow prune and the same sibling-body fix as Dart for `block` siblings under `defProc`.

title: Pascal const-param parse residual
text:
# Pascal const-param parse residual

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value refs accept a small residual false-positive tail where tree-sitter-pascal can context-dependently misparse a complex Delphi `const` parameter as `declConst`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#3 §7 says this parse-fidelity FP remains after restricting Pascal targets to `constant` only and is documented as an accepted caveat.

title: Pascal constant-only value-ref targets
text:
# Pascal constant-only value-ref targets

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal value-ref target capture must restrict targets to `constant` nodes only, because its extractor emits parameters and class fields as `variable` at a broad parent scope that would collapse into noisy file-wide targets. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#3 §7 says the genuine shared values were all `constant` (`declConst`) and the fix is a per-language restriction in `captureValueRefScope`.

title: Pascal implementation free routines
text:
# Pascal implementation free routines

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal procedures and functions defined only in the implementation section now get function nodes so their calls attribute to the routine instead of the file. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 Pascal call-coverage follow-ups says free-routine attribution (#795) resolved file-level aggregate attribution into per-routine edges.

title: Pascal paren-less calls
text:
# Pascal paren-less calls

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal no-argument method calls without parentheses are now extracted as calls only in statement position, leaving assignment and condition positions alone because they are ambiguous with field or property access. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 Pascal call-coverage follow-ups says paren-less calls (#793) were resolved and scoped to statement position.

title: Pascal paren-less reference capture
text:
# Pascal paren-less reference capture

Lifecycle status: accepted

Pascal paren-less expressions such as `Result := DoInitialize` are captured as references, not calls, because Pascal cannot distinguish a procedure value from a paren-less call without types. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits says the dependency direction is correct, these edges were previously invisible in #791, and the label is imperfect.

title: Pending re-index warning banner
text:
# Pending re-index warning banner

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph tool responses add a warning banner naming files whose watcher-observed edits are pending re-index, so agents read only those files directly while trusting the rest. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 New Features.

title: Pending startup causes fallback
text:
# Pending startup causes fallback

Lifecycle status: accepted

When the host sees CodeGraph as pending with zero tools on turn one, the agent starts with `Read`/`grep` and may never use CodeGraph in that session. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says startup pending caused this in nested evals and that real users hit a milder first-query version.

title: Per-OS index isolation
text:
# Per-OS index isolation

Lifecycle status: accepted

The same checkout opened from Windows and WSL needs separate CodeGraph indexes because one shared `.codegraph/` cannot safely serve both operating systems. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features `CODEGRAPH_DIR` bullet.

title: Per-call telemetry stream
text:
# Per-call telemetry stream

Lifecycle status: accepted

Sending per-keystroke or per-call telemetry is an anti-pattern for CodeGraph because usage must be locally aggregated into daily rollups before leaving the machine. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Non-goals / never collected and Events sections.

title: Per-call worktree index resolution
text:
# Per-call worktree index resolution

Lifecycle status: accepted

A long-running MCP server re-checks which index a path belongs to on each call. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says worktrees that gain their own `.codegraph/` are picked up without restart and stale different-worktree warnings drop.

title: Per-channel native bridge resolvers
text:
# Per-channel native bridge resolvers

Lifecycle status: proposed

Each mixed iOS or React Native bridging mechanism should be modeled as its own dispatch channel with its own resolver or synthesizer, validation, and playbook matrix row. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#0 §2 says each row is a separate dispatch channel in the playbook vocabulary, each gets its own resolver or synthesizer, validation, and §6 matrix row.

title: Per-definition ambiguous reports
text:
# Per-definition ambiguous reports

Lifecycle status: accepted

For same-named symbols across monorepo apps, `codegraph_callers`, `codegraph_callees`, and `codegraph_impact` report one section per distinct definition and accept a `file` argument to focus the intended definition. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 same-named symbols bullet.

title: Per-symbol family skeletonization
text:
# Per-symbol family skeletonization

Lifecycle status: proposed

Adaptive explore should eventually keep base-class methods full while eliding only redundant subclass bodies inside a family file. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Frontier says whole-file skeletonization makes `SQLCompiler.execute_sql` a signature and causes read-backs, and identifies per-symbol skeletonization within a family file as the ideal.

title: Per-symbol focused skeletons
text:
# Per-symbol focused skeletons

Lifecycle status: superseded

Collapsed family files render full bodies for on-spine, unique-named, and canonical-base-supertype methods while rendering only signatures for the rest. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 Further refinement item 2 describes the per-symbol focused view and its Django read-back fix.

title: Phase one bridge gate
text:
# Phase one bridge gate

Lifecycle status: proposed

Phase 2 must not begin until Swift-Objective-C bridging passes the mixed iOS §5a validation bar on Charts, Realm-Cocoa, and Wikipedia-iOS. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §6 Phase 1 says to validate on the Charts/Realm/Wikipedia corpus before moving on and not proceed to Phase 2 until Phase 1 passes the §5a bar on all three repos.

title: Pinia store instance bridge
text:
# Pinia store instance bridge

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph shipped piniaStoreEdges to link useStore().action() calls from consumer functions or Vue components to action nodes in the matching Pinia store file. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Vuex/Pinia row says the Pinia bridge shipped on 2026-06-20 with synthesizedBy:'pinia-store', factory binding, same-store-file gating, and tests.

title: Platform-local native include resolution
text:
# Platform-local native include resolution

Lifecycle status: accepted

Native includes and Kotlin Multiplatform imports resolve within the including file's local directory or source set before matching same-named platform alternatives. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 C/C++ quoted include and Kotlin `expect` source-set bullet.

title: Play routes file resolver
text:
# Play routes file resolver

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph indexes extensionless Play `conf/routes` files through a narrow file-walk opt-in and resolves `METHOD /path Controller.action(args)` lines to Scala controller actions. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks Scala Play done, with computer-database 0->8 and starter 0->4 while controls stayed unchanged.

title: Post-extraction resolver initialization
text:
# Post-extraction resolver initialization

Lifecycle status: accepted

`indexAll()` now calls `resolver.initialize()` after extraction completes so framework `detect()` runs against the populated index. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#2 §8c says the construction-time `initialize()` ran before any files were indexed, silently dropped indexed-file-aware framework resolvers, and was fixed by reinitializing after extraction.

title: Pre-edit blast radius visibility
text:
# Pre-edit blast radius visibility

Lifecycle status: accepted

Before editing, an agent should see dependents and relevant test coverage for the symbols it is inspecting without making a separate impact lookup. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.9 says `codegraph_explore` includes compact blast radius locations and covering test files so the agent can see what else to update and which tests to run.

title: Pre-index framework detection
text:
# Pre-index framework detection

Lifecycle status: accepted

Running framework `detect()` before file extraction is an anti-pattern for resolvers that consult the indexed file list, because it silently drops valid framework resolvers. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#2 §8c says the construction-time initialize pass happened before indexing, so all `context.getAllFiles()` / `context.readFile()` based framework resolvers returned false and dropped themselves.

title: Precision is recall's price
text:
# Precision is recall's price

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dispatch synthesis recall only helps when precision guards prevent false dynamic edges, including zero edges on non-pattern controls. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Discipline item 3 says redux-thunk's zero on shapeshift is the good kind of zero and sets the same bar for every synthesizer below.

title: Prefer deterministic adoption levers
text:
# Prefer deterministic adoption levers

Lifecycle status: accepted

Agent-adoption work should prioritize deterministic, shippable startup/tooling fixes before behavioral steering when the deterministic fix helps all users and avoids behavioral guesswork. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#1 lists verifying/decoupling `serve --mcp` `tools/list` first as highest-value, shippable, broadly helpful, and free of behavioral guesswork, before prototyping the PreToolUse(Read) redirect hook.

title: Preserve JSONC user edits
text:
# Preserve JSONC user edits

Lifecycle status: accepted

Installer edits to `opencode.jsonc` must preserve comments and formatting across install, reinstall, and uninstall. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.9 says comments and formatting survive because the installer makes surgical edits instead of rewriting the whole file.

title: Preserve diffuse flow breadth
text:
# Preserve diffuse flow breadth

Lifecycle status: accepted

Adaptive explore must not starve diffuse flows that genuinely need broad source context. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 Motivation explicitly requires avoiding starvation of diffuse flows, and the problem section contrasts interchangeable sibling files with distinct Excalidraw render-pipeline steps.

title: Probe the parsed call shape
text:
# Probe the parsed call shape

Lifecycle status: accepted

A language can look blocked if only the wrong syntactic form is probed; Pascal/Delphi was initially read as blocked because only the paren-less form was tested, while the paren'd chain port was clean. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 says the initial Pascal blocked read was wrong and caused by probing only the paren-less form.

title: Probe-only skeletonization validation
text:
# Probe-only skeletonization validation

Lifecycle status: accepted

Using only the deterministic probe query to validate skeletonization is unsafe because the probe can disagree with the real agent query about named symbols, spines, skeletonized files, and read-backs. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Dead ends item 6 says the probe reported Django had 0 skeletons and flat reads while the real agent skeletonized `compiler.py` and Read it back.

title: Programmatic API export
text:
# Programmatic API export

Lifecycle status: accepted

The package exports the `CodeGraph` class and building blocks such as `DatabaseConnection`, `QueryBuilder`, `initGrammars`, and `FileLock` for direct application embedding via `require` or `import`. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.8 New Features.

title: Project-local config auto-wiring
text:
# Project-local config auto-wiring

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph init` auto-wires project-local agent configuration for agents previously installed globally, so a global install applies in each opened project without per-project reinstall. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.7 says one global `codegraph install` works in every project you open because `codegraph init` wires project-local agent config for globally installed agents.

title: Project-name term exception
text:
# Project-name term exception

Lifecycle status: accepted

Project-name terms should be dropped from path scoring and explore type-disambiguation bias only when they are not the entire query; a bare project-name search must still work. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 search relevance bullet states the project name is dropped unless it is the only term.

title: Project-name-neutral intent ranking
text:
# Project-name-neutral intent ranking

Lifecycle status: accepted

Search ranking should not let a repo-wide project name overpower the query terms that identify the actual code area. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 says users naturally include the project name in queries, but it over-weighted matching paths and buried the backend in mixed-stack repos until project-name terms were neutralized for path scoring and type-disambiguation bias.

title: Project-name-neutral search scoring
text:
# Project-name-neutral search scoring

Lifecycle status: accepted

Search path relevance now counts each query word once and removes words matching the project name from path scoring and `codegraph_explore` type-disambiguation bias, unless the project name is the only term. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 search relevance bullet.

title: Prompt hook degrades safely
text:
# Prompt hook degrades safely

Lifecycle status: accepted

The Claude Code prompt hook must be additive and degradable: non-structural prompts and un-indexed projects are left alone, uninstall removes it, and `CODEGRAPH_NO_PROMPT_HOOK=1` disables it without uninstalling. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#9 Claude Code front-load hook bullet states these degradation, uninstall, and opt-out behaviors.

title: Property-string binding exclusion
text:
# Property-string binding exclusion

Lifecycle status: accepted

Markup property-string bindings such as `asp-for="Prop"` and `th:field="*{prop}"` are out of scope for the parser because they require model-type inference and have low value with high noise. Evidence: docs/design/template-markup-parser.md#0 Reference patterns section explicitly marks these bindings as the data-flow frontier and out of scope.

title: Public-codegraph anonymous telemetry
text:
# Public-codegraph anonymous telemetry

Lifecycle status: superseded

The public CodeGraph engine ships anonymous usage telemetry across CLI, MCP server, and installer scope, with Worker deploy/DNS and release still pending. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Status and Scope lines.

title: Python absolute import files
text:
# Python absolute import files

Lifecycle status: accepted

Python absolute dotted imports now link to the imported module's file while standard-library imports create no edge. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says `import conduit.apps.signals` previously did not link to that module file, leaving side-effect and setup imports with no dependents.

title: Python builtin-name filter tax
text:
# Python builtin-name filter tax

Lifecycle status: accepted

Filtering bare Python names such as `index`, `get`, `update`, or `count` as built-ins can silently drop legitimate route-to-handler edges when a declared symbol owns that name; the declared-symbol guard must apply to bare names, not only dotted method calls. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#5 says microblog's `index` view lost `/` and `/index` until the bare branch mirrored the existing `knownNames` guard, with +2 legitimate edges on realworld and 0 change on the Django control, and calls the builtin-name filter a silent precision tax across Python.

title: Python whole-module imports

title: Qualified resolution fixes

title: Qualified symbol disambiguation
text:
# Qualified symbol disambiguation

Lifecycle status: accepted

text:

Calls whose receiver is itself a factory, singleton, or builder call must resolve the outer method against the inner call's returned receiver type. Redux-thunk dispatch target resolution now prefers thunk-signature constants before other constants, same-file callables, and first-match fallback, fixing name collisions where a service function and thunk const share a name. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#2 redux-thunk follow-up 1 says octo-call leaveCall mis-resolved to the service function and the fix now targets the thunk const at call.ts:201.

title: Reference-existence dispatch routing
text:
# Reference-existence dispatch routing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dynamic-dispatch coverage must choose resolver or synthesizer based on whether a named reference exists: named refs use resolvers, while anonymous computed callbacks require registrar-dispatcher synthesis. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 2 states the key distinction driving mechanism choice: named refs resolve through a resolver; no ref exists for `cb()`, so a synthesizer correlates registrar and dispatcher sites.

title: Reflection DI registration modeling
text:
# Reflection DI registration modeling

Lifecycle status: proposed

Convention-heavy apps need a separate reflection and DI-registration modeling pass to move beyond the markup parser's ASP.NET coverage ceiling. Evidence: docs/design/template-markup-parser.md#0 Non-goals says reflection/proxy registration, AutoMapper, Swagger, DI container, and middleware remain separate work needed for 95% coverage.

title: Regex captures need consumers
text:
# Regex captures need consumers

Lifecycle status: accepted

A framework extractor is not correct just because its regex captures the handler; the captured group must be destructured and emitted into references so route-to-handler links can form. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#0 Background says Django captured the view name in group 2 but discarded it during destructuring, so even a live hook would not link the route to the view, and similar shape bugs existed across most frameworks.

title: Reject blanket Read-deny hook
text:
# Reject blanket Read-deny hook

Lifecycle status: accepted

The blanket Read-deny redirect hook must not ship as the CodeGraph adoption mechanism. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says the hook was A/B'd and REJECTED, kept only as an eval artifact, because it regressed target metrics and the agent routed around it.

title: Release verifies npm package presence
text:
# Release verifies npm package presence

Lifecycle status: accepted

A CodeGraph release must verify that every expected platform package reached the npm registry so a release cannot pass green while missing a package. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.1 says the linux-x64 package was missing in 0.9.0 and the release pipeline now verifies every package reached npm.

title: Remove CodeGraph config file
text:
# Remove CodeGraph config file

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph removed `.codegraph/config.json`, the related config API surface, and `.codegraphignore`; existing config files are ignored. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.2 Breaking Changes says the config file and config API were removed and `.codegraphignore` is no longer supported.

title: Repeatable dispatch coverage method
text:
# Repeatable dispatch coverage method

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph uses a repeatable per-language/framework method: choose the canonical flow, measure the hole deterministically, classify the dispatch shape, implement the matching resolver or synthesizer, and validate with deterministic, precision, regression, and agent-eval checks. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 Section 4 lays out Steps 1-5 and says to run this methodology per language/framework.

title: Replace implementation Reads
text:
# Replace implementation Reads

Lifecycle status: accepted

Agents should use CodeGraph instead of `Read`/`grep` during implementation, with success measured by wall-clock time, tool-call count, and Read=0 rather than token cost. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 frames P1 as agents still reaching for `Read`/`grep` and states the optimization target is wall-clock + tool-call count + Read=0, not token cost.

title: Repo-root extension mapping
text:
# Repo-root extension mapping

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph reads a repo-root `codegraph.json` `extensions` map and indexes files with those custom extensions as the named language instead of silently skipping them. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#10 documents `{ "extensions": { ".dota_lua": "lua", ".tpl": "php" } }`, layering over built-ins and preserving old behavior when absent.

title: Request route flow reachability
text:
# Request route flow reachability

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph needs request-route-handler flow edges for web frameworks so route declarations connect to the components, handlers, services, repositories, or APIs they invoke. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 lists canonical flows such as request→route→handler→service, url→view→model, request→@Controller→DI service→repo, and request→route→controller across many frameworks.

title: Request-handler flow rollout
text:
# Request-handler flow rollout

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph request-to-handler flows trace end-to-end across many web stacks, including Express, Rails, Spring, Django/DRF, Laravel, Flask, FastAPI, Gin, chi, ASP.NET, Drupal, Axum, actix, Vapor, Play, Vue/Nuxt, Svelte/SvelteKit, and React Router. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 New Features.

title: Rocket route macro links
text:
# Rocket route macro links

Lifecycle status: accepted

Rocket handler paths inside `routes![...]` and `catchers![...]` macros are linked to the `mount` or `register` call that mounts them. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 Rocket route handlers bullet.

title: Root-confined file reads
text:
# Root-confined file reads

Lifecycle status: accepted

File-view reads must validate requested paths within the project root. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says `handleFileView` preserves security by reading through `validatePathWithinRoot`, referencing #527.

title: Root-ish files path normalization
text:
# Root-ish files path normalization

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_files` treats root-ish paths like `/`, `.`, `./`, empty string, and Windows-style `\` as the whole project, and normalizes subdirectory filters across slash styles. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 Fixes.

title: Route counts catch regressions
text:
# Route counts catch regressions

Lifecycle status: accepted

Cross-repo route-count checks catch resolver regressions that a single example can miss. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 says a first Spring mapping fix regressed mall from 292 to 1 route by dropping method-level `@RequestMapping`, and the cross-repo route-count check caught it.

title: Route prefix propagation
text:
# Route prefix propagation

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph should propagate framework route prefixes from grouping APIs into nested route labels when the handler target already resolves. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 lists this frontier for Go subrouter/`PathPrefix` path prefixes, GoFrame reflective `Bind` group prefixes, and Rust actix `web::scope("/api")` prefixes.

title: Route prefix propagation backlog
text:
# Route prefix propagation backlog

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph should add prefix propagation for grouped or scoped route APIs whose handlers already resolve but whose route labels omit framework grouping prefixes. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 marks Go subrouter/`PathPrefix`, GoFrame reflective `Bind` group prefixes, and Rust actix `web::scope("/api")` prefix prepending as frontiers.

title: Route references reuse resolution
text:
# Route references reuse resolution

Lifecycle status: superseded

Framework extraction should emit route-to-handler targets as `UnresolvedRef` entries and feed them into the existing unresolved-reference pipeline, so the name matcher, import resolver, and framework `resolve()` strategies create ordinary final `references` edges. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#0 Architecture states extracted references flow into the existing unresolved-references pipeline and gives the `path('/users', UserListView.as_view())` route node linked by `references` to `UserListView` as the net effect.

title: Route references reuse resolution shipped
text:
# Route references reuse resolution shipped

Lifecycle status: accepted

Framework resolver references flow through the existing resolution pipeline, including name matching, import resolution, and framework-specific `resolve()`, to produce `route -> handler` edges. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#4 Fix says handler references flow through the existing resolution pipeline to produce route-to-handler edges.

title: Ruby constant-assignment value refs
text:
# Ruby constant-assignment value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

Ruby value-reference support creates nodes for `CONST = ...` assignments, accepts `class:` and `module:` parents in the target gate, and scans `constant` reader nodes so class/module-internal constants can produce same-file value-reference edges. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#2 says Ruby had 0 top-level vs 58 class-internal constants in jekyll `lib/`, the original file-scope-only gate covered almost nothing, and Ruby required those three Ruby-specific fixes.

title: Ruby lifecycle hook edges
text:
# Ruby lifecycle hook edges

Lifecycle status: accepted

Ruby lifecycle hook symbols such as `before_action`, `after_save`, validations, and `rescue_from` handlers now link to class or inherited methods, while plural `validates` is excluded because it names attributes. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 Ruby lifecycle-hook symbols bullet.

title: Ruby mixin and require edges
text:
# Ruby mixin and require edges

Lifecycle status: accepted

Ruby impact and `codegraph affected` now follow module mixins and `require` or `require_relative` file dependencies. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says `include`, `extend`, and `prepend` were previously read as method calls, required files had no dependents, and a typical gem improved from about 71% to about 100% of files showing real dependents.

title: Runtime selector dispatch out of scope
text:
# Runtime selector dispatch out of scope

Lifecycle status: proposed

Native bridge coverage should not attempt runtime dispatch through Objective-C `performSelector:`. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §7 lists runtime dispatch on `performSelector:` as out of scope and ties it to the named-only anti-goal.

title: Runtime-keyed boundary surfacing
text:
# Runtime-keyed boundary surfacing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph surfaces runtime-keyed, reflective, typed-mediator, and proxy dispatch as query-time dynamic boundaries instead of synthesizing unsafe edges. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#1 Step 3 says runtime-keyed tables, dynamic `getattr`, reflection, typed mediator buses, and `new Proxy` dispatch that cannot be precision-gated should use boundary surfacing in `src/mcp/dynamic-boundaries.ts` rather than edge synthesis.

title: Rust extractor
text:
# Rust extractor

Lifecycle status: accepted

The Rust extractor is the CodeGraph indexing surface for Rust module paths, struct literals, use/pub use edges, trait implementations, and framework macros. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 Rust impact, module path, and Rocket bullets.

title: Rust module graph dependencies
text:
# Rust module graph dependencies

Lifecycle status: accepted

Rust struct literals, `use`/`pub use`, Rust module paths, and trait dispatch are connected into impact and affected so module hubs and trait-only implementations have dependents. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 Rust impact and affected bullet.

title: Rust relative module-path calls
text:
# Rust relative module-path calls

Lifecycle status: accepted

Rust cross-module calls such as sibling `users::router()` and deeper `database::profiles::find()` paths resolve relative to the current module instead of only the crate root. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 Rust cross-module function calls bullet.

title: Rust web route extraction
text:
# Rust web route extraction

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph resolves Rust Axum chained methods and namespaced handlers, Rocket attribute macros, and actix builder API route declarations. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 marks Axum `.route("/x", get(h1).post(h2))` per-method extraction and last-`::` handler capture done, Rocket attribute macros at 550/556, and actix `web::resource(...).route(web::get().to(h))`, `.to(h)`, and App `.route(... web::get().to(h))` support raising actix-examples from 51→128 routes and 35→112 resolved.

title: RxJS subscribe deferral
text:
# RxJS subscribe deferral

Lifecycle status: deprecated

CodeGraph deliberately does not build an RxJS subscribe synthesizer because observable-to-observer flow is predominantly anonymous closures with no stable static name to seed. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Tier C lists RxJS subscribe under frontier do-not-build and says the playbook keeps it deferred.

title: Safe temp marker open
text:
# Safe temp marker open

Lifecycle status: accepted

The temp-dir marker written by `codegraph_context` must be opened safely so it cannot follow a symlink to another writable file on a shared machine. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.2 Security says the marker is now opened safely, closing a symlink redirection hole.

title: Same-file value-ref scope
text:
# Same-file value-ref scope

Lifecycle status: accepted
