Value-reference edges are same-file only: targets and reader scopes are reset per file and `flushValueRefs()` emits only within that file. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §1 says targets and scopes are per-file, reset each flush, and the edge is same-file only.

title: Same-file value-ref yield limit
text:
# Same-file value-ref yield limit

Lifecycle status: accepted

Same-file-only value-reference capture has lower yield in languages where constants are commonly read cross-file or cross-unit, such as PHP and Pascal, but remains correct rather than noisy. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says PHP and Pascal have low yield because reads are often cross-file/cross-unit while value-refs remain same-file only.

title: Sample variable targets before trusting
text:
# Sample variable targets before trusting

Lifecycle status: accepted

Before trusting a new language's `variable` targets for value refs, sample them to confirm they represent module/global shared state rather than parameters or instance fields. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#3 §7 states this as the Pascal trap after `Dest` and `aItem` were read everywhere because parameter and field variables passed the target gate.

title: Scala object vals as constants
text:
# Scala object vals as constants

Lifecycle status: accepted

Scala value-reference support treats top-level and singleton `object` `val`/`var` definitions as constants/variables, while class/trait/enum member vals remain fields. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says Scala has no static, singleton object vals are the shared-constant idiom, and the `val_definition` handler walks to the enclosing definition to choose constant/variable versus field.

title: Scala programmatic dispatch frontier
text:
# Scala programmatic dispatch frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph still lacks Scala Play SIRD programmatic router includes and Akka actor message-to-handler dispatch for `receive` and `Behaviors.receiveMessage`. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks SIRD and Akka actor dispatch as hole-identified frontiers after Play `conf/routes` support.

title: Scala typeclass dependency graph
text:
# Scala typeclass dependency graph

Lifecycle status: accepted

Scala impact and `codegraph affected` now connect parameterized supertypes, type-signature references, context bounds, implicit typeclass parameters, and `new T[...]` instantiations. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says Scala previously linked only plain calls and bare non-generic supertypes, missing most typeclass-heavy graphs such as cats and algebra.

title: Scalar callback field synthesis
text:
# Scalar callback field synthesis

Lifecycle status: proposed

Callback synthesis should add a scalar-store variant for single-callback fields assigned to `this.onChange` and later invoked. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work item 5 says this single-callback field variant is not built.

title: Schema-advertised filter behavior
text:
# Schema-advertised filter behavior

Lifecycle status: accepted

A CodeGraph tool filter advertised in its schema must return the matching indexed symbols rather than silently matching nothing. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 says `codegraph_search` advertised `kind: "type"` but silently matched nothing until fixed to find type aliases.

title: Scriptable index freshness checks
text:
# Scriptable index freshness checks

Lifecycle status: accepted

CI and scripts need one command or library call that reports the running CLI version, index location, and last-indexed freshness timestamp. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features `codegraph status --json` bullet.

title: Scriptable installer operation
text:
# Scriptable installer operation

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph installation should be automatable for scripts and CI without interactive prompts. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.7 says non-interactive install is supported with `--target`, `--location`, `--yes`, `--no-permissions`, and `--print-config`.

title: Search result shape gotcha
text:
# Search result shape gotcha

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph value-ref tests must unwrap `searchNodes` results with `.map(r => r.node)` and iterate `getImpactRadius().nodes.values()`, because `searchNodes` returns `SearchResult[]` while impact-radius nodes are stored in a `Map`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#3 §7 lists this as a trap already hit.

title: Self-contained runtime distribution
text:
# Self-contained runtime distribution

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph ships its own self-contained runtime, allowing install on any Node version or no Node and eliminating native build steps from the normal install path. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.0 says CodeGraph now ships its own self-contained runtime, installs on any Node version or none, and has no native build step.

title: Self-ignoring index folder
text:
# Self-ignoring index folder

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph writes `.codegraph/.gitignore` so everything in the generated index folder is ignored except the ignore file itself. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says the database, `daemon.pid`, sockets, and logs stop showing up as untracked changes.

title: Sensitive config summarization
text:
# Sensitive config summarization

Lifecycle status: accepted

File-view must summarize `yaml` and `properties` files by key rather than dumping their contents. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says security was preserved by summarizing yaml/properties by key and never dumping them, referencing #383.

title: Sequential spines are irreducible
text:
# Sequential spines are irreducible

Lifecycle status: accepted

Sequential-flow spines with no redundant siblings must be rendered rather than capped or collapsed. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 says the Alamofire sequential-flow spine is irreducible and the fix is to render it, not cap it.

title: Server resolver extract rollout shipped
text:
# Server resolver extract rollout shipped

Lifecycle status: accepted

The server framework resolver rollout updated Laravel, Rails, Spring, Gin, Axum, ASP.NET, and Vapor to emit both route nodes and handler references under the shared `extract()` contract. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#4 Fix says all 13 existing framework resolvers, including Laravel, Rails, Spring, Gin, Axum, ASP.NET, and Vapor, now emit route nodes and handler references.

title: SessionStart daemon prewarm hook
text:
# SessionStart daemon prewarm hook

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph should consider an opt-in Claude Code `SessionStart` hook to pre-warm the daemon as a cheap mitigation if instant static tool listing is hard. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 ranks this as a CodeGraph-side mitigation and recommends shipping it in parallel with the static `tools/list` fix.

title: Shadow prune counts syntax declarators
text:
# Shadow prune counts syntax declarators

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-ref shadow pruning must compare syntax-tree declarator counts against file-scope graph-node counts, not a flat duplicate-name count, so inner rebindings are pruned while conditional module definitions survive. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#1 §3 says inner rebindings are not graph nodes, declarators are counted at syntax-tree level, per-language declarator node types matter, and comparison against file-scope node count keeps conditional module defs such as `try: X=...; except: X=...`.

title: Shadowed value-ref targets pruned
text:
# Shadowed value-ref targets pruned

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-reference emission must prune targets shadowed by local declarations before walking reader scopes, because otherwise a local declaration with the same name would create wrong reader-to-file-scope edges. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §1 says `flushValueRefs()` prunes shadowed targets, and §2 calls PR #895 the flip-on plus shadow-prune change with tests verifying shadowed consts are not edged.

title: Shape-oriented dispatch backlog
text:
# Shape-oriented dispatch backlog

Lifecycle status: accepted

The dispatch-synthesizer backlog is organized by dispatch shape rather than language-by-framework because one framework can contain multiple indirection shapes and one shape can recur across frameworks and languages. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Relationship to the playbook contrasts the playbook's language x framework matrix with this doc's dispatch-shape organization.

title: Shared background server
text:
# Shared background server

Lifecycle status: accepted

The shared background server is the daemon CodeGraph sessions attach to for MCP/tool service across clients. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 shared background server logging, lifecycle, and restart bullets.

title: Shared chained-call resolvers
text:
# Shared chained-call resolvers

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph centralizes chained-call matching in three shared resolvers in `src/resolution/name-matcher.ts`: C/C++ field-expression chains, PHP/Rust scoped chains, and dotted chains for Java-family and similar languages. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 lists `matchCppCallChain`, `matchScopedCallChain`, and `matchDottedCallChain`, all calling `resolveMethodOnType`.

title: Shared daemon lingers never
text:
# Shared daemon lingers never

Lifecycle status: accepted

The shared background server drops clients whose process is gone and refuses to run indefinitely with attached but inactive clients. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 two further safeguards bullet says these guarantee wind-down on every platform.

title: Shared project daemon
text:
# Shared project daemon

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph runs one background daemon per project shared by multiple AI agents, with one file watcher, one SQLite connection, and one tree-sitter warm-up instead of independent copies per client. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 New Features.

title: Shared project indexing cost
text:
# Shared project indexing cost

Lifecycle status: accepted

Multiple AI agents in the same project should share indexing infrastructure instead of each paying for its own watcher, SQLite connection, and tree-sitter warm-up. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 says parallel agents now share one background daemon per project with a single file watcher, SQLite connection, and tree-sitter warm-up.

title: Shell-only graph access
text:
# Shell-only graph access

Lifecycle status: accepted

Agents that only have shell access should still be able to use CodeGraph graph answers without MCP by calling CLI commands that return the same content as MCP tools. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 subagents bullet describes `codegraph explore` and `codegraph node` for any agent with a shell.

title: Shopify JSON section links
text:
# Shopify JSON section links

Lifecycle status: accepted

Shopify OS 2.0 JSON templates and section groups now link listed section `type` values to their `sections/<type>.liquid` files. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says sections used only from JSON templates were reported as having no dependents, and JSON files are now read so editing a section surfaces templates that render it.

title: Sibling CodeGraph directory exclusion
text:
# Sibling CodeGraph directory exclusion

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph skips sibling `.codegraph-*` directories during indexing and watching so separate environment-specific indexes do not see or disturb each other's data. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features `CODEGRAPH_DIR` bullet.

title: Sibling class constant ambiguity
text:
# Sibling class constant ambiguity

Lifecycle status: accepted

The file-wide class-scope target map accepts a residual false-positive risk when sibling classes in the same file define the same constant name. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A says this is the only real false-positive case, observed at about 1.7% of Ruby targets on Rails, and valid code rarely hits it because a bare sibling-class constant is a Ruby NameError.

title: Sibling exemplar selection
text:
# Sibling exemplar selection

Lifecycle status: proposed

When no interceptor or sibling implementation is on the spine, adaptive explore may need to show one forced exemplar instead of skeletonizing all siblings. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Frontier says all siblings skeletonize today in this case and a forced exemplar might read better, but it is untested.

title: Sibling gate protects distinct steps
text:
# Sibling gate protects distinct steps

Lifecycle status: accepted

The sibling condition is what makes adaptive skeletonization safe; a core-floor gate can collapse distinct flow steps and regress cost. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Dead ends item 4 says a plain core-floor gate skeletonized Excalidraw's distinct steps and caused a 17% cost regression, while the sibling condition is safe.

title: Sibling threshold at three implementers
text:
# Sibling threshold at three implementers

Lifecycle status: accepted

Only supertypes with at least three implementers count as polymorphic sibling families for skeletonization. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 defines `MIN_SIBLINGS` as ≥3 and says 1:1 service-interface pairs are not siblings and stay full.

title: Sibling-body reader scans
text:
# Sibling-body reader scans

Lifecycle status: accepted

Some grammars store a function or procedure body as a sibling of the signature node used as the reader scope, so value-reference scanning must pull in those sibling bodies or it will find no reads. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says Dart required scanning the next-sibling `function_body`, and Pascal required extending the same fix to sibling `block` bodies.

title: Sidekiq deferred forms
text:
# Sidekiq deferred forms

Lifecycle status: accepted

Sidekiq synthesis v1 intentionally leaves superclass-chain worker detection, `Jobs.enqueue(:sym)` facade dispatch, and dispatch from non-method contexts for later work. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Sidekiq row lists those forms under Deferred.

title: Sidekiq dispatch synthesizer
text:
# Sidekiq dispatch synthesizer

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph shipped `sidekiqDispatchEdges` for Ruby Sidekiq by linking `perform_async`, `perform_in`, and `perform_at` call sites to the worker class's instance `perform` method, gated on Sidekiq worker includes. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Sidekiq row marks it shipped on 2026-06-20 with 100% precision on loomio and forem plus zero edges on jekyll.

title: Sidekiq namespace disambiguation
text:
# Sidekiq namespace disambiguation

Lifecycle status: accepted

Sidekiq worker resolution must prefer exact qualified names and bail on ambiguous unqualified collisions because simple-name matching can target the wrong namespace. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Sidekiq row says forem exposed four `SendEmailNotificationWorker`s and simple-name resolution mis-targeted 7 of 143 edges before the namespace fix.

title: Sidekiq worker-include gate
text:
# Sidekiq worker-include gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

Sidekiq dispatch synthesis must only link calls to classes proven to include `Sidekiq::Job` or `Sidekiq::Worker` and must not match ActiveJob `perform_later` or `perform_now`. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Sidekiq row says the receiver class is gated by reading the include from class body source and ActiveJob is deliberately not matched.

title: Silent beats wrong synthesis
text:
# Silent beats wrong synthesis

Lifecycle status: accepted

Dispatch synthesizers should remain silent rather than emit wrong edges when a shape cannot be resolved precisely enough. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 status legend marks deliberately not built as silent beats wrong.

title: Silent daemon attach by default
text:
# Silent daemon attach by default

Lifecycle status: accepted

The shared background server no longer logs a normal daemon attach as an error-like line by default; `CODEGRAPH_MCP_LOG_ATTACH=1` opts into the message for debugging. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 shared background server attach-log bullet.

title: Single FrameworkExtractionResult type
text:
# Single FrameworkExtractionResult type

Lifecycle status: accepted

`FrameworkExtractionResult` must be defined once and reused by every framework resolver's `extract` signature to keep route-node and reference return types consistent. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#4 Self-Review Checklist says `FrameworkExtractionResult` is defined once in Task 1 and used by every resolver's `extract` signature.

title: Single-callback field synthesis
text:
# Single-callback field synthesis

Lifecycle status: proposed

Callback synthesis should support scalar callback fields such as `this.onChange = cb` followed by `this.onChange()`. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work item 5 names single-callback fields as an unbuilt scalar-store variant.

title: Single-hop chained resolution
text:
# Single-hop chained resolution

Lifecycle status: accepted

The current chain re-encoding resolves one hop; deeper fluent chains keep the bare name and should be re-measured on deep fluent-builder repos. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 Edge cases says deeper hops such as `a.b().c().d()` keep the bare name because the inner `()` defeats the class-method split.

title: Single-hop event bus rendering
text:
# Single-hop event bus rendering

Lifecycle status: accepted

A custom event bus whose emit and handler connect through one synthesized hop now shows that hop explicitly with the registration site instead of rendering no flow section. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features `codegraph_explore` related event-bus sentence.

title: Single-repo synthesis is unvalidated
text:
# Single-repo synthesis is unvalidated

Lifecycle status: accepted

A dispatch synthesizer validated on one repository is still unvalidated because the apparent second repository may not contain the target shape at all. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Discipline item 1 says redux-thunk was tuned on trezor-suite alone, while shapeshift correctly produced zero thunk edges because it was an RTK Query codebase.

title: Sizing requires skeletonization
text:
# Sizing requires skeletonization

Lifecycle status: accepted

Explore output size only shrinks when bodies are skeletonized, not when low-value files are merely demoted or ranked lower. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Dead ends item 1 says demoting low-value files improved content quality but not size because explore refilled the freed budget, and concludes that ranking is not shrinking.

title: Skip Luau chained calls
text:
# Skip Luau chained calls

Lifecycle status: deprecated

Luau chained-call support was evaluated and intentionally not shipped because real Luau rarely annotates factory returns, producing +0 on both Fusion and matter despite synthetic support. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 Coverage and Full README classification classify Luau as evaluated and skipped because gradual typing makes the mechanism low-yield.

title: Skip TypeScript chained calls
text:
# Skip TypeScript chained calls

Lifecycle status: deprecated

TypeScript chained-call support was fully implemented and evaluated but intentionally not shipped because inferred rather than declared factory return types caused +0 added edges and net recall regression on real repos. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 Why TypeScript was skipped reports typeorm +0/-6, nest +0/-164, and says the only path to a win is inferred return-type analysis.

title: Slice-index dispatch needs synthesis
text:
# Slice-index dispatch needs synthesis

Lifecycle status: accepted

When a framework dispatches by indexing a handler slice, ordinary callee resolution can dead-end on helper code and agents may waste time re-querying the wrong site; find the dynamic dispatcher and synthesize the registration-to-dispatch edges instead. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 says Gin `Context.Next` calls `c.handlers[c.index](c)`, tree-sitter could not resolve it, `callees(Next)` dead-ended at `safeInt8`, and the agent rabbit-holed until `ginMiddlewareChainEdges` linked the dispatcher to registered handlers.

title: Slow-filesystem MCP startup tolerance
text:
# Slow-filesystem MCP startup tolerance

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph makes MCP tools appear reliably on slow filesystems such as Docker Desktop VirtioFS on macOS and WSL2, where startup handshakes could time out while the process kept running. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.10 Fixes says the startup handshake timeout was fixed so tools reliably appear.

title: Specific project root indexing
text:
# Specific project root indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Indexing roots should be intentional project directories, not broad filesystem roots that accidentally include caches, libraries, and unrelated projects. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says running the installer or `codegraph init` / `codegraph index` from the home folder or filesystem root no longer indexes everything underneath and now refuses those roots unless `--force` is passed.

title: Spring controller bean bridging
text:
# Spring controller bean bridging

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph bridges Spring controllers through mappings, DI service interfaces, concrete beans, and configuration property bindings. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 marks bare `@GetMapping`/`@PostMapping` with class `@RequestMapping` prefix join done, DI controller→service resolution done, interfaceOverrideEdges shipped for interface/base method to implementation dispatch, field-injected concrete-bean trace fixed by stripping `this.` and resolving declared field types, and `@Value`/`@ConfigurationProperties` application config binding done.

title: Spring event deferred forms
text:
# Spring event deferred forms

Lifecycle status: accepted

Spring event synthesis v1 intentionally leaves `publishEvent(bareVar)`, listener-return-value republish, `@DomainEvents` or `AbstractAggregateRoot.registerEvent`, and generic `PayloadApplicationEvent<X>` params for later work. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Spring events row lists those forms under Deferred.

title: Spring event synthesizer
text:
# Spring event synthesizer

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph shipped `springEventEdges` for Spring events by mapping `publishEvent(new XEvent(...))` sites to `@EventListener`, `@TransactionalEventListener`, and `ApplicationListener<X>` listeners through type-keyed two-pass synthesis. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Spring events row marks it shipped on 2026-06-20 with 100% precision on halo and thombergs/code-examples plus zero edges on gson.

title: Spring exact event-type match
text:
# Spring exact event-type match

Lifecycle status: accepted

Spring event synthesis must key publishers and listeners by exact event type names from `publishEvent(new XEvent(...))` and listener type declarations, with no imprecise name resolution. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#1 Spring events row says it is keyed by exact type name and precision is structural from param type to `new X` type.

title: Spring external config frontier
text:
# Spring external config frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph still needs config-key linkage beyond in-repo application/bootstrap config files, including `@PropertySource` external property files and Spring Cloud Config remote properties. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 lists those as Spring config-key linkage coverage frontiers after `@Value` and `@ConfigurationProperties` resolution shipped.

title: Stale files must be named
text:
# Stale files must be named

Lifecycle status: accepted

When watcher-observed edits are not yet indexed, CodeGraph responses must tell the agent exactly which files are stale instead of silently serving a stale graph as fresh. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 releases 0.9.5 and 0.9.6 say tool responses add a warning banner naming stale files and watcher sync keeps files stale while another process holds the index lock.

title: Stale-engine status warning
text:
# Stale-engine status warning

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph status` flags when a project index was built by an older engine than the running binary and recommends re-indexing, including in JSON output. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 status bullet.

title: Stale-lock watcher accuracy
text:
# Stale-lock watcher accuracy

Lifecycle status: accepted

The file watcher keeps edited files marked stale while another process holds the index lock, instead of marking them fresh before indexing actually succeeds. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 Fixes.

title: Standalone template extractor pattern
text:
# Standalone template extractor pattern

Lifecycle status: accepted

Razor markup parsing follows the existing standalone non-tree-sitter extractor pattern rather than adding a grammar, because the markup references are highly stylized and match the Svelte/Vue/Liquid scanning model. Evidence: docs/design/template-markup-parser.md#0 Architecture says to mirror the existing standalone extractors exactly and build `razor-extractor.ts` as a regex/line scan because no grammar is needed.

title: Startup pending largely disappears
text:
# Startup pending largely disappears

Lifecycle status: proposed

If static local `tools/list` exposure lands, pending-at-startup should largely disappear without a host-side MCP client change. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says this would make CodeGraph connected instantly for everyone and largely remove pending-at-startup.

title: Static identifier value-ref boundary
text:
# Static identifier value-ref boundary

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-reference edges intentionally cover only reads with a static identifier to match, so reactive or computed reads reachable only through framework getters are out of scope. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#3 Known limitations says reactive/computed reads with no static identifier to match are not covered.

title: Static member type dependencies
text:
# Static member type dependencies

Lifecycle status: accepted

A type referenced only through a static member, enum value, or class constant now records a dependency on that type. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says enum values, static constants, and class constants previously missed type dependencies, and the fix applies to Java, C#, Kotlin, Swift, Scala, Dart, PHP, and C++.

title: Static method target resolution
text:
# Static method target resolution

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph resolves cross-file static method calls such as `ClassName.staticMethod()` to the method itself instead of the class construction target. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says callers and impact for static methods no longer come back empty for TypeScript/JavaScript utility classes, with Python and similar languages benefiting too.

title: Status command
text:
# Status command

Lifecycle status: accepted

The `codegraph status` command reports project index state, including stale engine-version warnings. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 status bullet.

title: Status freshness JSON
text:
# Status freshness JSON

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph status --json` reports the running CLI `version`, `indexPath`, and `lastIndexed` timestamp, and `CodeGraph.getLastIndexedAt()` exposes the same freshness check through the library API. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features `codegraph status --json` bullet.

title: Status ignore-rule parity
text:
# Status ignore-rule parity

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph status` change detection applies the same ignore rules as full indexing and sync. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says tracked files inside committed dependency directories or under gitignored directories no longer create phantom pending changes that never clear.

title: Status reports journal mode
text:
# Status reports journal mode

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph status` reports the effective SQLite journal mode so database lock reports can be triaged quickly. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.0 says status now reports effective journal mode, making `database is locked` reports easy to triage at a glance.

title: Streaming dynamic call linking
text:
# Streaming dynamic call linking

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph streams function and method records while linking dynamic call relationships instead of loading every function and method into memory at once. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says symbol-dense files with tens of thousands of functions or methods no longer exhaust the heap and memory stays flat no matter how many symbols the project has.

title: Structural prompt graph grounding
text:
# Structural prompt graph grounding

Lifecycle status: accepted

Structural questions should be grounded with CodeGraph source and call paths before the agent starts answering, so the agent answers from the graph instead of grepping around to rebuild structure. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#9 Claude Code front-load hook bullet says structural prompts like 'how does X work', 'what calls Y', and 'trace the flow from A to B' inject relevant source and call paths up front.

title: Subagent-visible CodeGraph guidance
text:
# Subagent-visible CodeGraph guidance

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph guidance must be present in each agent instructions file because Task-tool subagents see those files while the MCP server's own guidance reaches only the main agent. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 subagents bullet says `codegraph install` writes marker-fenced sections into CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and GEMINI.md for the subagent-visible surface.

title: Submodule worktree exclusion
text:
# Submodule worktree exclusion

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph recognizes worktrees created from submodules and skips them as duplicate working views while keeping the submodule's own checkout indexed. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says one report had about 28% duplicate index content before this distinction.

title: Sufficiency beats forced routing
text:
# Sufficiency beats forced routing

Lifecycle status: accepted

When agents avoid CodeGraph, making the CodeGraph output genuinely sufficient is the right lever; forcing routing with blanket denial is the wrong lever. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 concludes that forcing is the wrong lever and making the tool genuinely better than Read is the right one.

title: Supertype signal overrides sparing
text:
# Supertype signal overrides sparing

Lifecycle status: accepted

The supertype signal must override named-callable sparing for family files, not spare them, because sparing a huge base-plus-subclasses file starves explore budget. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 says using the supertype signal as a spare was backwards and regressed Django to 9% costlier.

title: Supertype-definition spare
text:
# Supertype-definition spare

Lifecycle status: accepted

Sparing a file just because it defines the supertype is backwards for base-plus-subclasses family files because it keeps a huge family file full and starves sibling files from the explore budget. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Dead ends item 5 says Django `compiler.py` is 2,266 lines, Read anyway, and sparing it regressed Django to 9% costlier.

title: Svelte Vue script line offsets
text:
# Svelte Vue script line offsets

Lifecycle status: accepted

Svelte and Vue `<script>` block extraction now reports symbol line numbers exactly as they appear in the file, fixing the previous one-line offset across search, `codegraph_node`, and explore output. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 Svelte/Vue script-block line-number bullet.

title: Svelte action namespace frontier
text:
# Svelte action namespace frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph still needs the resolver interaction that lets `$lib`-alias namespace calls from extracted Svelte action nodes resolve the same way they do for `load`. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 says `api.post` from an extracted action node does not resolve through a `$lib` alias namespace while the same alias resolves for `load`, and marks it deferred.

title: SvelteKit action extraction
text:
# SvelteKit action extraction

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph extracts Svelte and SvelteKit template/composition flows, including exported-const object-of-functions SvelteKit actions. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 marks Svelte/SvelteKit already strong on realworld, skeleton, and shadcn, with template `{fn()}` calls, `<Pascal/>` composition, `import * as api` namespace, `load`→api, and exported-const object-of-functions extraction for `actions`.

title: SvelteKit extractor
text:
# SvelteKit extractor

Lifecycle status: accepted

The SvelteKit extractor is the CodeGraph surface for file-convention links between SvelteKit pages/layouts and their server load functions or actions. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 SvelteKit page/server load bullet.

title: SvelteKit route file convention links
text:
# SvelteKit route file convention links

Lifecycle status: accepted

SvelteKit pages and layouts are linked to sibling `load` functions and form `actions` by route-directory convention even without imports. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 SvelteKit pages and server load functions bullet.

title: Swappable telemetry backend
text:
# Swappable telemetry backend

Lifecycle status: accepted

The Worker isolates clients from the analytics backend, so replacing PostHog later is a Worker change rather than a client release. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Principles item 4 and Ingest endpoint section.

title: Swapped database reopen
text:
# Swapped database reopen

Lifecycle status: accepted

A long-running MCP server detects when the index database file is deleted and rebuilt at the same path, then reopens the live database in place. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says renamed or removed symbols no longer persist from an old deleted snapshot after `.codegraph/` is recreated on Linux and macOS.

title: Swift Fluent wrapper arguments
text:
# Swift Fluent wrapper arguments

Lifecycle status: accepted

Swift property-wrapper arguments now record dependencies on referenced model types such as Fluent many-to-many pivot models. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says `@Siblings(through: AcronymCategoryPivot.self, ...)` previously captured only the wrapper and declared property type, leaving pivot models orphaned.

title: Swift ObjC alias-name extraction
text:
# Swift ObjC alias-name extraction

Lifecycle status: proposed

Swift declarations should compute their auto-bridged Objective-C selector at extraction time and store it as an alternate name on the Swift method node, so normal Objective-C-side name resolution can find the Swift method without adding bridge-specific method-to-method edges. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#0 §4 says the cleanest Swift-Objective-C model is alias-name on the declaration node, with no new edges between Swift and ObjC method nodes needed.

title: Swift ObjC bridge resolver
text:
# Swift ObjC bridge resolver

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph resolves Swift and Objective-C selector calls across the language boundary using Apple's `@objc` name-bridging math, custom names, init forms, property accessor pairs, and reverse Cocoa preposition stripping. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks Swift x Objective-C done, citing Charts, realm-swift, wikipedia-ios validation and a generic-name blocklist with lower confidence than name-match ties.

title: Swift attribute dependency edges
text:
# Swift attribute dependency edges

Lifecycle status: accepted

Swift property wrappers and declaration attributes now record dependencies on their wrapper or attribute types. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says `@Argument`, `@Published`, `@State`, custom `@propertyWrapper`, and attributes like `@objc` or `@MainActor` were previously dropped, making wrapper types look unused and users depend on nothing.

title: Swift bare reference uniqueness gate
text:
# Swift bare reference uniqueness gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

Swift cross-file bare callback references may resolve only when repo-unique, and methods stay enclosing-type-only, because Swift sees module-wide symbols without imports. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits documents the repo-unique function rule and says cross-type `#selector` targets are scoped away.

title: Swift generic bridge misses
text:
# Swift generic bridge misses

Lifecycle status: proposed

Swift-only generics over Objective-C protocols can be silently missed by the native bridge plan, while `@objc` Swift extensions on ObjC classes still follow the Phase 1 path. Evidence: docs/design/mixed-ios-and-react-native-bridging.md#1 §7 says Swift-only generics over ObjC protocols are not handled and silently missed, while `@objc` extension methods use the same Phase 1 path; this is acceptable and matches the Java/Kotlin generics frontier.

title: Swift same-class parameter residual
text:
# Swift same-class parameter residual

Lifecycle status: accepted

Swift function-reference capture still cannot distinguish a parameter named after a method of the same enclosing type from an implicit-self method value, even after enclosing-type scoping removed cross-class collisions. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#1 Known limits says the Swift scoping change removed 44 wrong Alamofire edges but leaves same-type parameter collisions statically indistinguishable and documented.

title: Swift static stored constants
text:
# Swift static stored constants

Lifecycle status: accepted

Swift value-reference support treats top-level `let` and type-level `static let` as shared constants, widens the target gate to `struct:` and `enum:` parents, and skips computed properties. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §2 says Swift reused the Kotlin nested-name path, widened target parents for struct/enum constants, left instance `let` as field, and skipped `computed_property` children.

title: Symbol documentation coverage
text:
# Symbol documentation coverage

Lifecycle status: accepted

Symbol documentation should be captured for exported, const-assigned, and decorated declarations rather than only for plain declarations. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 says comments above `export class`, `export const`, plain `const` functions, and decorated Python defs/classes were previously dropped and are now found through wrappers.

title: Symlink realpath root confinement
text:
# Symlink realpath root confinement

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph resolves symlinks during file-access validation and refuses to serve any file whose real location is outside the indexed project root, while still allowing symlinks that remain within the project. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 1.0.0 Security.

title: Symlinked SDK project indexing
text:
# Symlinked SDK project indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Projects that keep in-repo directories as symlinks to external SDK locations must still be indexable. CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes cites Dota 2 custom games and similar SDK-linked layouts where `game/` and `content/` point into an engine tree.

title: Synth edges need endpoint surfacing
text:
# Synth edges need endpoint surfacing

Lifecycle status: accepted

A synthesized edge can be correct but still useless to agents if its endpoint kinds never enter the explore flow-surfacing path. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#2 redux-thunk follow-up 2 says constant-to-constant thunk edges existed but fell through both Flow and Relationships surfacing paths on small repos.

title: Synthesized dispatch hop surfacing
text:
# Synthesized dispatch hop surfacing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Synthesized dispatch hops must surface in explore Flow output even when the endpoints are non-callable nodes such as constants, variables, or fields. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#2 redux-thunk follow-up 2 says redux-thunk constant-to-constant edges were invisible because Flow scanned only callables and Relationships were hidden below 500 files.

title: Synthesized impl sibling signal
text:
# Synthesized impl sibling signal

Lifecycle status: accepted

Relying on `synthesizedBy:'interface-impl'` edges for sibling detection misses real polymorphic families when those synthetic edges are absent. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Dead ends item 3 says those edges were not created for OkHttp's Kotlin `fun interface` `Interceptor`, so the sibling signal must come from real `implements` and `extends` edges.

title: TS JS class field properties
text:
# TS JS class field properties

Lifecycle status: accepted

TypeScript and JavaScript class fields are reported as properties unless they hold arrow functions or function expressions, preventing data fields from absorbing same-named call edges while preserving callable field methods. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 TypeScript/JavaScript class fields bullet.

title: TS imports stay in language family
text:
# TS imports stay in language family

Lifecycle status: accepted

TypeScript and JavaScript references or imports no longer resolve to same-named classes in native languages, while genuine JS-native bridge edges remain enabled. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 TypeScript `TestRunner` / Swift `React` bullet.

title: TS value-reference dependencies
text:
# TS value-reference dependencies

Lifecycle status: accepted

TypeScript/JavaScript symbols count as dependencies when used in function-body type annotations, registry arrays, arguments, JSX, barrel re-exports, or namespace imports, including tsconfig path aliases. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 TypeScript dependency completeness bullet.

title: TSX JSX value refs
text:
# TSX JSX value refs

Lifecycle status: accepted

TSX value-reference coverage is handled by the TypeScript value-ref path, including const reads that occur only inside JSX subtrees. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#3 says excalidraw is a React/.tsx codebase covered by the TS rows, the JSX-only path relies on reader-scan descent into JSX, and `value-reference-edges.test.ts` locks it so no separate tsx repo sweep is needed.

title: Task 6 resolver extract rollout
text:
# Task 6 resolver extract rollout

Lifecycle status: superseded

Port the remaining server framework resolvers in Task 6 to the shared `extract(filePath, content): { nodes, references }` pattern, adding `languages`, route nodes, handler `UnresolvedRef` entries, and at least one unit test per framework. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#3 Task 6 lists Laravel, Rails, Spring, Gin/chi/gorilla, Axum/actix, ASP.NET, and Swift/Vapor with the same node-plus-reference pattern and one framework test each.

title: Team-shared custom extension indexing
text:
# Team-shared custom extension indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Teams should be able to teach CodeGraph about project-specific file extensions in a committed repo-local form so everyone indexes those files consistently. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#10 says a repo-root `codegraph.json` with an `extensions` map is opt-in and committed alongside code so the whole team shares mappings such as `.dota_lua` to Lua or `.tpl` to PHP.

title: Telemetry CLI
text:
# Telemetry CLI

Lifecycle status: accepted

The `codegraph telemetry` CLI exposes user-facing telemetry status/on/off controls and reports the current machine ID, state, and deciding source. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Status and Consent & controls sections.

title: Telemetry allowlist contract
text:
# Telemetry allowlist contract

Lifecycle status: accepted

The telemetry design doc and TELEMETRY.md form a field-by-field allowlist contract, and implementation must never collect anything outside that list. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 opening contract paragraph and Principles item 1.

title: Telemetry client
text:
# Telemetry client

Lifecycle status: accepted

The telemetry client is the `src/telemetry/` module that records counters, persists a bounded local queue, and flushes anonymous batches. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Status and Client architecture sections.

title: Telemetry consent resolution
text:
# Telemetry consent resolution

Lifecycle status: accepted

Telemetry enablement is resolved in priority order: DO_NOT_TRACK, CODEGRAPH_TELEMETRY, global telemetry config, then default-on gated by first-run notice, with installer and CLI surfaces persisting user choice. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Consent & controls section.

title: Telemetry ingest Worker
text:
# Telemetry ingest Worker

Lifecycle status: accepted

The telemetry ingest Worker is the public `telemetry-worker/` Cloudflare Worker endpoint that validates telemetry and forwards allowed anonymous events to the backend. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Status and Ingest endpoint sections.

title: Telemetry off deletes buffers
text:
# Telemetry off deletes buffers

Lifecycle status: accepted

When telemetry is disabled, CodeGraph must record nothing, send nothing, and delete buffered telemetry data. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 telemetry bullet says off means off and buffered data is deleted.

title: Telemetry reset rotates machine ID
text:
# Telemetry reset rotates machine ID

Lifecycle status: accepted

Deleting `~/.codegraph/telemetry.json` resets telemetry state, including the random anonymous machine ID. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Consent & controls CLI paragraph.

title: Telemetry schema allowlist
text:
# Telemetry schema allowlist

Lifecycle status: accepted

The telemetry schema is the allowlist: clients send only documented events, the Worker validates the same allowlist, and unknown events or properties are dropped or stripped. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Principles item 1 and Ingest endpoint section.

title: Telemetry user control
text:
# Telemetry user control

Lifecycle status: accepted

Users need clear telemetry controls, including opt-out by standard environment variables, explicit process overrides, persisted config, installer choice, first-run notice, and CLI status/on/off. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Consent & controls section.

title: Template graph shape stability
text:
# Template graph shape stability

Lifecycle status: accepted

Template extraction must emit one component node per template file, use references edges for tags, avoid per-tag node explosion, and be idempotent across re-indexes. Evidence: docs/design/template-markup-parser.md#0 Node/edge shape & invariants section states +1 component node per template file, no per-tag node explosion, all edges are references, and stable node count across re-runs.

title: Template markup parser
text:
# Template markup parser

Lifecycle status: accepted

The template markup parser is the CodeGraph extraction surface for Razor and Blazor markup files, centered on `src/extraction/razor-extractor.ts` and wired through `grammars.ts` and `tree-sitter.ts`. Evidence: docs/design/template-markup-parser.md#0 Architecture names those files and says Razor/Blazor markup is parsed by `src/extraction/razor-extractor.ts`.

title: Template-only dependent reachability
text:
# Template-only dependent reachability

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph needs dependencies that appear only in template markup to count as in-repo dependents, otherwise code-behind, components, view-models, and DTOs referenced only from markup look unused. Evidence: docs/design/template-markup-parser.md#0 Problem states template markup was not parsed, making markup-only references look like they had no in-repo dependent.

title: This-member callback resolution
text:
# This-member callback resolution

Lifecycle status: accepted

TypeScript and JavaScript callback registrations through `this.<member>` now resolve to the enclosing class's own method, never a same-named unrelated method or data field. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 callback registration through `this` bullet.

title: Thymeleaf Django template deferral
text:
# Thymeleaf Django template deferral

Lifecycle status: proposed

Thymeleaf and Django template extraction is deferred because those template links are weak and their measured framework gaps come mostly from other mechanisms. Evidence: docs/design/template-markup-parser.md#0 Problem and Phasing say Thymeleaf/Django are P4, deferred/probably skipped, with weak template-to-code links and real gaps elsewhere.

title: Tool calls may await daemon
text:
# Tool calls may await daemon

Lifecycle status: proposed

Decoupling `tools/list` must still let actual MCP tool calls resolve or wait on the daemon connection in the background. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says to advertise static tools immediately and resolve the daemon in the background for actual tool calls.

title: Trace endpoint node relevance
text:
# Trace endpoint node relevance

Lifecycle status: accepted

Endpoint pair scoring added node relevance to penalize empty stubs and test-file symbols so overloaded names resolve to real methods instead of protocol or delegate stubs. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 3d says `handleTrace` added a `nodeRelevance` term penalizing empty stubs and test-file symbols after Alamofire traces resolved `request` to a no-op protocol/delegate stub over the real `Session.request`.

title: Trace flow dossier
text:
# Trace flow dossier

Lifecycle status: superseded

`codegraph_trace` returns a self-contained flow dossier where each hop includes its full body plus the destination's outgoing calls, so one trace often answers how X reaches Y without follow-up explore, node, or Read. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 New Features.

title: Trace from concrete methods
text:
# Trace from concrete methods

Lifecycle status: accepted

When trace names are common, start from the specific method node rather than a class name or broad symbol because trace can choose the wrong matching node. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#6 warns that common names such as `render` and `execute_sql` match many nodes, trace may start from the wrong one, and users should trace from the specific method rather than a class name.

title: Trace wrongness masquerades as adoption floor
text:
# Trace wrongness masquerades as adoption floor

Lifecycle status: accepted

A small repo read-heavy result can be a fixable trace endpoint bug rather than an adoption floor; compare what the agent read with the tool output immediately before it. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Section 3d says Alamofire was misread as the small-repo floor until transcripts showed the tool returned wrong stub endpoints, and the methodology lesson says transcript reasoning, not the median, tells which case it is.

title: Tree-sitter callback arg recovery
text:
# Tree-sitter callback arg recovery

Lifecycle status: proposed

Field-channel registration argument recovery should use tree-sitter rather than regex so arrows, multi-argument calls, and line-wrapped calls are robustly handled. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work item 4 calls for replacing the Stage 4 regex with tree-sitter arg recovery.

title: Tree-sitter extraction walker
text:
# Tree-sitter extraction walker

Lifecycle status: accepted

The shared `tree-sitter.ts` walker is the CodeGraph extraction surface where named inline callback extraction and similar cross-language node-emission changes can affect many languages. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#6 says Phase-3 named-inline-callback extraction is in the shared `tree-sitter.ts` walker.

title: Tree-sitter registration arg recovery
text:
# Tree-sitter registration arg recovery

Lifecycle status: proposed

Field-channel registration recovery should replace the regex with tree-sitter parsing. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 Remaining work item 4 says this is needed for arrows, multi-argument calls, and line-wrapped calls.

title: Trezor barrel namespace deferral
text:
# Trezor barrel namespace deferral

Lifecycle status: deprecated

CodeGraph deliberately shelves the cross-file barrel-namespace dispatch synthesizer because discovery found only one independent design lineage and meaningful implementation complexity for a single-lineage win. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#2 Immediate next actions says the strict shape appears in trezor-suite and OneKey hardware-js-sdk, but OneKey is a @trezor/connect fork, while 15 diverse repos and GitHub-wide search disproved broader coverage.

title: Trezor facade skip
text:
# Trezor facade skip

Lifecycle status: deprecated

CodeGraph skips the trezor connect-common/factory facade because it is low-value: it has a single call fan-in and does not disambiguate per-method targets. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#2 Immediate next actions says the facade remains low-value and should be skipped.

title: TurboModule spec resolver
text:
# TurboModule spec resolver

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph partially resolves React Native TurboModule JS specs by parsing `TurboModuleRegistry.get*<Spec>('Name')` and matching Spec interface methods to native implementations by ObjC selector first-keyword or JVM identifier. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#3 marks TurboModules partial, validating react-native-svg 9 precise bridges while noting iOS Codegen-generated impls without legacy macros remain a frontier.

title: Type reference edge coverage
text:
# Type reference edge coverage

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph emits reference edges for types used in TypeScript interface property/method signatures and C# parameter, return, property, and field types, so callers/impact on DTO and service types include shape-only consumers. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 releases 0.9.5 and 0.9.6 Fixes.

title: Type-alias search filter
text:
# Type-alias search filter

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_search` implements its schema-advertised `kind: "type"` filter by returning type aliases instead of silently matching nothing. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 `codegraph_search` type filter bullet.

title: Type-anchored method references
text:
# Type-anchored method references

Lifecycle status: accepted

Java/Kotlin same-package references, Kotlin companion-object members, and cross-file C++ member pointers now resolve through the named type, never a same-named member on another class. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 method references to a type needing no import bullet.

title: TypeScript RPC tuple symbols
text:
# TypeScript RPC tuple symbols

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph indexes each string-literal service name in TypeScript service/RPC contracts defined as tuples of generic `Service<...>` types, while deliberately leaving utility types and route paths out. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features TypeScript service/RPC contracts bullet.

title: TypeScript contract noise guard
text:
# TypeScript contract noise guard

Lifecycle status: accepted

TypeScript type-level symbol extraction must leave utility types such as `Pick`, `Omit`, and `Record`, plus route paths, out of searchable symbols to avoid noise. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features TypeScript service/RPC contracts bullet.

title: TypeScript extractor
text:
# TypeScript extractor

Lifecycle status: accepted

The TypeScript extractor is the CodeGraph indexing surface for TypeScript symbols, including type-level API contract patterns. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features TypeScript service/RPC contracts bullet.

title: TypeScript module extension indexing
text:
# TypeScript module extension indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph indexes `.mts` and `.cts` TypeScript module files. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says TypeScript `.mts` and `.cts` files are now indexed instead of skipped.

title: TypeScript recall regression
text:
# TypeScript recall regression

Lifecycle status: accepted

TypeScript support was precision-positive but recall-negative: missing declared factory return annotations dropped existing bare-name edges while adding no real-repo edges. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 Why TypeScript was skipped says Nest regressed by -164, mostly `Test.createTestingModule(...).compile()`, with +0 added on typeorm and nest.

title: Typed RPC surface searchability
text:
# Typed RPC surface searchability

Lifecycle status: accepted

Typed RPC and BFF clients need service names encoded in TypeScript type declarations to be searchable because those type names are the app's primary API surface and source of truth for runtime proxies. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features TypeScript service/RPC contracts bullet.

title: UI resolver extract rollout shipped
text:
# UI resolver extract rollout shipped

Lifecycle status: accepted

React Router and SvelteKit resolvers were migrated to the shared `extract()` contract; handler references are emitted where supported, while React Router element-to-component handler edges remain a documented follow-up. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#4 Fix lists React Router and SvelteKit among the 13 updated resolvers, and Known gaps says React Router `<Route element={<Page/>}/>` handler edges remain follow-up work.

title: UI resolver node-only migration
text:
# UI resolver node-only migration

Lifecycle status: superseded

React and Svelte route resolvers should migrate to the new `extract()` interface while preserving existing node-only behavior by returning `{ nodes, references: [] }`; component references are left as follow-up work. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#3 Task 6h says UI frameworks map routes to components rather than server handlers, so keep existing behavior, add languages, rename `extractNodes` to `extract`, and return empty references.

title: Ungated local function-ref matching
text:
# Ungated local function-ref matching

Lifecycle status: accepted

Ungated local RHS and variable-initializer matching is an anti-pattern because ordinary locals can collide with unique same-named functions elsewhere and create wrong callback-registration edges. Evidence: docs/design/function-ref-capture.md#0 Precision rule 2 says `prev = next`, `*str = field`, and `arena_ind_prev = arena_ind` in redis/jemalloc produced wrong edges when RHS/varinit were ungated.

title: Unicode directory traversal
text:
# Unicode directory traversal

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph indexes files under directories with non-ASCII names instead of silently skipping them. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says directories with names such as CJK characters are no longer skipped during indexing.

title: Uninstall preserves user edits
text:
# Uninstall preserves user edits

Lifecycle status: accepted

Uninstall paths must remove CodeGraph-owned config without deleting content the user added outside CodeGraph markers. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.3 says Cursor uninstall deletes `.cursor/rules/codegraph.mdc` while keeping any content added outside CodeGraph markers, and the new uninstall command removes only what install wrote.

title: Universal dynamic-dispatch coverage
text:
# Universal dynamic-dispatch coverage

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph should close dynamic-dispatch static-extraction coverage holes across every supported language and framework so cross-symbol flows exist in the graph everywhere. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#0 Mission says to systematically close dynamic dispatch holes across every language and framework CodeGraph supports and validate each one the same way.

title: Upgrade command
text:
# Upgrade command

Lifecycle status: accepted

The `codegraph upgrade` command updates installed CodeGraph releases in place across standalone, npm, and npx install modes. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#3 upgrade bullet.

title: Validate on two pattern repos
text:
# Validate on two pattern repos

Lifecycle status: accepted

Every dispatch synthesizer must be built and validated against at least two real repositories that actually contain the target pattern. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Discipline item 1 says to build against at least two real repos that contain the pattern and that a synthesizer validated on one repo is unvalidated.

title: Validate startup by actual use
text:
# Validate startup by actual use

Lifecycle status: accepted

Startup fixes must be validated by timing `serve --mcp` `tools/list` and by counting cold-start runs where CodeGraph is connected with tools and actually called; a single pending init snapshot is insufficient. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 gives this validation method and warns to confirm actual CodeGraph usage.

title: Validate with real-agent A/B
text:
# Validate with real-agent A/B

Lifecycle status: accepted

Adaptive explore skeletonization changes must be confirmed with real-agent A/B runs, not only deterministic probe queries. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Dead ends item 6 says the probe and the agent's real explore query name symbols differently, so they form different spines and skeletonize different files; it says always confirm with `run-all.sh`.

title: Validation before chained edges
text:
# Validation before chained edges

Lifecycle status: accepted

Chained-call resolution must validate that the outer method exists on the inferred return type or a conforming supertype; a wrong or unknown inference must yield no edge. Evidence: docs/design/chained-call-resolution.md#0 says every resolver ends in `resolveMethodOnType`, so wrong inference yields no edge, never a wrong one.

title: Value-reader impact reachability
text:
# Value-reader impact reachability

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph needs dependency visibility from a file-scope constant, config object, or lookup table to the same-file symbols that read it, because calls/imports/inheritance edges miss this change-impact class. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §1 says const consumers used to look like nothing depends on this and value-reference edges exist so impact analysis catches constant/config/lookup-table changes.

title: Value-ref PR workflow
text:
# Value-ref PR workflow

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-reference validation and precision work must follow the documented PR hygiene: branch from main, keep pure validation docs/test changes separate from focused precision code fixes when practical, put user-facing changelog entries under Unreleased, include the specified generated-by trailers, and leave merge decisions to the maintainer. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §6 lists the branch, PR split, commit trailer, PR body trailer, maintainer-merge rule, admin squash note, and changelog placement.

title: Value-ref agents need impact calls
text:
# Value-ref agents need impact calls

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-reference edges do not reduce agent reads unless the agent calls an edge-traversing tool such as `impact` or `explore`; the durable win is blast-radius correctness exposed through `getImpactRadius`. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#3 Agent A/B says indexed-repo runs used one codegraph call with 0 Read/0 Grep in both arms, often called `codegraph_search`/`callers` instead of `impact`/`explore`, and explicitly says not to claim value-refs reduce agent reads.

title: Value-ref env opt-out
text:
# Value-ref env opt-out

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-reference emission must remain disableable with `CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS=0` even though it is default-on. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges.md#0 Status says the shipped feature is default-on for the supported language set and that `CODEGRAPH_VALUE_REFS=0` disables it.

title: Value-ref extractor kind check
text:
# Value-ref extractor kind check

Lifecycle status: accepted

A value-reference language extension must confirm that sample module-level constants are emitted as `constant` or `variable` before relying on the target gate. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5C says `captureValueRefScope` keys targets off `kind in {constant, variable}` and instructs agents to query indexed sample nodes, adjusting the target gate if constants instead emit as `field`, `property`, `import`, or another kind.

title: Value-ref false-positive handling
text:
# Value-ref false-positive handling

Lifecycle status: accepted

During value-reference validation, false-positive clusters must be fixed while isolated singletons are recorded as known residuals. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §0 instructs agents to hunt FPs during the validation sweep, fix FP clusters, and record singletons.

title: Value-ref impact-radius correction
text:
# Value-ref impact-radius correction

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-reference edges improve impact-radius correctness by turning constants read by many symbols from a single affected node into the actual reader set; the documented win is correctness, not agent read reduction. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §1 says a const read by 90 symbols goes from 1 affected to 90 and explicitly says the win is impact-radius correctness, not agent read-reduction.

title: Value-ref parent-kind gate
text:
# Value-ref parent-kind gate

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-reference targets must register only under shared-scope parents accepted by the target gate: file, class, module, struct, or enum. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5A says the target gate now accepts `file:`, `class:`, `module:`, `struct:`, and `enum:` parents, and warns that a missing parent kind makes a language silently emit no value-reference edges even when constant nodes exist.

title: Value-ref public OSS validation
text:
# Value-ref public OSS validation

Lifecycle status: accepted

Value-reference language extensions must be validated on small, medium, and large public open-source repositories for that language, never on the maintainer's own repos. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §0 requires the validation sweep on S/M/L public OSS repos and states the hard scope rule to never eval on maintainer-owned repos.

title: Value-ref validation invariants
text:
# Value-ref validation invariants

Lifecycle status: accepted

A value-reference language extension must keep node counts identical on/off, hold precision guards, reproduce the impact-radius win, add a matrix row, and add a test case. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §0 and §2 require the validation sweep, matrix update, tests, node parity, precision guards, and impact-win reproduction.

title: Value-ref wiring check is load-bearing
text:
# Value-ref wiring check is load-bearing

Lifecycle status: accepted

Adding value-reference coverage for a language must start by checking the language's declarator node types and file/class/module scope behavior, because a wrong node type or scope assumption can make the feature silently emit nothing or emit wrong edges. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §0 says §5 steps A-C are where languages differ, where most real decisions are, and must not be skipped.

title: Value-reference edge capture
text:
# Value-reference edge capture

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph emits same-file `references` edges with `metadata.valueRef: true` from reader symbols to file-scope `const`/`var` targets, and feeds them through the existing impact-radius/reference traversal path without agent-behavior changes. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#0 §1 defines the edge shape, same-file scope, and flow into `getImpactRadius`, `codegraph impact`, `codegraph_explore`, and `codegraph_node`.

title: Vapor route extraction
text:
# Vapor route extraction

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph rewrote Swift Vapor route extraction to handle grouped builders, optional/non-string path segments, grouped prefixes, and `use:` handlers instead of requiring app/router/routes receivers and a string path literal. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 says Vapor was previously 0 routes on real apps, then any receiver, optional/non-string path segments, `.grouped`/`.group{}` prefix tracking, and `use:` discrimination produced vapor-template 0→3, SteamPress 0→27, and SwiftPackageIndex-Server 0→14 with full handler resolution.

title: Version command aliases
text:
# Version command aliases

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph accepts `codegraph version`, `codegraph -v`, and `codegraph -version` in addition to `codegraph --version`. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says checking the installed version is easy to reach however users guess at it.

title: Vue Nuxt extractor
text:
# Vue Nuxt extractor

Lifecycle status: accepted

The Vue/Nuxt extractor is the CodeGraph surface for Vue template component usage and Nuxt component auto-import naming conventions. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 Nuxt nested components bullet.

title: Vue composable handler aliases
text:
# Vue composable handler aliases

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph resolves Vue template handlers that are aliases from destructured composable returns when the returned function is defined in the composable file. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 says composable-destructure handlers are resolved for `@click="closeSidebar"` via alias to composable returned `close`, dropping the vitepress sidebar flow from 6 to 0 reads, with no fallback to the composable itself.

title: Vue prefix kebab frontier
text:
# Vue prefix kebab frontier

Lifecycle status: proposed

CodeGraph still needs a safe way to resolve Vue prefix-convention kebab components such as Element Plus `el-button` when the implementation component is named `button` rather than `ElButton`. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 says PascalCase is covered but prefix-convention kebab remains unresolved for element-plus.

title: Vue store extraction foundation
text:
# Vue store extraction foundation

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph shipped Vuex/Pinia extraction foundations that create store action, mutation, and getter nodes for several Vuex and Pinia store shapes before dispatch bridging. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Tier A marks the Vuex/Pinia extraction foundation shipped on 2026-06-20 and says codegraph_node can find store actions such as login and getSessionList.

title: Vue store split-file gap
text:
# Vue store split-file gap

Lifecycle status: accepted

The shipped Vue store work still leaves Vuex split-file export-default dispatch plus computed-key constant-string resolution deferred. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Vuex/Pinia row says vue2-elm form-2 and computed-key support are deferred because n=1 needs export-default dispatch and const-string resolution.

title: Vue stores are multiple shapes
text:
# Vue stores are multiple shapes

Lifecycle status: accepted

Vuex and Pinia dispatch coverage is not one clean string-keyed shape; it splits across Vuex modules, split-file computed keys, Pinia options stores, Pinia setup stores, and useStore instance dispatch. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Vuex/Pinia row says the corpus probe found about five shapes and enumerates them.

title: Vue template component usages
text:
# Vue template component usages

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph indexes Vue Single-File Component template tags as component usages, including PascalCase and kebab-case forms. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says `codegraph_callers` and `codegraph_impact` now include components used only in another component's markup, including through barrel re-exports.

title: Vue template flow extraction
text:
# Vue template flow extraction

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph covers Vue template events and component composition across representative Vue repositories. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#2 marks Vue/Nuxt events plus composition done on vitepress, vben, and element-plus, while explicitly deferring vue-core Proxy reactive→render runtime behavior as a frontier.

title: Vuex string-key dispatch bridge
text:
# Vuex string-key dispatch bridge

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph shipped vuexDispatchEdges to bridge string-key store.dispatch and commit calls to Vuex action and mutation nodes, resolving namespaced paths to store-file targets. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Vuex/Pinia row says the Vuex string-key dispatch bridge shipped on 2026-06-20 with synthesizedBy:'vuex-dispatch', namespace routing, store-file gating, and tests.

title: WSL mnt watcher auto-skip
text:
# WSL mnt watcher auto-skip

Lifecycle status: accepted

On WSL2 `/mnt/*` drives, CodeGraph skips the live file watcher and offers git hooks/manual sync so slow watchers do not break MCP startup. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.8.0 says WSL `/mnt/*` watcher is skipped, git hooks can keep the index fresh, and env/CLI flags force or disable watching.

title: Watch sync pipeline
text:
# Watch sync pipeline

Lifecycle status: accepted

The watch sync pipeline is CodeGraph's file-watcher and incremental synchronization layer that keeps the index aligned with filesystem edits, git pulls, branch switches, and MCP reconnects. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 releases 0.9.5 and 0.9.6 describe watcher excludes, filesystem-based change detection, catch-up on connect, debounce tuning, and stale-lock handling.

title: Watch sync stale-edge tolerance
text:
# Watch sync stale-edge tolerance

Lifecycle status: accepted

Watch sync drops a single stale edge instead of aborting the whole daemon sync with a `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` error. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.6 Fixes.

title: Watcher cost stays flat
text:
# Watcher cost stays flat

Lifecycle status: accepted

The recursive and bounded watcher design keeps CodeGraph's background watch cost flat with project size and avoids machine-wide file-descriptor exhaustion. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says unrelated apps previously failed after the watcher piled up tens of thousands of handles, and the new strategy keeps cost flat regardless of project size.

title: Watcher debounce tuning
text:
# Watcher debounce tuning

Lifecycle status: accepted

`CODEGRAPH_WATCH_DEBOUNCE_MS` lets users tune the file-watcher quiet window, defaulting to 2000ms, for bursty write workflows such as format-on-save chains and generated outputs. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 New Features.

title: Watcher excludes ignored paths
text:
# Watcher excludes ignored paths

Lifecycle status: accepted

The file watcher excludes the same default and `.gitignore` directories as the indexer before registering watches, preventing large repos from exhausting OS watch budgets. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 Fixes.

title: Watcher resource cost bounded
text:
# Watcher resource cost bounded

Lifecycle status: accepted

The background file watcher must keep operating-system file-handle and watch-resource use bounded so CodeGraph cannot exhaust machine-wide limits on large projects. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#7 says the macOS watcher previously kept one open file handle per watched file and could cause unrelated apps to fail with too many open files.

title: Whole-file family skeletonization
text:
# Whole-file family skeletonization

Lifecycle status: accepted

The current adaptive explore implementation skeletonizes family files as whole files to shrink sibling-heavy output; per-symbol family skeletonization is not yet expressible and remains future work. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Frontier says `compiler.py` is skeletonized whole, causing `SQLCompiler.execute_sql` to become a signature and be Read back in about half the Django runs, and says whole-file skeletonization cannot express the ideal per-symbol behavior yet.

title: Whole-file family skeletonization
text:
# Whole-file family skeletonization

Lifecycle status: superseded

The current adaptive explore implementation skeletonizes family files as whole files; per-symbol family skeletonization is not yet expressible and remains future work. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#1 Frontier says `compiler.py` is skeletonized whole, causing `SQLCompiler.execute_sql` to become a signature and be Read back in about half the Django runs, and says whole-file skeletonization cannot express the ideal per-symbol behavior yet.

title: Whole-file shadow over-pruning
text:
# Whole-file shadow over-pruning

Lifecycle status: accepted

The value-reference shadow prune intentionally favors precision by dropping a shadowed target for the whole file, which can lose a legitimate edge from another reader in that file. Evidence: docs/design/value-reference-edges-playbook.md#2 §5B says this is inherited from TS/JS, and the Go sweep found over-pruning negligible enough that per-reader analysis was not worth adding, but the trade-off should be rechecked per language.

title: Whole-graph callback synthesis
text:
# Whole-graph callback synthesis

Lifecycle status: superseded

Callback dispatch is handled as a whole-graph pass after base resolution rather than as `FrameworkResolver.resolve()`. Evidence: docs/design/callback-edge-synthesis.md#0 says `cb()` has no named ref to resolve and needs cross-file multi-site correlation, so the pass lives in `src/resolution/callback-synthesizer.ts`, not under `frameworks/`.

title: Whole-method explore truncation
text:
# Whole-method explore truncation

Lifecycle status: accepted

When `codegraph_explore` hits its response budget, it drops whole methods or files and reports the omissions instead of cutting off a method body partway through. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#2 release 0.9.9 Fixes.

title: Windows parent-exit helper shutdown
text:
# Windows parent-exit helper shutdown

Lifecycle status: accepted

On Windows, CodeGraph helpers detect parent-process exit directly so helpers and the idle shared background server wind down promptly. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 Windows background processes bullet.

title: Wording is low salience
text:
# Wording is low salience

Lifecycle status: accepted

Changing tool descriptions or server instructions alone is an unreliable way to move agent tool choice and has regressed wall-clock before. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 states this doctrine constraint and the clean A/B showed steering moved some tool choice but still left five Reads and no file-view use.

title: Worker-mediated PostHog ingest
text:
# Worker-mediated PostHog ingest

Lifecycle status: accepted

Telemetry is ingested through the first-party Cloudflare Worker, which validates allowlisted events, strips unknown properties, never forwards or logs client IP, rate-limits by machine ID, and forwards to PostHog Cloud US. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Ingest endpoint section.

title: Worker-safe framework transfer
text:
# Worker-safe framework transfer

Lifecycle status: proposed
