Framework resolver objects with functions must not be sent through `worker_threads` postMessage; pass framework names and re-resolve resolver objects inside the worker instead. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-04-24-framework-resolver-extract.md#3 Task 7 Step 3 says objects with functions cannot cross worker_threads boundaries and instructs passing detected names then filtering `getAllFrameworkResolvers()` in the worker.

title: Workspace repository indexer
text:
# Workspace repository indexer

Lifecycle status: accepted

The workspace repository indexer is the CodeGraph init/sync/watch surface that discovers and indexes multiple nested git repositories under one workspace root. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#4 New Features multi-repository workspace bullet.

title: Worktree duplicate exclusion
text:
# Worktree duplicate exclusion

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph recognizes git worktrees nested inside a project and skips them as duplicate working views while still indexing real embedded repos and submodules. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says `.claude/worktrees/` could multiply every symbol and one report grew from about 1,850 files to over 24,000.

title: Worktree index conflict detection
text:
# Worktree index conflict detection

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph no longer silently borrows another git worktree's index; status and read tools now call out the conflict and point users to `codegraph init -i` in the worktree. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.5 Fixes.

title: Wrapped React component detection
text:
# Wrapped React component detection

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph recognizes React components declared through `forwardRef`, `memo`, styled-components, and emotion wrappers as components. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says usages like `<Button/>` now link back to wrapped declarations so callers and blast radius are complete for typical shadcn/ui-style design systems.

title: Wrapped declaration doc comments
text:
# Wrapped declaration doc comments

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph now follows export, const-assignment, and decorator wrapper nodes to attach preceding doc comments to the wrapped symbol. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 doc-comment bullet covering `export class`, `export const`, plain `const` functions, and decorated Python `def`/`class` declarations.

title: Wrong edge drops silently
text:
# Wrong edge drops silently

Lifecycle status: accepted

When CodeGraph cannot prove a candidate dependency belongs to the correct receiver, language family, source set, or file scope, it should emit no edge instead of a misleading one. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 C++ wrong guess produces no edge, type references stay within language families, and quoted includes/source sets prefer the correct local target.

title: XSJS JavaScript indexing
text:
# XSJS JavaScript indexing

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph treats SAP HANA `.xsjs` and `.xsjslib` files as JavaScript for indexing. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#8 says those files are now indexed as JavaScript instead of being skipped.

title: Yielding startup reconcile
text:
# Yielding startup reconcile

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph startup reconcile yields while running and gates the first tool call only briefly. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#11 Fixes says huge repositories no longer hang the first MCP call; the reconcile keeps the server responsive, waits up to `CODEGRAPH_CATCHUP_GATE_TIMEOUT_MS` by default, and finishes in the background.

title: Zero-config ignore semantics
text:
# Zero-config ignore semantics

Lifecycle status: accepted

Users should control CodeGraph indexing through existing ignore conventions rather than a separate CodeGraph config surface. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.2 says `.gitignore` is the single source of truth for what gets indexed and indexing is zero-config.

title: Zero-cost telemetry path
text:
# Zero-cost telemetry path

Lifecycle status: accepted

Telemetry may never add MCP hot-path latency, npm dependencies, stdout bytes, retries, or user-visible error noise; every failure mode is silence. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 Principles item 2.

title: Zero-edge non-pattern controls
text:
# Zero-edge non-pattern controls

Lifecycle status: accepted

Every dispatch synthesizer must produce zero edges on a control repository that lacks the target shape while producing precise non-zero edges on at least two repositories that have it. Evidence: docs/design/dispatch-synthesizer-backlog.md#0 Discipline item 3 says redux-thunk's zero on shapeshift was good and every synthesizer below must meet the same control and positive-repo bar.

title: claimsReference pre-filter hook
text:
# claimsReference pre-filter hook

Lifecycle status: accepted

Framework-specific route or ORM references may need a `claimsReference` hook so `resolveOne` does not discard references before framework `resolve()` can interpret them. Evidence: docs/design/dynamic-dispatch-coverage-playbook.md#4 says Rails `articles#index` names no declared symbol, so the pre-filter dropped it until Rails used the same claim hook as the Django ORM work.

title: codegraph-pro telemetry enablement
text:
# codegraph-pro telemetry enablement

Lifecycle status: accepted

Allowing installer-enableable telemetry in the private codegraph-pro fork is an anti-pattern because customer containers guarantee nothing leaves the box. Evidence: docs/design/telemetry.md#0 codegraph-pro rule.

title: codegraph_affected
text:
# codegraph_affected

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_affected` is the CodeGraph command/tool surface that traces changed files to tests and files depending on them. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#6 affected command bullets.

title: codegraph_context
text:
# codegraph_context

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_context` is the MCP context tool surface whose temp-dir marker write had to be hardened against symlink redirection. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.9.2 Security names the temp-dir marker written on each `codegraph_context` call.

title: codegraph_explore
text:
# codegraph_explore

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_explore` is the CodeGraph exploration surface whose output sizing and rendering policy are governed by the adaptive sibling-skeletonization design. Evidence: docs/design/adaptive-explore-sizing.md#0 names `codegraph_explore` throughout as the component being changed.

title: codegraph_node
text:
# codegraph_node

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_node` is the CodeGraph MCP node-inspection surface for returning source and symbol details. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 says `codegraph_node` and `codegraph_trace` now emit line-numbered source.

title: codegraph_node
text:
# codegraph_node

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_node` is the MCP tool surface for retrieving node details and source-oriented summaries, including the release 0.8.0 class/interface/struct/enum member outline behavior. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.8.0 says `codegraph_node` returns compact member outlines for type nodes while functions and methods return full source.

title: codegraph_node file view
text:
# codegraph_node file view

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_node` file-view mode is the MCP tool surface for reading indexed source files by passing a bare `file` with no `symbol`. Evidence: docs/design/agent-codegraph-adoption.md#0 says #733 added file-view mode in `src/mcp/tools.ts`, with `handleFileView` returning symbol maps, dependents, and source bodies.

title: codegraph_search
text:
# codegraph_search

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_search` is the CodeGraph MCP search surface, including schema-advertised filters such as `kind`. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 `kind: "type"` filter bullet.

title: codegraph_trace
text:
# codegraph_trace

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph_trace` is the CodeGraph MCP trace surface for returning execution paths and inline flow dossiers. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#1 release 0.9.4 says `codegraph_trace` follows bridged flows, labels bridged hops, returns full bodies inline, and emits line-numbered source.

title: opencode AGENTS guidance
text:
# opencode AGENTS guidance

Lifecycle status: accepted

The opencode installer writes an `AGENTS.md` file with CodeGraph usage guidance so opencode chooses `codegraph_*` tools instead of native search. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.9 New Features says the installer now writes this guidance for opencode.

title: opencode XDG config path
text:
# opencode XDG config path

Lifecycle status: accepted

CodeGraph installs opencode's global MCP entry in the cross-platform opencode config location `~/.config/opencode/`, honoring `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, instead of the Windows `%APPDATA%\opencode\` path opencode does not read. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 opencode Windows bullet.

title: opencode stale APPDATA cleanup
text:
# opencode stale APPDATA cleanup

Lifecycle status: accepted

`codegraph install` and `codegraph uninstall` remove stale CodeGraph entries from the old `%APPDATA%\opencode\` location while leaving other servers and comments in that file untouched. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#5 opencode Windows bullet.

title: opencode surgical config edits
text:
# opencode surgical config edits

Lifecycle status: accepted

The installer edits `opencode.jsonc` surgically rather than rewriting the whole file, preserving user comments and formatting across install, reinstall, and uninstall. Evidence: CHANGELOG.md#0 release 0.7.9 New Features states this exact behavior.
